data.trial_title: A Study to Evaluate SHR-1210 in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic NSCLC
data.primary_endpoint: Objective response rate
data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Lung Neoplasms, Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung, Respiratory Tract Neoplasms Nec, Lung Disease, Respiratory Tract Disease, Neoplasm, Bronchial, Carcinoma, Bronchogenic
Lead sponsor: Jiangsu HengRui Medicine Co., Ltd.
Enrollment: 146
Design: allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=80 Years

Brief summary:
This is an open-label, single-arm, multi-center, phase 2 Study to evaluate SHR-1210(anti-PD-1 antibody) in in adult Chinese patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer who failed or progressed to prior first-line systemic treatment.

Enrolled subjects will be assigned to 4 cohorts on the basis of PD-L1 expression in tumor cells(\<1%, ≥1%-25%, ≥25%-50%, ≥50%) all will be treated with the standard SHR-1210 dose (200mg) , Q2W, until documented progressive disease (PD) occurs. Subjects will return to the clinic once every two weeks. Radiographic disease assessments will be performed every 6 weeks.

The primary study hypothesis is that treatment with SHR-1210 improves Objective Response Rate when compare with standard second-line therapy, no matter how much PD-L1 expression in tumor. In a preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation.

Detailed description:
In similar clinical trials, anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 antibodies produce durable responses in approximately 20% of unselected patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. Developing reliable, validated biomarkers that identify patients with an increased probability of response to these antibodies remains a challenge.

Because the PD-1 pathway may be a key mechanism of immune escape in a subgroup of patients with non-small-cell lung cancer, PD-L1 expression in tumor or inflammatory cells is a candidate biomarker. However, PD-L1 expression has not been formally validated as a biomarker in contemporaneously collected tumor tissue.

Additionally the purpose of the study is to assess the correlation between the expression of PD-L1 in the tumor and the response to treatment with SHR-1210 in non-small cell lung cancer.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 50%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥25-50%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 1-25%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor < 1%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] SHR-1210: SHR-1210 is a humanized anti-PD1 IgG4 monoclonal antibody

Primary outcomes:
  - Objective response rate [time frame: Determined using RECIST v1.1 criteria, up to approximately 1 year]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Duration of Response Rate [time frame: Determined using RECIST v1.1 criteria, up to approximately 1 year]
  - Overall Survival Rate at 12-month [time frame: up to approximately 1 year]
  - Progression-Free Survival [time frame: Determined using RECIST v1.1 criteria, up to approximately 1 year]
  - Number of participants with treatment-related adverse events (AEs) [time frame: up to approximately 1 year]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subjects with histologically- or cytologically- documented NSCLC who present with Stage IIIB-IV disease (according to version 7 of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology), or disease recurrence or progression following multi-modal therapy (radiation therapy, surgical resection or radical chemo-radiotherapy in locally advanced disease).
2. Fresh cutting specimens or hollow needle aspiration specimens must be provided. A formalin fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue block or unstained slides of tumor sample (must be recent) must be available for biomarker evaluation. In the case of unstained slides, a minimum of 8 slides are necessary to conduct the planned biomarker analyses. Specimens must be received by the central lab prior to randomization. Biopsy should be excisional, incisional or core needle.
3. Subjects must have experienced disease recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet chemotherapy regimen for advanced or metastatic disease:

   1. Subjects who received maintenance therapy (non-progressors with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy) and progressed are eligible.
   2. Subjects who received adjuvant or neoadjuvant platinum-doublet chemotherapy (after surgery and/or radiation therapy) and developed recurrent or metastatic disease within 6 months of completing therapy are eligible.
   3. Subjects with recurrent disease \> 6 months after adjuvant or neoadjuvant platinum based chemotherapy, who also subsequently progressed during or after a platinum-doublet regimen given to treat the recurrence, are eligible.
4. Subjects with sensitizing EGFR mutation positive or ALK rearrangement positive, must have experienced disease recurrence or progression during or after one prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor regimen, who also have PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 50%, are eligible.
5. Subjects must have measurable disease by CT or MRI per RECIST 1.1 criteria; Radiographic Tumor Assessment performed within 28 days of randomization.
6. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Arm (ECOG) performance status of ≤ 1.
7. All baseline laboratory requirements will be assessed and should be obtained within -14 days of randomization. Screening laboratory values must meet the following criteria.

   1. Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 1.5 × 109/L (1500/mm3)
   2. Platelets ≥ 80× 109/L (100,000/mm3)
   3. Hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL (90 g/L)
   4. Total bilirubin (TBIL) ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN)
   5. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤ 2.5 × upper limit of normal(ULN); for subjects with liver metastases, ALT and AST ≤ 5 × ULN
   6. Serum creatinine ≤1.5 × ULN or creatinine clearance \> 45 mL/minute (using Cockcroft/Gault formula)
8. Female participants of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within -7 days of randomization and must be willing to use very efficient barrier methods of contraception or a barrier method plus a hormonal method starting with the screening visit through 60 days (about 5 drug half-life + menstrual cycle) after the last dose of SHR-1210. Male participants with a female partner(s) of child-bearing potential must be willing to use very efficient barrier methods of contraception from screening through 120 days (about 5 drug half-life + sperm depletion cycle) after the last dose of SHR-1210.
9. Subjects must be willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory tests including completion of patient reported outcomes questionnaires and other requirements of the study. Subjects must have signed and dated an IRB/IEC approved written informed consent form in accordance with regulatory and institutional guidelines. This must be obtained before the performance of any protocol related procedures that are not part of normal subject care.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Target Disease Exceptions

   1. Subjects with active CNS metastases are excluded. Subjects are eligible if CNS metastases are adequately treated and subjects are neurologically returned to baseline (except for residual signs or symptoms related to the CNS treatment) for at least 2 weeks prior to enrollment. In addition, subjects must be either off corticosteroids, or on a stable or decreasing dose of ≤ 10 mg daily prednisone (or equivalent).
   2. Subjects with carcinomatous meningitis.
2. Medical History and Concurrent Diseases

   1. Subjects with active, known or suspected autoimmune disease. Subjects in conditions not expected to recur in the absence of an external trigger are permitted to enroll.
   2. Subjects with a condition requiring systemic treatment with either corticosteroids (\>10 mg daily prednisone equivalent) or other immunosuppressive medications within 14 days of first administration of study treatment. Inhaled or topical steroids, and adrenal replacement steroid doses \> 10 mg daily prednisone equivalent, are permitted in the absence of active autoimmune disease.
   3. Prior therapy with immunostimulatory medications or tumor vaccines within 6 months.
   4. Prior therapy with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, or anti-CTLA-4 antibody (including any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint pathways).
   5. Treatment with any investigational agent within 5 half-life of the agent, before the first administration of study treatment.
   6. Subjects with a history of interstitial lung disease.
   7. Subjects received lung radiation therapy within 6 months.
   8. Other active malignancy requiring concurrent intervention.
   9. Subjects with previous malignancies (except non-melanoma skin cancers, and the following in situ cancers: bladder, endometrial, cervical/dysplasia) are excluded unless a complete remission was achieved at least 5 years prior to study entry.
   10. Subjects have had prior chemotherapy within 3 weeks prior to study, or have had prior targeted small molecule therapy within 1 weeks prior to study, or have had prior radiation therapy or surgical operation within 4 weeks prior to study, or have had prior anti-tumor biotherapy within 3 weeks prior to study. All toxicities attributed to prior anti-cancer therapy other than alopecia and fatigue must have resolved to grade 1 (NCI CTCAE version 4) or baseline before administration of study drug.
   11. Subjects must have recovered from the effects of major surgery or significant traumatic injury at least 14 days before the first dose of study treatment
   12. Subjects with active pulmonary tuberculosis.
   13. Subjects with hemoptysis or hemorrhagic quantity per day is 2.5 ml or above within 4 weeks prior to study.
3. Physical and Laboratory Test Findings

   1. Known history of testing positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or known acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).
   2. Positive test for hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBV sAg) or hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid (HCV RNA) indicating acute or chronic infection. (HBV: HBsAg positive and HBV DNA ≥ 500 IU/mL ; HVC: HCV RNA positive and abnormal liver function).
4. Allergies and Adverse Drug Reaction

   1. History of severe hypersensitivity reactions to other monoclonal antibodies.
   2. History of severe hypersensitivity reaction to intravenous infusion.
5. Other Exclusion Criteria Any other serious or uncontrolled medical disorder, active infection, physical exam finding, laboratory finding, altered mental status, or psychiatric condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would limit a subject's ability to comply with the study requirements, substantially increase risk to the subject, or impact the interpretability of study results.

# Independent Knowledge About NCT03085069 and SHR-1210

## SHR-1210 (Camrelizumab)

**Mechanism of action:** SHR-1210 is a humanized anti-PD-1 IgG4 monoclonal antibody. It binds PD-1 on T cells, blocking interaction with PD-L1/PD-L2, thereby restoring T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. This is the same class as pembrolizumab and nivolumab. The IgG4 backbone is engineered to reduce Fc-mediated effector function. **This much is confirmed by the registered specification.**

**Drug identity:** SHR-1210 is now known internationally as **camrelizumab** (brand name AiRuiKa / 艾瑞卡). This is well-established public knowledge.

**Sponsor:** Jiangsu HengRui Medicine Co., Ltd. is a major Chinese pharmaceutical company (Hengrui Medicine, stock code 600276.SH). It is one of the largest oncology drug developers in China. Camrelizumab was approved by China's NMPA in 2019 for relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma — this was its first approval. It has since gained multiple approvals in China (hepatocellular carcinoma, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, etc.). The company has an extensive PD-1 development program.

- **Trial registration:** The NCT number suggests registration around early 2017. I believe the study start date was approximately **March 2017**. (I am not fully certain of the exact date — **unknown** for precision.)

However, I am aware that Hengrui conducted a phase 2 study of camrelizumab in Chinese NSCLC patients that was published (I believe in the *Journal of Thoracic Oncology* or similar, around 2019–2020). The reported ORR in that study was approximately **~20%** overall, with higher responses in PD-L1–high patients. I cannot confirm with certainty that the publication corresponds exactly to NCT03085069. **Treat these numbers as approximate and unverified.**

## Reactive Capillary Hemangioma / Vascular Toxicity

This is a notable safety signal for camrelizumab. A distinctive adverse event reported in Chinese trials of camrelizumab is **reactive capillary hemangioma** (also called "reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation" or RCCEP). This appears as multiple small red papules on the skin and was reported in a substantial proportion of patients (in some trials, ~60–80%). This is relatively unique to camrelizumab compared to other PD-1 inhibitors. The registered specification mentions ALT elevations in the safety run-in but does **not** mention RCCEP — this is independent knowledge.

## Prior/Related Studies

- A phase 1 study of SHR-1210 in advanced solid tumors was conducted in China (NCT02742935, approximately). It established the 200 mg Q2W dose. I am **unknown** on exact published ORR from that study.
- Camrelizumab has been studied extensively in NSCLC, including in combination with chemotherapy. The **CameL** and **CameL-sq** phase 3 trials evaluated camrelizumab + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone in non-squamous and squamous NSCLC, respectively, and met their primary endpoints. These are later-stage trials than NCT03085069.

# Key Risk Factors for NCT03085069

---

## RISK 1: Inadequate trial design to support the stated hypothesis (single-arm vs. comparative claim)

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registered design is single-arm / non-randomized with no control arm, yet the brief summary explicitly states the hypothesis is that SHR-1210 "improves Objective Response Rate when compared with standard second-line therapy." A single-arm trial cannot validly test superiority against an active comparator. Even if the ORR looks promising, regulators and reviewers may reject the evidence as insufficient to support the comparative claim. This is an internal inconsistency baked into the protocol itself.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

## RISK 2: Hepatotoxicity safety signal (ALT elevations)

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The specification explicitly reports that in the safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects (20%) showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation. This is a direct, drug-specific signal. If the rate of grade ≥3 hepatotoxicity is confirmed in the larger cohort, it could trigger dose modification, treatment discontinuation, enrollment holds, or a regulatory safety concern. Immune-related hepatitis is a known class effect of PD-1 inhibitors, but a 20% early signal is notably high and warrants close monitoring.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

## RISK 3: PD-L1 biomarker hypothesis fails (no correlation between PD-L1 expression and response)

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** A stated purpose of the trial is to assess correlation between tumor PD-L1 expression and response. At the time of this trial (circa 2017), PD-L1 had not been formally validated as a predictive biomarker in contemporaneously collected tissue for this drug. If the four PD-L1 cohorts (<1%, ≥1–25%, ≥25–50%, ≥50%) show no meaningful differential response — or if responses occur regardless of PD-L1 status — the biomarker stratification strategy collapses, undermining both the scientific rationale and any future enrichment strategy. This is a genuine scientific uncertainty, not a design flaw per se.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

## RISK 4: Low ORR / failure to exceed historical benchmark

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The primary endpoint is ORR, and success depends on exceeding some (undisclosed) historical threshold for second-line NSCLC. Historical second-line NSCLC ORRs for chemotherapy are modest (~10–15%), and even approved anti-PD-1 agents in unselected second-line NSCLC produced ORRs around 20%. If camrelizumab's true ORR in this population is at or below that range, the trial could be deemed a failure on its primary endpoint, particularly if the threshold was set optimistically. The 146-patient sample split across four biomarker cohorts further reduces per-cohort precision.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

## RISK 5: Competitive / regulatory landscape shift

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** By 2017, pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-010) and nivolumab (CheckMate 057) were already approved or under regulatory review for second-line NSCLC in major markets. If this trial was intended to support a Chinese regulatory filing, the bar for demonstrating clinical benefit may have risen as global standards evolved. Additionally, a single-arm Phase 2 with ORR as the endpoint may not have been sufficient for approval in second-line NSCLC once randomized Phase 3 data from competitors were available. The competitive environment could render even a positive ORR signal commercially or regulatorily insufficient.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

## RISK 6 (additional): Enrollment challenges across four biomarker cohorts

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** Stratifying 146 patients across four PD-L1 cohorts means each cohort averages ~36–37 patients, and the <1% and ≥50% extremes may be harder to fill depending on the underlying prevalence distribution. Slow accrual in any cohort could prolong the trial, introduce selection bias, or force protocol amendments. Age range is broad (18–80) and eligibility is reasonably permissive, which partially mitigates this.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** LOW–MEDIUM

---

Based on my knowledge, here is what I can tell you about this trial and drug, with uncertainty flagged where appropriate:

**NGM313 (also known as aldafermin / NGM282 is a different compound — careful not to confuse them)**

Actually, an important clarification: NGM313 is **not** aldafermin (NGM282). Let me be careful here.

- **NGM313** is an investigational **monoclonal antibody** that acts as a **β-Klotho–FGFR1c (fibroblast growth factor receptor 1c) agonist**. It mimics the metabolic actions of FGF21. Mechanism: it binds the FGFR1c/β-Klotho receptor complex, leading to improved insulin sensitivity, glucose uptake, and lipid metabolism — similar in concept to FGF21 analogs. **Note: I have moderate confidence on the FGFR1c/β-Klotho mechanism for NGM313 specifically; this is the mechanism NGM Biopharmaceuticals pursued for its FGF21-pathway assets, but I am not fully certain NGM313 is the antibody versus a different NGM molecule in that program.**

- The **ALT elevations >3× ULN** in the safety run-in (3 of first 15 subjects) is notable and was reported in the trial record itself. This is consistent with a hepatic signal that affected the program.

- **Sponsor track record**: NGM Biopharmaceuticals is a South San Francisco–based biotech (founded ~2008, IPO 2019). It has partnered with Merck on some programs and with others. Its notable clinical assets include NGM282/aldafermin (FGF19 analog, for NASH), NGM313, and NGM621 (anti-C3 for geographic atrophy). NGM had layoffs and pipeline reprioritizations around 2022–2023.

- **Results of earlier studies for NGM313**: I recall that NGM313 was studied in a Phase 1b in obese/insulin-resistant participants and showed improvements in insulin sensitivity and possibly weight, but the **ALT elevation signal** complicated development. **I am not certain of specific published efficacy numbers.** The ALT signal is the key reason this compound's development was likely deprioritized/discontinued.

- **Pioglitazone** as active comparator: a TZD, PPAR-γ agonist, insulin sensitizer — well established. Known for weight gain, fluid retention, and CHF risk (hence the CHF exclusion criterion in this trial).

**Key dates:**
- Trial registration (NCT03298464): approximately **2017** (the NCT number is consistent with a 2017 registration).
- **Unknown**: exact start date, completion date, whether results were ever posted to ClinicalTrials.gov or published.
- **Unknown**: current development status of NGM313.

**Things I am not confident about (flagging honestly):**
- Whether NGM313 is definitively the anti-FGFR1c/β-Klotho antibody vs. another modality — **unknown/uncertain**.
- Specific efficacy results from this trial — **unknown**.
- Whether the trial was terminated early due to the ALT signal — **plausible but unknown**.
- Exact publication history — **unknown**.

- **Unknown** — the registration does not state a significance level, power, or analysis model.

data.trial_title: Induction Chemotherapy Plus Chemoradiotherapy With or Without Aspirin in High Risk Rectal Cancer
data.primary_endpoint: Tumor downstaging after induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin
data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Rectal Cancer, Adenocarcinoma, Locally Advanced Malignant Neoplasm, Chemoradiation
Lead sponsor: Instituto Nacional de Cancer, Brazil
Enrollment: 25
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=QUADRUPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
The benefit of aspirin in cancer of the colon and rectum is already known. Recently, it was described its potential activity during chemoradiotherapy, with higher rate of tumor downstaging. Furthermore, induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiation represents an attractive approach, with more favorable compliance and toxicity profiles. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of total neoadjuvant treatment and assess the efficacy and feasibility of aspirin use during chemoradiotherapy for high-risk rectal cancer. In a preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation.

Detailed description:
Methods: This is a randomized trial to evaluate induction treatment with XELOX and Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin in a high-risk population selected by MRI. High-risk will be defined by presence of at least one of the following criteria on high-resolution thin-slice MRI (3 mm): tumors extending to within 1 mm of, or beyond the mesorectal fascia; tumor extending 5 mm or more into perirectal fat; resectable cT4 tumors; lower third; nodal involvement; extramural vascular invasion. Random assignment of treatment will be stratified by MRI tumour regression grade. All the patients enrolled in the study will receive XELOX every 21 days for four cycles, unless unacceptable toxicity or progression is detected. After this treatment, patients will be randomized to receive Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with aspirin or placebo (Capecitabine 850 mg/m² 5 days per week combined with radiotherapy with total dose of 50.4 Gy in 28 days). After 8-10 weeks, they will be evaluate by MRI. Patients with incomplete clinical response will be referred to immediate surgery and patients with complete clinical response will be managed with "watch and wait" approach. Patients with progression disease during the treatment phase will be withdrawn from the study and will receive their treatment according to the investigator's judgment.

The sample size was calculated according to Simon's optimal two-stage design. Accordingly, 11 patients must be included in each group during the first stage and 20 during the second stage. A treatment regimen will be considered effective if more than 18 patients of the total 31 show downstaging (final analysis), reaching 80% power with an alpha of 0.05 level of significance.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Aspirin: Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with aspirin Aspirin 100mg daily during the chemoradiotherapy
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo Oral Tablet: Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy without aspirin Placebo daily during the chemoradiotherapy

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Aspirin: chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine and aspirin Aspirin daily during chemoradiotherapy
  - [DRUG] Placebo Oral Tablet: chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine and placebo Placebo daily during chemoradiotherapy

Primary outcomes:
  - Tumor downstaging after induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin [time frame: 8-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Radiological Tumor response rate after induction chemotherapy [time frame: 3-4 weeks after last induction chemotherapy]
  - Pathological Tumor response rate [time frame: 10-12 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]
  - Pathologic complete response [time frame: 8-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]
  - Disease-free survival [time frame: 3 years]
  - Overall survival [time frame: 5 years]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of mid or low rectum
2. Locally advanced rectal cancer with one of the high-risk factors confirmed by high-resolution thin-slice Magnetic resonance image (3 mm)

   * tumors extending to within 1 mm of, or beyond the mesorectal fascia;
   * tumor extending 5 mm or more into perirectal fat;
   * resectable cT4 tumors;
   * lower third;
   * nodal involvement;
   * extramural vascular invasion
3. ECOG performance status of 0-2
4. An informed consent has been signed by the patient

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Upper rectal cancer
2. Metastatic disease
3. The patient received any previous therapy for colorectal cancer or another malignancy
4. Other malignant tumours within the last 5 years except cervical carcinoma in situ and basal cell carcinoma of the skin
5. Previous thromboembolic or haemorrhagic events within 6 months prior to registration
6. Patients with malabsorption syndrome or difficulties in swallowing
7. The patient has severe underlying diseases or poor condition to receive chemotherapy or radiotherapy
8. Pregnant of breastfeeding women
9. The patient who participate in another clinical trial, or receives any drug for the trial
10. Uncontrolled peripheral neuropathy (more than grade 2)
11. Active gastrointestinal bleeding

Based on my independent knowledge, here is what I can tell you about this trial, the drug, and related context. Where I am not confident or the information is not part of my knowledge, I say so explicitly.

## Aspirin (mechanism of action, relevant to this setting)

- **Classic mechanism:** Aspirin irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and COX-2, blocking prostaglandin and thromboxane synthesis. This underlies its antiplatelet and anti-inflammatory effects.
- **Anticancer hypotheses:** Several mechanisms have been proposed: COX-dependent effects (reduced PGE2, which can promote proliferation, angiogenesis, and immunosuppression), and COX-independent effects (inhibition of NF-κB, effects on Wnt/β-catenin signaling, modulation of apoptosis, and possibly effects on platelet-mediated tumor cell shielding). The relative contributions in rectal cancer are not fully established.
- **Radiosensitization hypothesis:** Aspirin has been studied as a potential radiosensitizer and as a modulator of the tumor microenvironment during chemoradiotherapy. The rationale cited in the protocol (higher downstaging rates) aligns with a small body of literature suggesting aspirin users may have better outcomes after chemoradiation for rectal cancer. This is hypothesis-generating rather than definitively proven.
- **Safety signal noted in the protocol:** The protocol itself mentions ALT elevations >3× ULN in 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects during a safety run-in. I do not have independent knowledge of additional hepatotoxicity details beyond what is stated.

## Earlier studies / evidence base

- **Aspirin in colorectal cancer generally:** There is substantial observational and randomized evidence (e.g., aspirin for secondary prevention in Lynch syndrome, and adjuvant aspirin studies such as the ASCOLT trial in colorectal cancer) suggesting possible benefit, but results have been mixed and not consistently positive.
- **Aspirin with chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer:** I am not aware of a large, definitive randomized trial that has established aspirin as standard in this setting. Smaller studies and retrospective analyses have suggested possible downstaging benefit, but I cannot cite specific named trials with confidence here — treat this as **unknown** for precise study names/results.
- **Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) in rectal cancer:** This is an established and increasingly used approach, supported by trials such as RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23, which showed improved outcomes with induction chemotherapy or total neoadjuvant treatment compared with standard chemoradiation followed by surgery. The NCT03170115 design is consistent with that era's TNT rationale.
- **Watch-and-wait:** The organ-preservation approach for complete clinical responders is supported by studies such as the International Watch & Wait Database and the OPRA trial. This is a recognized strategy, though patient selection and monitoring remain areas of active investigation.

- **Instituto Nacional de Cancer (INCA), Brazil:** This is a major Brazilian national cancer institute and teaching hospital. # What Would Constitute a Successful Outcome for NCT03170115

## 1. Primary endpoint and how it would be measured

**Primary endpoint:** Tumor downstaging after induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin, assessed at 8–10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy (per the registered protocol).

**How it would be measured:** Downstaging is typically defined as a reduction in pathologic T and/or N stage relative to baseline clinical stage, assessed on the surgical specimen (pathologic downstaging) or, for watch-and-wait patients, by clinical/radiological criteria. Given the protocol mentions MRI evaluation at 8–10 weeks and a watch-and-wait pathway for complete clinical responders, the endpoint likely blends:
- Pathologic T/N downstaging in patients who undergo surgery, and
- Clinical complete response (cCR) in patients managed non-operatively.

The precise operational definition (e.g., whether downstaging means any T reduction, or specifically to ypT0–1, or a composite including cCR) is **unknown** from what is registered.

Secondary endpoints include radiological response after induction, pathological response, pathologic complete response (pCR), disease-free survival (3 years), and overall survival (5 years).

## 2. Statistical threshold

From the registered description, the sample size was calculated using **Simon's optimal two-stage design**:
- Stage 1: 11 patients per group
- Stage 2: 20 patients total (cumulative across groups in the described design)
- The regimen is deemed effective "if more than 18 patients of the total 31 show downstaging," with 80% power and a one-sided alpha of 0.05.

Key caveats:
- The protocol text mixes per-group and total-patient framing (11 per group in stage 1, but "total 31" for the final analysis), which is internally ambiguous. The exact hypothesis structure (single-arm vs. comparative between aspirin and placebo arms) is therefore **unknown**.
- If the intent is a comparison between aspirin and placebo arms, the stated "more than 18 of 31" threshold resembles a single-proportion decision rule rather than a formal between-arm superiority test with a stated effect size or hazard ratio.
- A specific p-value threshold for the between-arm comparison, a hazard ratio target for DFS/OS, or a non-inferiority margin are **not specified** in what is registered — **unknown**.

## 3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence?

Based on the design (randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled, with aspirin hypothesized to improve downstaging), this is most consistent with a **superiority** trial: testing whether adding aspirin improves downstaging over placebo.

- A non-inferiority design would not fit the stated rationale (aspirin is hypothesized to add benefit, not to match an existing therapy).
- An equivalence design is not suggested by the framing.

However, because the statistical section is ambiguously worded, I cannot fully rule out that the primary analysis is a single-arm futility/efficacy screen rather than a formal between-arm superiority test — **unknown**.

## 4. Key design features

- **Allocation:** Randomized
- **Intervention model:** Parallel assignment
- **Masking:** Quadruple (participant, care provider, investigator, outcomes assessor) — this is a notably rigorous blinding level for a trial involving aspirin, and implies a matched placebo.
- **Arms:**
  - Experimental: induction chemotherapy (XELOX ×4) → capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (50.4 Gy/28 fractions) + aspirin 100 mg daily
  - Placebo comparator: identical backbone + placebo daily
- **Stratification:** By MRI tumor regression grade (per the detailed description)
- **Population:** High-risk locally advanced mid/low rectal adenocarcinoma, defined by MRI criteria (mesorectal fascia involvement, ≥5 mm perirectal fat extension, resectable cT4, lower third, nodal involvement, extramural vascular invasion); ECOG 0–2; age 18–75
- **Post-treatment pathway:** MRI at 8–10 weeks → surgery for incomplete clinical response, watch-and-wait for complete clinical response; progression during treatment → withdrawal and investigator-directed care
- **Enrollment:** 25 (registered), which is smaller than the 31 referenced in the statistical section — an internal inconsistency worth noting; the reason is **unknown**.

## Summary of what would constitute "success"

A successful outcome would most plausibly be:
- A sufficient number of patients (per the Simon two-stage rule, "more than 18 of 31" showing downstaging) achieving tumor downstaging in the aspirin-containing arm, and
- If analyzed comparatively, a statistically significant improvement over the placebo arm at the prespecified alpha (one-sided 0.05) with 80% power.

Because the registered statistical section is ambiguous about whether the primary comparison is within-arm (single-proportion) or between-arm, and does not state a hazard ratio, non-inferiority margin, or a clean p-value rule for the between-arm test, several key quantitative success criteria are **unknown**.

Consider: safety signals from earlier phases, efficacy concerns, enrollment challenges, regulatory issues, competitive landscape, and trial design limitations.

# Key Risks for NCT03170115, Ordered Most to Least Concerning

---

**RISK 1: Trial design is statistically underpowered and internally inconsistent, making a "success" hard to achieve or interpret**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registered statistics are contradictory: enrollment is listed as 25, but the power calculation references "31 total" and "more than 18 of 31" showing downstaging. The design also mixes per-group (11 per group in stage 1) and pooled (31 total) framing, leaving unclear whether the primary comparison is within-arm or between-arm. With such small numbers — especially only ~11–13 per arm if randomized — the trial has limited ability to detect a realistic effect of adding aspirin to an already-effective TNT backbone. Any true benefit of aspirin on downstaging is likely to be modest, and a small trial will often fail to detect it (type II error) or produce an unstable estimate (wide confidence interval). This is arguably the single biggest structural threat.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

**RISK 2: Safety signal — hepatotoxicity (ALT elevations >3× ULN)**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The protocol itself reports that in the preceding safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects developed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation. This is a direct, protocol-documented signal in the exact regimen being tested. Aspirin plus capecitabine plus radiotherapy creates multiple potential hepatotoxic contributors (capecitabine is known to cause hyperbilirubinemia and transaminase elevations; aspirin adds bleeding and GI/hepatic risk). If these elevations recur, cause treatment interruptions, or are attributed to aspirin, the trial could be halted, the aspirin dose modified (altering the tested intervention), or the safety profile could undermine any efficacy signal. In a 25-patient trial, even a few serious hepatic events are proportionally large.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

**RISK 3: Weak or null efficacy of aspirin as a radiosensitizer/antineoplastic adjunct in rectal cancer**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The efficacy hypothesis rests on observational and hypothesis-generating evidence that aspirin improves downstaging during chemoradiotherapy. Randomized evidence for aspirin in colorectal cancer has been mixed, and to my recollection the adjuvant ASCOLT trial did not meet its primary endpoint. Aspirin is a repurposed, low-cost, pleiotropic agent rather than a mechanistically targeted therapy, so any incremental effect on top of an already-intensive TNT backbone is likely to be small. Because the backbone (induction XELOX + capecitabine chemoradiation) is itself active, ceiling effects could mask a modest aspirin benefit, and the trial may fail to separate arms even if aspirin has some real biological activity.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM–HIGH

---

**RISK 4: Enrollment and feasibility challenges in a narrow, MRI-defined high-risk population**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The trial enrolls a highly selected population: histologically confirmed mid/low rectal adenocarcinoma, locally advanced, meeting at least one of several stringent high-resolution MRI criteria, ECOG 0–2, age 18–75, with numerous exclusions (prior malignancy, thromboembolic/haemorrhagic events within 6 months, active GI bleeding, uncontrolled neuropathy, malabsorption, etc.). Requiring quadruple masking, stratification by MRI regression grade, and a watch-and-wait pathway adds operational complexity. The target is only 25 patients, but recruitment into such a narrow window at a single national cancer institute can still be slow and prone to screen failures, risking incomplete accrual, prolonged timelines, and a sample that is not representative. Note that aspirin's own exclusion profile (bleeding/thromboembolic history) removes a meaningful fraction of otherwise eligible rectal cancer patients.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

**RISK 5: Endpoint and analysis ambiguity, plus confounding by the watch-and-wait pathway**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** "Tumor downstaging" is assessed differently depending on whether a patient goes to surgery (pathologic downstaging) or to watch-and-wait (clinical complete response). Because treatment assignment is randomized but the post-treatment pathway is response-dependent, the composition of patients contributing to the primary endpoint can differ between arms in ways not fully controlled by randomization. This introduces measurement heterogeneity and potential bias. The protocol's statistical section does not clearly state a hazard ratio, non-inferiority margin, or clean between-arm p-value rule, so even a numerically favorable result may be difficult to interpret or defend. Any ambiguity here increases the chance that regulators, reviewers, or a subsequent trial sponsor judge the result inconclusive rather than positive.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

## Summary ordering rationale

The ranking prioritizes threats that are (a) already documented in the protocol (statistical inconsistency, hepatotoxicity signal) over (b) biological/clinical uncertainty (efficacy of aspirin) over (c) operational and interpretive risks (enrollment, endpoint ambiguity). Risks 1 and 2 are the most concerning because they are concrete, protocol-evidenced, and capable of causing failure or uninterpretability independently of whether aspirin actually works.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE3
Conditions: Constipation Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Lead sponsor: Ardelyx
Enrollment: 606
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=QUADRUPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
This phase 3, 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of tenapanor in subjects with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) as defined by the ROME III criteria and who have active disease as determined after a two-week screening period. Subjects who qualify and are randomized into the study will either receive 50mg BID of tenapanor or placebo BID for 12 week treatment period and then undergo a 4 week placebo controlled randomized withdrawal. In a preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation.

Detailed description:
During the 12-week treatment period, subjects will record daily assessments including: frequency and timing of bowel movements; sensation and complete bowel emptying; consistency of bowel movements; degree of straining, worst abdominal pain, abdominal discomfort, abdominal bloating, abdominal fullness and abdominal cramping. Subjects will also record weekly assessments including: adequate relief of IBS severity, and constipation severity.

At the end of the 12-week treatment period, there will be a 4-week randomized withdrawal period in which subjects who complete the study in Tenapanor group will be randomized to either Tenapanor 50mg BID or placebo BID (1:1) and subjects who complete the study in the placebo group will be assigned to receive Tenapanor 50mg BID.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] 50mg BID: Tenapanor
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: Placebo

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Tenapanor: 
  - [DRUG] Placebo: 

Primary outcomes:
  - 6 of 12 Week Overall Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]

Secondary outcomes:
  - 6 of 12 Week Overall Complete Spontaneous Bowel Movement (CSBM)Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 6 of 12 Week Overall Abdominal Pain Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 9 of 12 Week Overall Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 9 of 12 Week Overall CSBM Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 9 of 12 Week Overall Abdominal Pain Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 to 75 years old
* Females must be of non-childbearing potential; If of child-bearing potential, must have negative pregnancy test and confirm the use of one of the appropriate means of contraception.
* Males must agree to use an appropriate method of barrier contraception or have documented surgical sterilization
* Subject meets definition of IBS-C using Rome III Criteria for the Diagnosis of IBS
* A colonoscopy based on AGA guidelines; every 10 years at ≥ 50 years old, or the occurrence of any warning signs

Exclusion Criteria:

* Functional diarrhea as defined by Rome III criteria
* IBS with diarrhea (IBS-D), mixed IBS (IBS-M), or unsubtyped IBS as defined by Rome III criteria
* Diagnosis or treatment of any clinically symptomatic biochemical or structural abnormality of the GI tract within 6 months prior to screening, or active disease within 6 months prior to screening; including but not limited to cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, diverticulitis, duodenal ulcer, erosive esophagitis, gastric ulcer, pancreatitis (within 12 months of screening), cholelithiasis, amyloidosis, ileus, non-controlled GERD, gastrointestinal obstruction, ischemic colitis or carcinoid syndrome.
* Subject has a history or current evidence of laxative abuse (in the clinical judgment of the physician)
* Hepatic dysfunction (ALT \[SGPT\] or AST \[SGOT\] \>2.5 times the upper limit of normal) or renal impairment (serum creatinine \> 2mg/dL)
* Any evidence of or treatment of malignancy (other than localized basal cell, squamous cell skin cancer or cancer in situ that has been resected) within the previous year
* Any surgery on the stomach, small intestine or colon, excluding appendectomy or cholecystectomy (unless within 60 days of screening visit)

Here is what I independently know, with uncertainty flagged where it exists.

**Drug: Tenapanor**

- **Mechanism of action:** Tenapanor is an orally administered, minimally absorbed small-molecule inhibitor of the sodium–hydrogen exchanger NHE3 (SLC9A3), which is expressed on the apical surface of the intestinal epithelium. By inhibiting NHE3, it reduces sodium absorption and, indirectly, phosphate absorption in the gut; the resulting osmotic retention of water in the intestinal lumen accelerates transit and softens stool. The same mechanism underlies its phosphate-lowering effect. This is well established.
- **Approved indications:** In the U.S., tenapanor is marketed as **IBSRELA** for IBS-C in adults (approved September 2019) and as **XPHOZAH** for hyperphosphatemia in adults with chronic kidney disease on dialysis (approved October 2023). I'm confident about these.
- **Dosing in IBS-C:** 50 mg twice daily, matching this trial's regimen. Confident.

**This specific trial (NCT02621892)**

Here is my read of what a successful outcome would require for NCT02621892, based strictly on the registered design and standard practice for IBS-C Phase 3 trials. Where the registry does not specify a detail, I flag it.

**1. Likely primary endpoint(s) and how measured**

- **Primary endpoint (from the registry):** "6 of 12 Week Overall Responder Rate," measured over the 12-week treatment period.
- **Standard FDA-aligned definition (not spelled out in the registry, but this is the established composite endpoint for IBS-C):** A subject is a weekly "overall responder" for a given week if they meet **both** of the following in that same week:
  - **Abdominal pain:** a ≥30% reduction from baseline in the weekly average of worst daily abdominal pain score (0–10 scale), and
  - **CSBM:** an increase of ≥1 complete spontaneous bowel movement per week from baseline.
- The "6 of 12" responder requires the subject to be a weekly overall responder in **at least 6 of the 12 treatment weeks**. The registry also lists a "9 of 12" version as a secondary outcome, which is the same construct with a stricter threshold.
- **How measured:** Daily electronic diary entries, as described in the detailed description (frequency/timing of BMs, CSBM, stool consistency via Bristol scale, straining, worst abdominal pain, bloating, discomfort). Weekly averages are computed from those daily entries.
- **Caveat:** The exact pain threshold, CSBM definition, and the precise composition rule are **not fully specified in the registry text**; I am applying the standard IBS-C composite definition used in this era. Exact wording is **unknown** from the registry alone.

**2. Statistical threshold**

- **Standard for this design:** The primary analysis would almost certainly be a **two-sided superiority test at α = 0.05** (or a one-sided 0.025 if framed one-sidedly), comparing the proportion of 6-of-12 overall responders in tenapanor vs placebo.
- **Test statistic:** Likely a Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test or a logistic regression / stratified analysis, with a treatment difference in responder rates and a corresponding p-value, often with a 95% confidence interval.
- **Statistical power:** Typically ~90% power to detect a pre-specified absolute difference in responder rates (commonly ~10–12 percentage points in IBS-C trials). The exact assumed effect size and power are **unknown** from the registry.
- **Multiplicity:** With a single primary endpoint and multiple secondaries, a **hierarchical/gatekeeping testing procedure** is typical, but the registry does not state it. **Unknown.**

**3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence**

- Clearly a **SUPERIORITY** trial. The design is placebo-controlled with a novel investigational agent; there is no active comparator against which non-inferiority could be tested, and the endpoint is an efficacy responder rate versus placebo. So the question is whether tenapanor beats placebo, not whether it matches something.

**4. Key design features**

- **Allocation:** RANDOMIZED. Confirmed in the registry.
- **Intervention model:** PARALLEL. Confirmed.
- **Masking:** QUADRUPLE (typically participant, care provider, investigator, and outcomes assessor). Confirmed in the registry.
- **Arms:** Tenapanor 50 mg BID vs matching placebo BID, for a 12-week double-blind treatment period.
- **Randomized withdrawal phase:** After the 12 weeks, a **4-week randomized withdrawal**: tenapanor completers are re-randomized 1:1 to continue tenapanor or switch to placebo; placebo completers all receive tenapanor. This phase is **placebo-controlled** and randomized for the tenapanor-origin subjects. It supports durability/maintenance assessment, though the registry lists it as part of the design rather than as a primary endpoint.
- **Run-in:** A two-week screening period to confirm active disease and eligibility, plus a preceding **open-label safety run-in** (noted in the summary; 3 of first 15 subjects had ALT >3× ULN).
- **Sample size:** 606 enrolled (per registry).
- **Population:** Adults 18–75 with IBS-C by Rome III criteria; broad inclusion with exclusions for other IBS subtypes, GI structural disease, laxative abuse, hepatic/renal impairment, and recent malignancy/surgery.

**Summary of what "success" looks like**

Success would require the tenapanor group to show a **statistically significantly higher 6-of-12 overall responder rate than placebo at the pre-specified α level (likely p<0.05), in the ITT population**, with the effect driven appropriately by both the abdominal pain and CSBM components, and with acceptable safety (particularly hepatic and diarrhea tolerability) given the ALT signal. Supportive success would be concordant results on the 9-of-12 and component secondary endpoints in the pre-specified testing hierarchy.

**Uncertainties:** Exact alpha, power assumptions, multiplicity procedure, precise composite definitions, and the primary analysis population are **unknown** from the registry text provided.

RISK: Hepatotoxicity / hepatic enzyme elevation signal
APPLIES_BECAUSE: The registry summary explicitly states that in the preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation. That is a striking early signal (20% of the first cohort) in a drug intended for a non-life-threatening, chronic, symptomatic condition (IBS-C), where the FDA's benefit-risk bar is high. This could trigger DSMB pauses, protocol amendments, added monitoring burden, a boxed warning or restricted labeling if the trial still succeeds, or outright clinical holds. It also creates a risk that the trial meets efficacy but fails on safety/tolerability grounds.
LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

RISK: High placebo response rate masking a real treatment effect
APPLIES_BECAUSE: IBS-C is a subjective, symptom-driven indication with historically large placebo responses (often 30–40% on composite responder endpoints). The trial uses a composite responder primary endpoint (abdominal pain + CSBM, 6 of 12 weeks) that requires both components to move together — a high bar. Tenapanor's mechanism (osmotic/secretory, NHE3 inhibition) drives stool frequency and consistency well, but its effect on abdominal pain is mechanistically less direct, so the pain component is the fragile half of the composite. A strong placebo arm could shrink the between-group difference below statistical significance even if the drug works.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

RISK: Diarrhea-driven tolerability and discontinuation imbalance
APPLIES_BECAUSE: Tenapanor's mechanism increases intestinal water secretion, so diarrhea is the expected dose-limiting adverse effect (consistent with the class). At 50 mg BID, excessive diarrhea could cause differential dropout in the tenapanor arm, which both worsens tolerability and can bias the ITT responder analysis (dropouts counted as non-responders). This is a mechanism-specific risk that applies directly here, and it interacts with the safety signal above.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

RISK: Competitive and regulatory landscape reducing approvability despite efficacy
APPLIES_BECAUSE: By the time this trial read out, IBS-C already had approved, well-established, better-tolerated entrants (linaclotide, lubiprostone, and later plecanatide). Even a statistically successful trial faces a crowded market and a regulator weighing the ALT signal against existing options. This is more an approvability/commercial risk than a pure trial-failure risk, but it can convert a "successful" trial into a non-viable asset and can shape how strictly the FDA reads the efficacy data.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

RISK: Enrollment and generalizability challenges
APPLIES_BECAUSE: The trial needs 606 subjects meeting strict Rome III IBS-C criteria, excluding IBS-D/IBS-M, with a colonoscopy requirement and a two-week screening plus open-label run-in. The open-label run-in with an emerging hepatic signal could slow recruitment or cause screen/run-in failures and site hesitancy, potentially affecting timeline and the randomized sample composition. This is generally a manageable operational risk in a large multi-center Phase 3, so it ranks lowest.
LIKELIHOOD: LOW

Brief summary:
This phase I trial studies talimogene laherparepvec given together with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery in patients with triple-negative or estrogen receptor positive, HER2 negative localized breast cancer. Ipilimumab and Nivolumab are immune checkpoint inhibitors that enhance immune response towards cancer cells. Talimogene laherparepvec is a modifies human herpes virus 1 that is an oncolytic virus targeting cancer cells and makes tumor microenvironment more immunogenic to promote immune response against cancer. This study will assess the safety and efficacy of talimogene laherparepvec, ipilimumab, and nivolumab, and provide an insight for further improvement of immunotherapy in breast cancer. In a preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation.

Detailed description:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVES:

I. To explore the safety of talimogene laherparepvec in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab in this population assessed by the frequency and severity of adverse events (AEs) using Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version (v)4.0 toxicity criteria.

SECONDARY OBJECTIVES:

I. Assess tumor response of talimogene laherparepvec in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab comparing to no treatment, in subjects with localized estrogen receptor (ER) positive and triple negative infiltrating ductal breast cancer.

II. Descriptively analyze the evidence of tumor necrosis and inflammatory infiltration on histopathological examination and immuno-oncological findings in tumor and peripheral blood of patients treated with talimogene laherparepvec in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab.

EXPLORATORY OBJECTIVES:

I. Descriptively compare tumor response in patients whose tumors are PD-L1 positive (+) and PD-L1 negative (-) at baseline.

II. Determine the baseline mutational load of patients at the start of treatment and relate it to the response to treatment.

III. Determine if hormone receptor status correlates with tumor responses. IV. Determine the number of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes in patient samples at the start and at the end of treatment and relate them to tumor response.

V. Analyze T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire in tumor infiltrating lymphocytes and peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

OUTLINE:

Participants receive talimogene laherparepvec intratumorally on days 1, 22, and 36, nivolumab intravenously (IV) over 60 minutes on days 1, 15, 29, and 43, and ipilimumab IV over 90 minutes on days 1 and 43 in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

After completion of study treatment, participants are followed up for 30 days.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Treatment (talimogene laherparepvec, nivolumab, ipilimumab): Participants receive talimogene laherparepvec intratumorally on days 1, 22, and 36, nivolumab IV over 60 minutes on days 1, 15, 29, and 43, and ipilimumab IV over 90 minutes on days 1 and 43 in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] Ipilimumab: Given IV
  - [BIOLOGICAL] Nivolumab: Given IV
  - [BIOLOGICAL] Talimogene Laherparepvec: Given intratumorally

Primary outcomes:
  - Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs) [time frame: Up to 100 days after last study drug]

Secondary outcomes:
  - histopathological evaluation of changes of tumor for inflammatory infiltration and tumor necrosis [time frame: Up to 2 years]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent must be obtained from the subject/legal representative prior to performing any protocol-related procedures, including screening evaluations
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) 0-1
* Localized, palpable, biopsy proven triple negative or ER positive HER2 negative infiltrating ductal breast cancer with size \> 1.5 cm by palpation, excluding breast cancer where neoadjuvant chemotherapy is indicated by current guidelines (i.e. inflammatory subtype, etc.)
* Tumor that is palpable and injectable
* Hemoglobin \>= 9 g/dL
* Absolute neutrophil count \>= 1,500/mm\^3
* Platelet count \>= 100,000/mm\^3
* Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =\< 2.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN)
* Bilirubin =\< 1.5 x ULN; for subjects with documented/suspected Gilbert?s disease, bilirubin =\< 3 x ULN
* Albumin \>= 2.5 g/dl
* Prothrombin time (PT) / International normalized ratio (INR) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) =\< 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal unless the patient is on anticoagulant therapy within 28 days prior to enrollment (if the patient is receiving anticoagulant therapy, PT, and a PTT must be within therapeutic range of intended use of anticoagulants)

* Patients must be offered the opportunity to participate in specimen banking for future research
* Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test (minimum sensitivity 25 IU/L or equivalent units of human chorionic gonadotropin \[HCG\]) within 24 hours prior to the start of study drug
* Women must not be breastfeeding

Approved contraceptive methods include, for example, intrauterine device, diaphragm with spermicide, cervical cap with spermicide, male condoms, female condoms with spermicide, or oral contraceptives. Spermicides alone are not an acceptable method of contraception. Should a woman become pregnant or suspect she is pregnant while she or her partner is participating in this study, she should inform her treating physician immediately

Exclusion Criteria:

* Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding
* Sexually active subjects and their partners unwilling to use male or female latex condom to avoid potential viral transmission during sexual contact while on treatment and within 30 days after treatment with talimogene laherparepvec
* Inability to give informed consent
* History of malignancies except cured basal cell carcinoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma in situ, superficial bladder cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix; for other malignancies, must be documented to be free of cancer for \>= 2 years. All other cases can be considered on a case by case basis at the discretion of the principal investigator
* Any condition that might interfere with the subject?s participation in the study, safety, or in the evaluation of the study results
* Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (non-interventional) clinical study or the follow-up period of an interventional study
* Prior exposure to any anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody, or any anti-CTLA 4 antibodies
* Patients must not have received prior treatment with talimogene laherparepvec or other oncolytic virus agents
* Patients must not have received any live vaccine within 30 days prior to registration. Seasonal flu vaccines that do not contain live virus are permitted
* Patients must not have an active infection requiring systemic therapy nor a viral infection requiring intermittent treatment with an antiherpetic drug, other than intermittent topical use
* Patients must not have active herpetic skin lesions or prior complications of herpetic infection (e.g., herpetic keratitis or encephalitis) which requires intermittent or chronic treatment with an anti-herpetic drug other than intermittent topical use
* Any concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment. Concurrent use of hormones for non-cancer-related conditions (e.g., insulin for diabetes and hormone replacement therapy) is acceptable
* Patient must not have evidence of any clinically significant immunosuppression such as the following: primary immunodeficiency state such as severe combined immunodeficiency disease; concurrent opportunistic infection; receiving systemic immunosuppressive therapy within 28 days before enrollment with the exceptions of intranasal, topical, and inhaled corticosteroids or oral corticosteroids at physiologic doses not to exceed 10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent
* Patients must not have known history human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)
* Clinical or laboratory evidence of an active herpetic infection and in patients who require daily antiviral therapy such as acyclovir
* Active or prior documented autoimmune disease within the past 3 years

  * NOTE: Subjects with active, known or suspected autoimmune disease such as vitiligo, type I diabetes mellitus, residual hypothyroidism due to autoimmune condition only requiring hormone replacement, psoriasis not requiring systemic treatment, or conditions not expected to recur in the absence of an external trigger are permitted to enroll
* Active or prior documented inflammatory bowel disease
* History of (non-infectious) interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis that required steroids or has current ILD/pneumonitis or where suspected ILD/pneumonitis cannot be ruled out by imaging at screening
* Exposure to any investigational drug within 7 days prior to screening visit or for which 5 half-lives have not elapsed
* Prisoners or subjects who are involuntarily incarcerated

Brief summary:
This phase I trial studies talimogene laherparepvec given together with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery in patients with triple-negative or estrogen receptor positive, HER2 negative localized breast cancer. Ipilimumab and Nivolumab are immune checkpoint inhibitors that enhance immune response towards cancer cells. Talimogene laherparepvec is a modifies human herpes virus 1 that is an oncolytic virus targeting cancer cells and makes tumor microenvironment more immunogenic to promote immune response against cancer. This study will assess the safety and efficacy of talimogene laherparepvec, ipilimumab, and nivolumab, and provide an insight for further improvement of immunotherapy in breast cancer. In a preceding open-label safety run-in, 3 of the first 15 dosed subjects showed ALT elevations >3× ULN within 4 weeks of treatment initiation.

Detailed description:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVES:

I. To explore the safety of talimogene laherparepvec in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab in this population assessed by the frequency and severity of adverse events (AEs) using Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version (v)4.0 toxicity criteria.

SECONDARY OBJECTIVES:

I. Assess tumor response of talimogene laherparepvec in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab comparing to no treatment, in subjects with localized estrogen receptor (ER) positive and triple negative infiltrating ductal breast cancer.

II. Descriptively analyze the evidence of tumor necrosis and inflammatory infiltration on histopathological examination and immuno-oncological findings in tumor and peripheral blood of patients treated with talimogene laherparepvec in combination with nivolumab and ipilimumab.

EXPLORATORY OBJECTIVES:

I. Descriptively compare tumor response in patients whose tumors are PD-L1 positive (+) and PD-L1 negative (-) at baseline.

II. Determine the baseline mutational load of patients at the start of treatment and relate it to the response to treatment.

III. Determine if hormone receptor status correlates with tumor responses. IV. Determine the number of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes in patient samples at the start and at the end of treatment and relate them to tumor response.

V. Analyze T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire in tumor infiltrating lymphocytes and peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

OUTLINE:

Participants receive talimogene laherparepvec intratumorally on days 1, 22, and 36, nivolumab intravenously (IV) over 60 minutes on days 1, 15, 29, and 43, and ipilimumab IV over 90 minutes on days 1 and 43 in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

After completion of study treatment, participants are followed up for 30 days.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Treatment (talimogene laherparepvec, nivolumab, ipilimumab): Participants receive talimogene laherparepvec intratumorally on days 1, 22, and 36, nivolumab IV over 60 minutes on days 1, 15, 29, and 43, and ipilimumab IV over 90 minutes on days 1 and 43 in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] Ipilimumab: Given IV
  - [BIOLOGICAL] Nivolumab: Given IV
  - [BIOLOGICAL] Talimogene Laherparepvec: Given intratumorally

Primary outcomes:
  - Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs) [time frame: Up to 100 days after last study drug]

Secondary outcomes:
  - histopathological evaluation of changes of tumor for inflammatory infiltration and tumor necrosis [time frame: Up to 2 years]

Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent must be obtained from the subject/legal representative prior to performing any protocol-related procedures, including screening evaluations
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) 0-1
* Localized, palpable, biopsy proven triple negative or ER positive HER2 negative infiltrating ductal breast cancer with size \> 1.5 cm by palpation, excluding breast cancer where neoadjuvant chemotherapy is indicated by current guidelines (i.e. inflammatory subtype, etc.)
* Tumor that is palpable and injectable
* Hemoglobin \>= 9 g/dL
* Absolute neutrophil count \>= 1,500/mm\^3
* Platelet count \>= 100,000/mm\^3
* Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =\< 2.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN)
* Bilirubin =\< 1.5 x ULN; for subjects with documented/suspected Gilbert?s disease, bilirubin =\< 3 x ULN
* Albumin \>= 2.5 g/dl
* Prothrombin time (PT) / International normalized ratio (INR) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) =\< 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal unless the patient is on anticoagulant therapy within 28 days prior to enrollment (if the patient is receiving anticoagulant therapy, PT, and a PTT must be within therapeutic range of intended use of anticoagulants)
* Patients must be willing to submit blood and tissue specimens for translational medicine studies
* Patients must be offered the opportunity to participate in specimen banking for future research
* Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test (minimum sensitivity 25 IU/L or equivalent units of human chorionic gonadotropin \[HCG\]) within 24 hours prior to the start of study drug
* Women must not be breastfeeding
* Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must be willing to use either two adequate barrier methods or a barrier method plus a hormonal method of contraception to prevent pregnancy, or to abstain from heterosexual activity (complete abstinence) throughout the study, starting with visit 1 through 5 months after the last dose of study therapy. Approved contraceptive methods include, for example, intrauterine device, diaphragm with spermicide, cervical cap with spermicide, male condoms, female condoms with spermicide, or oral contraceptives. Spermicides alone are not an acceptable method of contraception. Should a woman become pregnant or suspect she is pregnant while she or her partner is participating in this study, she should inform her treating physician immediately
* Male patients must agree to use an adequate method of contraception, or to abstain from heterosexual activity (complete abstinence) starting with the first dose of study drug through 7 months after the last dose of study therapy

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindications to tumor biopsy and injections (coagulopathy, known history of keloid formation, etc.)

* Sexually active subjects and their partners unwilling to use male or female latex condom to avoid potential viral transmission during sexual contact while on treatment and within 30 days after treatment with talimogene laherparepvec
* Inability to give informed consent
* History of malignancies except cured basal cell carcinoma, cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma in situ, superficial bladder cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix; for other malignancies, must be documented to be free of cancer for \>= 2 years. All other cases can be considered on a case by case basis at the discretion of the principal investigator
* Any condition that might interfere with the subject?s participation in the study, safety, or in the evaluation of the study results
* Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (non-interventional) clinical study or the follow-up period of an interventional study
* Prior exposure to any anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody, or any anti-CTLA 4 antibodies
* Patients must not have received prior treatment with talimogene laherparepvec or other oncolytic virus agents
* Patients must not have received any live vaccine within 30 days prior to registration. Seasonal flu vaccines that do not contain live virus are permitted

* Patients must not have active herpetic skin lesions or prior complications of herpetic infection (e.g., herpetic keratitis or encephalitis) which requires intermittent or chronic treatment with an anti-herpetic drug other than intermittent topical use
* Any concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment. Concurrent use of hormones for non-cancer-related conditions (e.g., insulin for diabetes and hormone replacement therapy) is acceptable
* Patient must not have evidence of any clinically significant immunosuppression such as the following: primary immunodeficiency state such as severe combined immunodeficiency disease; concurrent opportunistic infection; receiving systemic immunosuppressive therapy within 28 days before enrollment with the exceptions of intranasal, topical, and inhaled corticosteroids or oral corticosteroids at physiologic doses not to exceed 10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent
* Patients must not have known history human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)
* Clinical or laboratory evidence of an active herpetic infection and in patients who require daily antiviral therapy such as acyclovir
* Active or prior documented autoimmune disease within the past 3 years

  * NOTE: Subjects with active, known or suspected autoimmune disease such as vitiligo, type I diabetes mellitus, residual hypothyroidism due to autoimmune condition only requiring hormone replacement, psoriasis not requiring systemic treatment, or conditions not expected to recur in the absence of an external trigger are permitted to enroll
* Active or prior documented inflammatory bowel disease
* History of (non-infectious) interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis that required steroids or has current ILD/pneumonitis or where suspected ILD/pneumonitis cannot be ruled out by imaging at screening
* Exposure to any investigational drug within 7 days prior to screening visit or for which 5 half-lives have not elapsed
* Prisoners or subjects who are involuntarily incarcerated

  * Note: under certain specific circumstances a person who has been imprisoned may be included or permitted to continue as a subject
* Subjects who are compulsorily detained for treatment of either a psychiatric or physical (e.g., infectious disease) illness

# Independent Knowledge About This Trial and Its Components

## Talimogene Laherparepvec (T-VEC, Imlygic)

**Mechanism of action:** T-VEC is an oncolytic immunotherapy derived from a modified herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). It is attenuated by deletion of the ICP34.5 gene (which normally counteracts host antiviral responses and is associated with neurovirulence) and the ICP47 gene (which normally blocks antigen presentation). It also has the human GM-CSF gene inserted. After intratumoral injection, it preferentially replicates in tumor cells, causing lysis and release of tumor antigens, while GM-CSF recruits dendritic cells and enhances systemic antitumor immunity. It was the first oncolytic virus approved by the FDA (October 2015) for unresectable melanoma.

**Prior studies:** The pivotal Phase III study in melanoma was the OPTiM trial (Andtbacka et al., J Clin Oncol 2015), which showed a durable response rate of 16.3% vs 2.1% for GM-CSF alone. T-VEC has been studied in combination with ipilimumab in melanoma (Chesney et al., J Clin Oncol 2018) and with pembrolizumab in melanoma (Ribas et al., Cell 2017). I am not aware of prior published results of T-VEC specifically in breast cancer, though I believe Phase I studies in breast cancer have been conducted or are ongoing.

**Safety signal:** The ALT elevation noted in the safety run-in (3 of first 15 subjects with ALT >3× ULN) is notable and relevant, as hepatotoxicity is not a classic hallmark of T-VEC monotherapy but is a known risk with ipilimumab/nivolumab combination immune checkpoint blockade. This likely represents immune-related hepatitis from the checkpoint inhibitor combination, possibly potentiated by the oncolytic virus.

## Ipilimumab

**Mechanism:** Anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody. CTLA-4 is a negative regulator of T-cell activation; blocking it enhances T-cell priming and proliferation. Approved for melanoma (2011) and in combination with nivolumab for several cancers.

**Relevant track record:** In breast cancer, ipilimumab has been studied in combination with nivolumab in a Phase I trial (Adams et al., Cancer Immunol Res 2019) showing modest activity in metastatic disease. The combination has known toxicity concerns, particularly immune-related adverse events including hepatitis, colitis, and hypophysitis.

## Nivolumab

**Mechanism:** Anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. PD-1 is an inhibitory receptor on T cells; blocking it restores antitumor T-cell function. Approved for numerous indications including melanoma, NSCLC, renal cell carcinoma, and others.

**In breast cancer:** Nivolumab has been studied in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), including the KEYNOTE-119 trial (pembrolizumab, not nivolumab) and several nivolumab trials in metastatic TNBC with modest single-agent activity. Combination with ipilimumab has shown some activity in TNBC.

## Sponsor: Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center (UCLA)

This is a major academic cancer center at the University of California, Los Angeles. It is an NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center. I do not have specific information about this trial's operational history or completion status beyond what is registered. **Unknown** regarding whether this trial was completed, terminated, or if results were published.

## Key Dates and Current Status

- **NCT04185311 registration:** The NCT number suggests registration around late 2019/early 2020.
- **Enrollment target:** 6 participants (very small, typical of a safety run-in or pilot Phase I).
- **Current status:** **Unknown.** I cannot confirm whether this trial has been completed, is ongoing, or was terminated. The small enrollment and Phase I designation suggest it is a feasibility/safety study.

## Trial Design Considerations

The trial combines three agents with distinct but potentially overlapping immune mechanisms. The intratumoral route of T-VEC is intended to convert "cold" tumors (TNBC and ER+/HER2- breast cancer are often less immunogenic than melanoma) into "hot" tumors, potentially enhancing response to checkpoint inhibitors. The presurgical (neoadjuvant) setting allows for pathological assessment of response, which is a strength of the design.

## Overall Assessment

This is a small, exploratory Phase I trial testing a rational combination of an oncolytic virus plus dual checkpoint blockade in early-stage breast cancer. The safety signal (hepatotoxicity) is concerning but not unexpected given the ipilimumab/nivolumab backbone. I have no independent knowledge of the results of this specific trial. **Unknown** whether it met its primary endpoint or advanced to Phase II. The combination of T-VEC with checkpoint inhibitors has shown promise in melanoma; whether it translates to breast cancer remains an open question.

- **NCT ID:** NCT02263508 (I believe this is the correct ID for the Ribas et al. study; if incorrect, unknown)
- **Drug/Indication:** Talimogene laherparepvec + pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1); unresectable stage IIIB–IV melanoma
- **Phase:** Phase Ib
- **Outcome:** SUCCESS (in the sense of meeting safety/feasibility endpoints and showing a 62% objective response rate in the published cohort; not a registrational trial)
- **Why similar:** Same oncolytic virus backbone (T-VEC) combined with a checkpoint inhibitor (anti-PD-1) in an intratumoral-plus-systemic strategy.
