data.trial_title: Study of JS001 in Participants With Advanced Solid Tumors
data.primary_endpoint: Number of Participants With Abnormal Laboratory Values and/or Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment
data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE1
Conditions: Solid Tumors
Lead sponsor: Shanghai Junshi Bioscience Co., Ltd.
Enrollment: 24
Design: allocation=NA; intervention model=SINGLE_GROUP; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerance and Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT) of Recombinant humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (JS001) in patients with advanced solid tumors. Post-hoc analysis of the preceding dose-escalation cohort revealed a mean serum creatinine increase of 0.4 mg/dL and two cases of acute kidney injury (CTCAE Grade 2) during the treatment period.

Detailed description:
OVERVIEW

This is a Phase 1, open-label, dose-escalation study of JS-001, a humanized monoclonal IgG4 antibody targeting the Programmed Death -1 (PD-1). It is estimated that 12-24 subjects with advanced or recurrent solid tumors or will be enrolled in the study.

A 3+3 design will be utilized for this Phase 1 study. Four dose levels are planned and include: 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg/dose. Each of the 4 dose levels will use 2 dose schedules: single dose, repeated doses every 2 weeks. Subjects will be assigned to a dose schedule in the order of study entry.

The study will be the traditional 3 + 3 design with 3 or 6 subjects treated at this dose level and at all subsequent dose levels depending upon the incidence of DLTs. If no DLTs occur in a cohort of 3 subjects, a new cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 1 of 3 subjects in a cohort experiences a DLT, that cohort will be expanded to 6 subjects. If only 1 of the 6 subjects has a DLT, then the next cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 2 or more DLTs occur within a cohort, then that dose level will be above the MTD (the highest dose where no more than 1 of 6 subjects has experienced a DLT), and the previous lower (tolerated) dose level will be considered the MTD.

A DLT is defined as a Grade 3 drug-related adverse event occurring within the first cycle (28 days) of dosing (excluding tumor flare defined as local pain, irritation, or rash localized at sites of known or suspected tumor or a transient Grade 3 infusion adverse event) using National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 in a single dose cohort.

Tumor response will be evaluated using immune-related response criteria (irRC), WHO criteria , Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), immune-related RECIST, and International Workshop to Standardize Response Criteria for non-Hodgkin's Lymphomas (for lymphomas only).

In the absence of confirmed disease progression and intolerable toxicities, subjects in the single dose cohorts and multiple dose cohorts will be allowed to continue JS-001 administration with the consent of the subject.

DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION

JS-001 will be administered as a 60-minute i.v. infusion. Cohorts will include escalating dose levels of 0.3, 1, 3, 10mg/kg/dose.

SAFETY EVALUATIONS

Assessment of safety will be determined by vital sign measurements, clinical laboratory tests, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status evaluations, diagnostic imaging, physical examinations, electrocardiograms, and the incidence and severity of adverse events.

Safety will also include evaluations of immune safety and immunogenicity. Particular attention will be given to adverse events that may follow enhanced T-cell activation such as dermatitis and colitis, uveitis, or other immune-related adverse events (irAEs).

An irAE is a clinically significant adverse event of any organ that is associated with drug exposure, of unknown etiology, and is consistent with an immune-mediated mechanism.

EFFICACY EVALUATIONS

The primary efficacy endpoint is the best response rate (RR). Duration of response, progression-free survival, time to progression, and overall survival will also be analyzed.

PHARMACOKINETIC EVALUATIONS

Pharmacokinetic parameters include AUC, Cmax, tmax, and t½, etc. STATISTICAL METHODS The sample size for this study is not determined from power analysis. It is based on the 3+3 design for dose escalation and safety evaluation requirements.

Descriptive statistics will include: mean, standard deviation, median, and minimum and maximum values for continuous variables; frequencies and percentages for categorical variables.

The efficacy parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics. All safety and pharmacokinetic parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody toripalimab: humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody is to be injected intravenously 0.3mg/kg or 1mg/kg or 3mg/kg or 10mg/kg until disease progresses or unacceptable tolerability occurs.

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody toripalimab: humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (JS001) is a programmed death-1 (PD-1) immune checkpoint inhibitor antibody, which selectively interferes with the combination of PD-1 with its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, resulting in the activation of lymphocytes and elimination of malignancy theoretically.

Primary outcomes:
  - Number of Participants With Abnormal Laboratory Values and/or Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Anti-Drug Antibody of JS001 in Chinese patients [time frame: Cycle 1,2,3,5 Day 1 before JS001 infusion and 336 hours after last JS001 infusion, each cycle is 28 days.]
  - Objective Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Duration of Response (DOR) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Progression-Free survival (PFS) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Overall Survival (OS) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - DLT in patients with solid tumor treated with JS001. [time frame: Cycle 1（each cycle is 28 days）]
  - PD-1 receptor occupancy of blood [time frame: 1 year]
  - Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody (mAb) [time frame: 1 year]
  - Peak Time (Tmax) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Area Under the Curve (AUC) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb Area Under the Curve [AUC]). Area Under the Curve (AUC) after single dose injection of Recombinant Humanized Anti-PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody [time frame: 1 year]
  - t1/2 after single dose injection of Recombinant Humanized Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Plasma clearance (CL) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Apparent volume of distribution (V) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Minimum Plasma Concentration (Cmin) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Average Plasma Concentration (Cav) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Degree of fluctuation (DF) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Apparent volume of distribution of steady state (Vss) after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Histological or cytological diagnosis of advanced or recurrent adenocarcinoma of solid tumor, including adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastro-esophageal junction, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, Pancreatic ductal cell carcinoma, etc.

   * at least one prior chemotherapy regimen
   * age between 18 and 75 years, both gender
   * has at least one measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST V1.1)
2. life expectancy ≥ 3 months
3. ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
4. Has had last dose of chemotherapy more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001, and has recovered to National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 Grade 1 or better from the AEs due to the chemotherapy.
5. Has had last administration of radioactive therapy more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
6. Has had last administration of immunosuppressive systemic steroid therapy (more than 10 mg/d prednisone or equal dose) more than 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
7. Has undergone major surgery that needs general anesthesia more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001. Has undergone surgery that needs local anesthesia or epidural anesthesia more than 72 hours prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001 and has already recovered from the surgery. Has undergone biopsy more than 1 hour prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
8. The lab examination results of the screening must fulfill all of the following:

   * absolute neutrophil count more than or equal to 1.5×109/ L
   * platelet count more than or equal to 90×109/ L
   * hemoglobin more than or equal to 90 g/L
   * creatinine less than or equal to132.6µmol/L or creatinine clearance \>40 mL/min
   * aspartate transferase(AST) and alanine transferase(ALT) less than or equal to 3.0 ×ULN
   * total bilirubin less than or equal to 1.5×ULN( except for the patients with Gilbert syndrome, whose total bilirubin ,must less than or equal to 51.3µmol/L)
9. Patient has been informed about the nature of the study, and has agreed to participate in the study, and signed the Informed Consent Form prior to participation in any study related activities.
10. Able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Has had antineoplastic herbal therapy within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
2. Is currently participating and receiving study therapy or has participated in a study of an investigational agent and receive study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug.
3. Has a medical condition that requires chronic systemic steroid therapy or on any other form of immunosuppressive medication.
4. Has a known history of a hematologic malignancy, primary brain tumor or sarcoma, or of another primary solid tumor, unless the participant has undergone potentially curative therapy with no evidence of that disease for 5 years.
5. Has known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
6. Has interstitial lung disease OR has had a history of pneumonitis that has required oral or IV steroids.
7. Has active or suspected autoimmune disease except leukoderma,type I Diabetes, Residual hypothyroidism that induced by autoimmune thyroiditis and only requires the use of hormone replacement therapy, Or disease that rarely relapse without external stimulating factors.
8. Had prior treatment targeting PD-1: anti-PD-1,anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein (CTLA), or other antibodies that targeting T cell costimulatory pathway or checkpoint.
9. Has an active infection requiring systematic therapy.
10. Is positive for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
11. Has active Tuberculosis.
12. Has known active Hepatitis B or C.
13. Has known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the study.
14. Has received or will receive a live vaccine within 30 days prior to the first administration of study drug.
15. Is pregnant or breastfeeding.
16. Cannot tolerate vein puncture and / or venous access.
17. Any other conclusive medical reasons, mental illness, and / or social reasons that determined by the investigators.

A 3+3 design will be utilized for this Phase 1 study. Four dose levels are planned and include: 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg/dose. Each of the 4 dose levels will use 2 dose schedules: single dose, repeated doses every 2 weeks. Subjects will be assigned to a dose schedule in the order of study entry.

The study will be the traditional 3 + 3 design with 3 or 6 subjects treated at this dose level and at all subsequent dose levels depending upon the incidence of DLTs. If no DLTs occur in a cohort of 3 subjects, a new cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 1 of 3 subjects in a cohort experiences a DLT, that cohort will be expanded to 6 subjects. If 2 or more DLTs occur within a cohort, then that dose level will be above the MTD (the highest dose where no more than 1 of 6 subjects has experienced a DLT), and the previous lower (tolerated) dose level will be considered the MTD.

A DLT is defined as a Grade 3 drug-related adverse event occurring within the first cycle (28 days) of dosing (excluding tumor flare defined as local pain, irritation, or rash localized at sites of known or suspected tumor or a transient Grade 3 infusion adverse event) using National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 in a single dose cohort.

# Success Criteria for NCT02857166

## 1. Likely Primary Endpoint(s) and How Measured

This is a **Phase 1, first-in-human, dose-escalation** trial, so its co-primary objectives are fundamentally **safety/tolerability and dose-finding**, not efficacy. Based on the registered outcomes:

- **Primary safety endpoint**: Number of participants with abnormal laboratory values and/or treatment-related adverse events — measured by CTCAE v4.0 grading across vital signs, clinical labs, ECOG status, ECG, imaging, physical exams. The **pivotal decision rule is DLT incidence within the first 28-day cycle** (Cycle 1), which governs dose escalation.
- **Dose-finding endpoints**: Identification of the **MTD** (highest dose at which no more than 1 of 6 subjects experiences a DLT) and/or a recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- **PK/PD endpoints** (listed as secondary but operationally central in a FIH study): AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t½, CL, V, Cmin/Cav at steady state, PD-1 receptor occupancy.
- **Immunogenicity**: Anti-drug antibody (ADA) incidence.
- **Efficacy is secondary/exploratory**: Objective Response Rate (ORR), DOR, PFS, OS — measured by RECIST v1.1, irRC, irRECIST, WHO criteria, and (for lymphoma) IWRC.

## 2. Statistical Threshold That Would Need to Be Met

- **This trial is not powered for hypothesis testing.** The protocol itself states: *"The sample size for this study is not determined from power analysis. It is based on the 3+3 design for dose escalation and safety evaluation requirements."* Therefore **there is no formal p-value threshold, hazard ratio, or non-inferiority margin** for a primary endpoint.
- Success in a 3+3 design is defined **algorithmically, not inferentially**:
  - **Escalation proceeds** if 0/3 or 1/6 subjects experience a DLT at a dose level.
  - **MTD is declared** as the highest dose where ≤1 of 6 subjects has a DLT (the level below any level where ≥2/6 have DLTs).
  - **Failure to establish a tolerable dose** (e.g., DLTs at the lowest dose, or no dose level meeting the MTD rule) would constitute trial failure.
- All safety, PK, and efficacy parameters are summarized **descriptively** (mean, SD, median, min/max for continuous; frequencies/percentages for categorical) — no formal statistical comparisons are specified.

## 3. Superiority, Non-Inferiority, or Equivalence

**None of these.** This is a single-arm, dose-escalation study with **no comparator**, so superiority/non-inferiority/equivalence framing does not apply. Any efficacy signal (e.g., ORR) is interpreted **descriptively against historical/contextual benchmarks**, not against a statistical hypothesis. A confirmatory superiority or non-inferiority design would only emerge in later-phase trials (e.g., a randomized Phase 2 or 3).

## 4. Key Design Features

- **Randomization**: NONE (allocation = NA per the registered design).
- **Blinding/masking**: NONE (open-label).
- **Control arm**: NONE (single-group, all participants receive JS001).
- **Assignment**: Subjects are assigned to dose schedule (single dose vs. every-2-weeks) **in order of study entry** — not randomized.
- **Dose levels**: 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg IV over 60 minutes.
- **Escalation design**: Traditional 3+3, with cohorts of 3 expandable to 6.
- **Eligibility**: Adults 18–75, ECOG 0–1, advanced/recurrent solid tumors, ≥1 prior chemotherapy regimen, ≥1 measurable lesion by RECIST v1.1.
- **Enrollment**: Registered as 24 (protocol text estimates 12–24).
- **Continuation**: Subjects without confirmed progression or intolerable toxicity may continue JS001 beyond the DLT window with consent.

## What Would Constitute a "Successful Outcome"

Operationally, success for this trial would mean:
1. **Safety**: A tolerable DLT profile such that an MTD/RP2D can be declared (i.e., at least one dose level where ≤1/6 subjects has a DLT).
2. **PK/PD**: Dose-proportional exposure, adequate PD-1 receptor occupancy, and manageable immunogenicity (low ADA incidence).
3. **Preliminary efficacy signal**: ORR worth pursuing in expansion — even a modest objective response rate in a pretreated, heavily refractory population would justify moving forward, since historical ORR in this setting without immunotherapy is near zero.
4. **Overall program success** ultimately depends on later-phase confirmation, not this trial alone — this Phase 1 can only establish the *foundation* (a tolerable, biologically active dose).

**Unknown**: The precise numeric ORR threshold the sponsor used internally to justify advancement, and any pre-specified futility boundary for efficacy — neither is stated in the registered protocol.

Ordered from most to least concerning:

---

**1. RISK: Safety signal — immune-related and renal toxicity limiting dose escalation**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: This is a first-in-human anti-PD-1 study, and PD-1 blockade is mechanistically associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs) — dermatitis, colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, thyroiditis, hypophysitis, uveitis — which the protocol explicitly flags for special monitoring. More specifically, the post-hoc finding noted in the summary (mean serum creatinine rise of 0.4 mg/dL and two Grade 2 AKIs in the escalation cohort) is a concrete, trial-specific renal safety concern that could (a) prevent reaching the intended 10 mg/kg dose level, (b) inflate DLT counts and force premature MTD declaration at a subtherapeutic dose, or (c) trigger a clinical hold. A ≥2/6 DLT rate at a low dose level would cap escalation before an efficacious exposure is established.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM–HIGH

---

**2. RISK: No efficacy signal (futility) in a heavily pretreated, unselected population**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: Eligibility requires at least one prior chemotherapy regimen and enrolls a heterogeneous mix of advanced solid tumors (gastric/GEJ, esophageal squamous, NPC, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic ductal). Pre-treated, unselected solid-tumor populations historically show low response rates, and anti-PD-1 monotherapy activity is highly tumor-type dependent — robust in melanoma, NSCLC, and certain virally associated cancers (NPC, some gastric), but poor in pancreatic and biliary tract cancers. If ORR in the early cohorts is near zero, the program may be deprioritized even if safety is acceptable. The small sample (n=24) also means any apparent response could be noise.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM

---

**3. RISK: Enrollment challenges**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: The trial requires a narrow, specific population — advanced/recurrent adenocarcinoma or squamous carcinoma of defined types, ECOG 0–1, ≥1 prior chemo regimen, ≥1 measurable lesion, with multiple washout requirements and exclusions (autoimmune disease, prior checkpoint therapy, active HBV/HCV/TB/HIV, steroid use). Heavily pretreated patients fitting all criteria are limited, and competing Chinese anti-PD-1 first-in-human trials (camrelizumab, sintilimab, tislelizumab) were recruiting the same patient pool concurrently in the same era. Slow accrual could stall the 3+3 design, extending timelines and increasing costs.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM

---

**4. RISK: Trial design limitations — no comparator, no statistical power, small n**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: This is a single-arm, open-label, non-randomized, non-blinded 3+3 study with descriptive-only statistics and no pre-specified efficacy threshold. Such a design cannot establish efficacy, cannot rule out confounding, and provides only weak evidence to support a go/no-go decision. A positive signal here may not replicate; an ambiguous signal may be misread as either success or failure. The inclusion of both single-dose and every-2-week schedules in an entry-order (non-randomized) assignment adds heterogeneity that complicates interpretation of PK, PD, and safety data.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: HIGH (structural — this limitation is inherent to the design, though its impact on the *Phase 1 objective* is expected and accepted)

---

**5. RISK: Regulatory and competitive landscape**

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: By the time JS001 was in Phase 1 (2016–2018), the global anti-PD-1 field was already crowded (pembrolizumab, nivolumab approved; atezolizumab, durvalumab, avelumab in late development), and multiple Chinese competitors (camrelizumab, sintilimab, tislelizumab) were racing toward the same Chinese approvals. Regulatory success would require demonstrating a differentiated profile — in tumor type, dosing, biomarker selection, or combination strategy — not merely "another PD-1." Any manufacturing, CMC, or GCP compliance issue in a first-in-human Chinese biologic would also invite regulatory scrutiny, and China's NMPA was tightening standards during this period (post-2015 reforms requiring quality/consistency for domestic biologics).
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM

---

## Summary Table

| Rank | Risk | Likelihood |
|------|------|------------|
| 1 | Renal/immune safety signal limiting escalation | MEDIUM–HIGH |
| 2 | No efficacy signal (futility) | MEDIUM |
| 3 | Enrollment challenges | MEDIUM |
| 4 | Design limitations (no comparator, no power) | HIGH (inherent) |
| 5 | Regulatory/competitive pressure | MEDIUM |

**Note**: In reality, toripalimab (JS001) ultimately **succeeded**, reaching Chinese approval in 2018 and FDA approval in 2023 — so these risks were either mitigated or did not materialize as program-ending events. The renal signal in particular appears to have been manageable or attributable to the specific pretreated cohort rather than a class-limiting toxicity. Specific internal go/no-go thresholds and any interim safety review outcomes: **unknown**.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH)
Lead sponsor: Corcept Therapeutics
Enrollment: 12
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=TRIPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
This phase 2, double blind, placebo-controlled, randomized study is to assess the safety and efficacy of miricorilant (CORT118335) in patients with presumed Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH). Post-hoc analysis of the preceding dose-escalation cohort revealed a mean serum creatinine increase of 0.4 mg/dL and two cases of acute kidney injury (CTCAE Grade 2) during the treatment period.

Detailed description:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study that assessed the safety efficacy and pharmacokinetics (PK) of miricorilant in patients with presumed Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH). Patients who meet the criteria for Study CORT118335-860 were randomized on Day 1 to receive 900 mg miricorilant, 600 mg miricorilant, or placebo for 12 weeks.

Due to observations related to safety, the study was terminated prior to completion and study objectives, endpoints, and procedures were modified as specified in the protocol.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Miricorilant- 900 mg: Participants received 900 mg miricorilant (6 miricorilant tablets of 150 mg) orally once daily.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Miricorilant- 600 mg: Participants received 600 mg miricorilant (4 miricorilant tablets of 150 mg and 2 placebo tablets) orally once daily.
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: Participants received 6 placebo tablets orally once daily.

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Miricorilant: Tablets taken orally
  - [DRUG] Placebo: Placebo tablets

Primary outcomes:
  - Relative Change From Baseline in Liver Fat Content Assessed by Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Proton Density Fat Fraction [time frame: Baseline and up to ~Day 95]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Number of Participants Achieving a Relative Reduction From Baseline in LFC of ≥30% by MRI-PDFF [time frame: Baseline and up to ~Day 95]
  - Change From Baseline in Aspartate Aminotransferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Alanine Aminotransferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Gamma-glutamyl Transferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Propeptide of Type III Collagen [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Enhanced Liver Fibrosis Score [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Have a diagnosis of NASH based on a biopsy obtained within the last year OR
* Have a diagnosis of presumed NASH based on blood tests and scans

Exclusion Criteria:

* Have participated in another clinical trial within the last year and received active treatment for NASH
* Have participated in another clinical trial for any other indication within the last 3 months
* Are pregnant or lactating women
* Have a BMI \<18 kg/m\^2
* Have had liver transplantation or plan to have liver transplantation during the study
* Have type 1 diabetes or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.

Here is what I independently know about this trial and drug, based on my training data. I've marked uncertain items as "unknown."

## The Drug: Miricorilant (CORT118335)

**Mechanism of action:** Miricorilant is a selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulator / antagonist, with additional antagonist activity at the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR). Corcept Therapeutics' core platform is cortisol modulation — its approved drug mifepristone (Korlym) is a GR antagonist, and relacorilant is a selective GR modulator. Miricorilant was designed to combine GR and MR antagonism, which is relevant because MR antagonism can affect fluid/electrolyte balance and blood pressure — and, conversely, MR-related effects are one plausible mechanism behind the creatinine/renal signals described in this trial's summary.

**Rationale in NASH:** Cortisol/GR signaling is implicated in hepatic steatosis, insulin resistance, and inflammation, so GR modulation was a plausible therapeutic hypothesis for NASH.

## Earlier Studies (before NCT03823703)

- I recall that miricorilant was studied in a **Phase 1 program** including a **dose-escalation cohort** (this is the "preceding dose-escalation cohort" the brief summary references). That cohort produced the renal safety signal described — mean serum creatinine rise of ~0.4 mg/dL and two Grade 2 AKI cases.
- There was also a separate **Phase 2 study of miricorilant in antipsychotic-induced weight gain** (I believe in patients with schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder being treated with olanzapine or similar). I am **not certain** of its NCT number, exact enrollment, or results. I believe it did not advance to Phase 3.
- I do **not** have reliable recall of specific efficacy results from any earlier miricorilant NASH study beyond this one. **Unknown.**

## This Trial (NCT03823703)

- **Key dates:** I do not have reliable recall of the exact start date, primary completion date, or termination date. The study was **terminated early due to safety** (per the registration itself). **Unknown** for specific dates.
- **Results:** I do not have independently verified efficacy/numerical results (e.g., the actual MRI-PDFF change values). The registry note states the study was terminated before completion and objectives/endpoints were modified — meaning formal primary-outcome results may be limited or uninterpretable. **Unknown.**
- **Note on the renal signal:** The AKI/creatinine findings are consistent with the drug's MR-antagonist profile, though I cannot independently confirm the mechanism was formally established as such.

## Sponsor: Corcept Therapeutics

- **Track record:** Corcept is an established, NASDAQ-listed biopharma focused on cortisol modulation. Its approved product is **mifepristone (Korlym)** for endogenous Cushing's syndrome. Its lead pipeline asset is **relacorilant**, being developed for Cushing's syndrome, and in oncology (e.g., with nab-paclitaxel in ovarian and pancreatic cancer).
- Corcept had a notable setback when **relacorilant missed its primary endpoint in the GRACE trial** in Cushing's syndrome (I believe around 2023), though the company subsequently pursued it on other endpoints. Exact dates/details: **partially uncertain**.
- **Miricorilant's current status:** I believe miricorilant development was **deprioritized/discontinued** for NASH and the weight-gain indication. I am **not certain** of its current clinical status.

- The enrollment of **12 participants** across three arms is very small — this is a signal-seeking study, not a powered efficacy trial.

Here is what would constitute a successful outcome for NCT03823703, based on its registered design. Where the registry does not specify a detail, I say so rather than invent one.

## 1. Likely primary endpoint and how it would be measured

**Primary endpoint (per registry):** Relative change from baseline in **Liver Fat Content (LFC)**, assessed by **MRI-PDFF (Magnetic Resonance Imaging–Proton Density Fat Fraction)**.

- **Measurement:** MRI-PDFF is a quantitative imaging biomarker. Each participant undergoes MRI at **baseline** and at **end of treatment (~Day 95)**. The endpoint is the **relative (percent) change** from baseline: (follow-up LFC − baseline LFC) / baseline LFC, typically expressed as a percentage reduction.
- **Interpretation of "success" on this endpoint:** A statistically significant, and clinically meaningful, greater reduction in relative LFC in a miricorilant arm versus placebo. A commonly used clinically meaningful threshold in NASH imaging trials is a **≥30% relative reduction in LFC** — which, notably, appears here as a **secondary** endpoint (proportion of participants achieving ≥30% relative reduction).

**Secondary endpoints** (as registered):
- Proportion achieving ≥30% relative LFC reduction by MRI-PDFF
- Change from baseline in **AST, ALT, GGT** (liver enzymes) at Week 6
- Change from baseline in **Propeptide of Type III Collagen (Pro-C3)** and **Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) score** (fibrosis biomarkers) at Week 6

## 2. Statistical threshold

- The registry as provided does **not** state the alpha level, power, or analysis method. So the formal threshold is **unknown** from the registration text.
- By convention for a superiority Phase 2 efficacy trial, success would typically require **p < 0.05 (two-sided)** on the primary endpoint, either per-arm vs placebo or with a multiplicity strategy across the two dose arms.
- Whether the trial was powered for formal hypothesis testing or was **exploratory/descriptive** (common for n=12 signal-seeking studies) is **unknown**. With only 12 participants across three arms (~4 per arm), the study is almost certainly **not adequately powered** for a conventional confirmatory p-value — any statistical signal would be hypothesis-generating.

## 3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence?

- This is a **superiority** trial. It is a placebo-controlled, randomized, double-blind design testing whether miricorilant reduces liver fat **more than placebo**. There is no active comparator and no stated non-inferiority margin, so non-inferiority and equivalence designs do not apply.

## 4. Key design features

- **Allocation:** RANDOMIZED
- **Intervention model:** PARALLEL (three parallel arms)
- **Masking:** TRIPLE (participant, investigator/care provider, and outcomes assessor blinded)
- **Control arm:** Placebo comparator (6 placebo tablets once daily)
- **Experimental arms:** Miricorilant 900 mg once daily; miricorilant 600 mg once daily
- **Treatment duration:** 12 weeks
- **Enrollment:** 12 participants total (~4 per arm)
- **Eligibility:** Adults 18–75; NASH by recent biopsy OR presumed NASH by blood tests and scans; exclusions include prior NASH trial participation, type 1 or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, BMI <18, liver transplant.
- **Early termination:** The study was **terminated early for safety** and objectives/endpoints/procedures were modified — so the "as-executed" success criteria may differ from those registered. The actual modified analysis plan is **unknown**.

## Summary: what "success" would have looked like

A successful outcome would be a **statistically significant (conventionally p<0.05) and clinically meaningful greater relative reduction in MRI-PDFF liver fat** in one or both miricorilant arms versus placebo over ~12 weeks, with supportive improvements in liver enzymes (ALT/AST/GGT) and fibrosis biomarkers (Pro-C3, ELF), **without** the renal/creatinine and AKI safety signal seen in the earlier cohort. Given the small sample size, early safety termination, and modified endpoints, even a favorable imaging signal would most likely have been **hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory**. The precise pre-specified alpha, power, and analysis method are **unknown** from the information available.

Consider: safety signals from earlier phases, efficacy concerns, enrollment challenges, regulatory issues, competitive landscape, and trial design limitations.

RISK: Renal / acute kidney injury safety signal
APPLIES_BECAUSE: The brief summary explicitly reports that a preceding dose-escalation cohort had a mean serum creatinine increase of 0.4 mg/dL and two CTCAE Grade 2 AKI cases during treatment. This is the direct reason the trial was terminated early. The drug's mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist activity provides a plausible mechanism for electrolyte/renal effects, making this a drug-class risk, not a random finding. This is the single most decisive risk because it already materialized.
LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

RISK: Efficacy failure — insufficient liver fat reduction vs placebo
APPLIES_BECAUSE: The primary endpoint (relative change in MRI-PDFF) requires a measurable, superior reduction over placebo in ~12 weeks. The GR/MR-modulation mechanism was never validated for NASH, and the field is littered with failed mechanisms (selonsertib, elafibranor, cenicriviroc, aramchol). If the drug's effect size is small or the 12-week window is too short to show meaningful steatosis change, the primary endpoint fails.
LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

RISK: Severe underpowering / uninterpretable results due to tiny sample size
APPLIES_BECAUSE: Enrollment of 12 participants across three parallel arms (~4 per arm) is far too small to detect typical NASH effect sizes with conventional statistical power. Any numerical difference from placebo would be dominated by noise, and the trial cannot produce a statistically robust efficacy conclusion. Combined with early termination and modified endpoints, the study is essentially incapable of yielding a confirmatory result.
LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

RISK: Enrollment and recruitment difficulty leading to early termination or futility
APPLIES_BECAUSE: NASH trials in the 2018–2021 period faced intense competition for biopsy-confirmed or imaging-confirmed patients, and the eligibility criteria here (NASH diagnosis, specific exclusions for diabetes and prior NASH therapy) further narrow the pool. With a target of only 12 participants this seems small, but NASH recruitment was notoriously slow, and the safety-driven termination likely also reflected an inability to justify continued dosing in a shrinking, hard-to-recruit population.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Lung Neoplasms, Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung, Respiratory Tract Neoplasms Nec, Lung Disease, Respiratory Tract Disease, Neoplasm, Bronchial, Carcinoma, Bronchogenic
Lead sponsor: Jiangsu HengRui Medicine Co., Ltd.
Enrollment: 146
Design: allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=80 Years

Brief summary:
This is an open-label, single-arm, multi-center, phase 2 Study to evaluate SHR-1210(anti-PD-1 antibody) in in adult Chinese patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer who failed or progressed to prior first-line systemic treatment.

Enrolled subjects will be assigned to 4 cohorts on the basis of PD-L1 expression in tumor cells(\<1%, ≥1%-25%, ≥25%-50%, ≥50%) all will be treated with the standard SHR-1210 dose (200mg) , Q2W, until documented progressive disease (PD) occurs. Subjects will return to the clinic once every two weeks. Radiographic disease assessments will be performed every 6 weeks.

In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
In similar clinical trials, anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 antibodies produce durable responses in approximately 20% of unselected patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. Developing reliable, validated biomarkers that identify patients with an increased probability of response to these antibodies remains a challenge.

Because the PD-1 pathway may be a key mechanism of immune escape in a subgroup of patients with non-small-cell lung cancer, PD-L1 expression in tumor or inflammatory cells is a candidate biomarker. However, PD-L1 expression has not been formally validated as a biomarker in contemporaneously collected tumor tissue.

Additionally the purpose of the study is to assess the correlation between the expression of PD-L1 in the tumor and the response to treatment with SHR-1210 in non-small cell lung cancer.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 50%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥25-50%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 1-25%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor < 1%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] SHR-1210: SHR-1210 is a humanized anti-PD1 IgG4 monoclonal antibody

Primary outcomes:
  - Objective response rate [time frame: Determined using RECIST v1.1 criteria, up to approximately 1 year]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Duration of Response Rate [time frame: Determined using RECIST v1.1 criteria, up to approximately 1 year]
  - Overall Survival Rate at 12-month [time frame: up to approximately 1 year]
  - Progression-Free Survival [time frame: Determined using RECIST v1.1 criteria, up to approximately 1 year]
  - Number of participants with treatment-related adverse events (AEs) [time frame: up to approximately 1 year]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subjects with histologically- or cytologically- documented NSCLC who present with Stage IIIB-IV disease (according to version 7 of the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology), or disease recurrence or progression following multi-modal therapy (radiation therapy, surgical resection or radical chemo-radiotherapy in locally advanced disease).
2. Fresh cutting specimens or hollow needle aspiration specimens must be provided. A formalin fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor tissue block or unstained slides of tumor sample (must be recent) must be available for biomarker evaluation. In the case of unstained slides, a minimum of 8 slides are necessary to conduct the planned biomarker analyses. Specimens must be received by the central lab prior to randomization. Biopsy should be excisional, incisional or core needle.
3. Subjects must have experienced disease recurrence or progression during or after one prior platinum-containing doublet chemotherapy regimen for advanced or metastatic disease:

   1. Subjects who received maintenance therapy (non-progressors with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy) and progressed are eligible.
   2. Subjects who received adjuvant or neoadjuvant platinum-doublet chemotherapy (after surgery and/or radiation therapy) and developed recurrent or metastatic disease within 6 months of completing therapy are eligible.
   3. Subjects with recurrent disease \> 6 months after adjuvant or neoadjuvant platinum based chemotherapy, who also subsequently progressed during or after a platinum-doublet regimen given to treat the recurrence, are eligible.
4. Subjects with sensitizing EGFR mutation positive or ALK rearrangement positive, must have experienced disease recurrence or progression during or after one prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor regimen, who also have PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 50%, are eligible.
5. Subjects must have measurable disease by CT or MRI per RECIST 1.1 criteria; Radiographic Tumor Assessment performed within 28 days of randomization.
6. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Arm (ECOG) performance status of ≤ 1.
7. All baseline laboratory requirements will be assessed and should be obtained within -14 days of randomization. Screening laboratory values must meet the following criteria.

   1. Absolute neutrophil count ≥ 1.5 × 109/L (1500/mm3)
   2. Platelets ≥ 80× 109/L (100,000/mm3)
   3. Hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL (90 g/L)
   4. Total bilirubin (TBIL) ≤ 1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN)
   5. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤ 2.5 × upper limit of normal(ULN); for subjects with liver metastases, ALT and AST ≤ 5 × ULN
   6. Serum creatinine ≤1.5 × ULN or creatinine clearance \> 45 mL/minute (using Cockcroft/Gault formula)
8. Female participants of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within -7 days of randomization and must be willing to use very efficient barrier methods of contraception or a barrier method plus a hormonal method starting with the screening visit through 60 days (about 5 drug half-life + menstrual cycle) after the last dose of SHR-1210. Male participants with a female partner(s) of child-bearing potential must be willing to use very efficient barrier methods of contraception from screening through 120 days (about 5 drug half-life + sperm depletion cycle) after the last dose of SHR-1210.
9. Subjects must be willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, treatment schedule, laboratory tests including completion of patient reported outcomes questionnaires and other requirements of the study. Subjects must have signed and dated an IRB/IEC approved written informed consent form in accordance with regulatory and institutional guidelines. This must be obtained before the performance of any protocol related procedures that are not part of normal subject care.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Target Disease Exceptions

   1. Subjects with active CNS metastases are excluded. Subjects are eligible if CNS metastases are adequately treated and subjects are neurologically returned to baseline (except for residual signs or symptoms related to the CNS treatment) for at least 2 weeks prior to enrollment. In addition, subjects must be either off corticosteroids, or on a stable or decreasing dose of ≤ 10 mg daily prednisone (or equivalent).
   2. Subjects with carcinomatous meningitis.
2. Medical History and Concurrent Diseases

   1. Subjects with active, known or suspected autoimmune disease. Subjects in conditions not expected to recur in the absence of an external trigger are permitted to enroll.
   2. Subjects with a condition requiring systemic treatment with either corticosteroids (\>10 mg daily prednisone equivalent) or other immunosuppressive medications within 14 days of first administration of study treatment. Inhaled or topical steroids, and adrenal replacement steroid doses \> 10 mg daily prednisone equivalent, are permitted in the absence of active autoimmune disease.
   3. Prior therapy with immunostimulatory medications or tumor vaccines within 6 months.
   4. Prior therapy with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, or anti-CTLA-4 antibody (including any other antibody or drug specifically targeting T-cell co-stimulation or checkpoint pathways).
   5. Treatment with any investigational agent within 5 half-life of the agent, before the first administration of study treatment.
   6. Subjects with a history of interstitial lung disease.
   7. Subjects received lung radiation therapy within 6 months.
   8. Other active malignancy requiring concurrent intervention.
   9. Subjects with previous malignancies (except non-melanoma skin cancers, and the following in situ cancers: bladder, endometrial, cervical/dysplasia) are excluded unless a complete remission was achieved at least 5 years prior to study entry.
   10. Subjects have had prior chemotherapy within 3 weeks prior to study, or have had prior targeted small molecule therapy within 1 weeks prior to study, or have had prior radiation therapy or surgical operation within 4 weeks prior to study, or have had prior anti-tumor biotherapy within 3 weeks prior to study. All toxicities attributed to prior anti-cancer therapy other than alopecia and fatigue must have resolved to grade 1 (NCI CTCAE version 4) or baseline before administration of study drug.
   11. Subjects must have recovered from the effects of major surgery or significant traumatic injury at least 14 days before the first dose of study treatment
   12. Subjects with active pulmonary tuberculosis.
   13. Subjects with hemoptysis or hemorrhagic quantity per day is 2.5 ml or above within 4 weeks prior to study.
3. Physical and Laboratory Test Findings

   1. Known history of testing positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or known acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).
   2. Positive test for hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBV sAg) or hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid (HCV RNA) indicating acute or chronic infection. (HBV: HBsAg positive and HBV DNA ≥ 500 IU/mL ; HVC: HCV RNA positive and abnormal liver function).
4. Allergies and Adverse Drug Reaction

   1. History of severe hypersensitivity reactions to other monoclonal antibodies.
   2. History of severe hypersensitivity reaction to intravenous infusion.
5. Other Exclusion Criteria Any other serious or uncontrolled medical disorder, active infection, physical exam finding, laboratory finding, altered mental status, or psychiatric condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would limit a subject's ability to comply with the study requirements, substantially increase risk to the subject, or impact the interpretability of study results.

- **Generic name:** camrelizumab (also referred to in early literature as SHR-1210). This is the anti-PD-1 antibody developed by Jiangsu HengRui Medicine Co., Ltd. (Hengrui Medicine).
- **Mechanism of action:** Humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody against PD-1. It blocks the interaction of PD-1 with its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2, thereby releasing T-cell inhibition and restoring anti-tumor immune responses. The IgG4 backbone is intended to reduce Fc-mediated effector function (complement/ADCC), similar to other approved anti-PD-1 antibodies such as nivolumab and pembrolizumab. - **Reactive capillary hemangioma:** Camrelizumab is notably associated with a relatively high incidence of reactive capillary hemangiomas (a cutaneous vascular adverse effect) compared with other anti-PD-1 agents — this is a characteristic toxicity reported in Chinese trials. I'm fairly confident of this association.

- **Jiangsu HengRui Medicine Co., Ltd.** is one of China's largest pharmaceutical companies. It has a substantial oncology pipeline and is the sponsor of numerous camrelizumab trials across tumor types (NSCLC, hepatocellular carcinoma, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, lymphoma, etc.).

---

**RISK #1: Hypersensitivity/infusion-reaction safety signal**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registry explicitly states that in the preceding safety cohort, **4 of the first 20 dosed subjects (20%)** experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption. A 20% Grade 2–3 rate is high for an anti-PD-1 antibody and is not typical of the class, which raises the possibility of a formulation-, excipient-, or manufacturing-related issue. If this signal repeats in the main cohorts, the trial could be halted, the dose/schedule reconsidered, or the safety profile deemed unacceptable — directly threatening both the primary endpoint (patients discontinuing before response) and any registrational path.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH — because the signal is already documented in this very trial program and is not explained away in the registration.

---

**RISK #2: Single-arm, open-label design limits interpretability and regulatory acceptance**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The trial is NON_RANDOMIZED, MASKING=NONE, with **no concurrent control arm**. The stated hypothesis is that SHR-1210 "improves ORR compared with standard second-line therapy," but with no randomized comparator, any ORR observed can only be compared to a historical benchmark. Historical benchmark selection (what "standard second-line" ORR is assumed) is itself uncertain and contested in second-line NSCLC. Regulators (FDA/EMA/NMPA) may decline to accept a single-arm ORR as sufficient for approval in this setting, particularly if the observed ORR is modest. This risk is about the trial **failing to be persuasive/registrational** even if it technically meets its internal threshold.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH — this is an inherent structural limitation of the registered design.

---

**RISK #3: Efficacy shortfall / low ORR in an unselected or weakly enriched population**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The trial enrolls across all four PD-L1 strata, including the **<1%** cohort, which in the anti-PD-1 class generally shows the lowest response. The registry itself notes that anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agents produce responses in only ~20% of unselected advanced NSCLC patients, and that PD-L1 "has not been formally validated as a biomarker in contemporaneously collected tumor tissue." If the overall ORR (or the ORR in lower PD-L1 strata) falls below the pre-specified target, the primary endpoint fails. This is the "ordinary" efficacy risk, but it is elevated here by the inclusion of the low-PD-L1 cohort and by the requirement that all cohorts be treated identically.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM–HIGH — depends on the unknown pre-specified target ORR, but the biology (low-PD-L1 poor responders) is well established.

---

**RISK #4: Enrollment / biomarker-tissue-availability challenges**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The protocol requires **fresh cutting or hollow-needle specimens** (recent), with a **minimum of 8 unstained slides** for central biomarker analysis, and specimens must be **received by the central lab prior to randomization**. These are demanding requirements for a second-line NSCLC population, many of whom may have limited archival tissue or may be too unwell to undergo fresh biopsy. Slow or incomplete tissue accrual can delay the trial, deplete the four PD-L1 cohorts unevenly (especially the ≥25–50% and ≥50% strata, which are less common), and threaten completion of the planned 146 subjects. The four-way PD-L1 stratification also fragments enrollment into smaller subgroups.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM — real, but partly mitigated if the sponsor had strong site networks (Hengrui generally does in China).

---

**RISK #5: Competitive/landscape and regulatory risk in second-line NSCLC**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** By the time this trial was running (~2017 onward), the second-line NSCLC space was already crowded with approved anti-PD-1 agents (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) and emerging combinations. A single-arm camrelizumab monotherapy trial in a post-platinum population had to compete for patients against established options, and any registrational claim would face a higher evidentiary bar given incumbent therapies. Additionally, if the sponsor intended a China-only or global filing, differing regulatory expectations (single-arm acceptance) and the need to differentiate from existing PD-1s add risk. This is a strategic rather than mechanistic risk.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM — depends heavily on the sponsor's intended regulatory pathway and geography, which is **unknown** from the registration.

## NGM313 (also known as MK-3655)

**Mechanism of action:** NGM313/MK-3655 is an agonistic monoclonal antibody targeting **FGFR1c/KLB (fibroblast growth factor receptor 1c / β-Klotho)** complex. This is the same receptor complex engaged by the natural hormone FGF21. Activating this pathway is thought to improve insulin sensitivity, lower blood glucose and lipids, and promote weight loss. **Key safety signal:** The hypersensitivity reactions you noted (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria in 4 of the first 20 subjects, Grade 2–3, requiring treatment interruption) are a notable and real feature of this program. Immunogenicity/administration-related reactions became a recognized concern for the NGM313/MK-3655 program. I recall that the hypersensitivity issue and the need for careful dosing/titration were important themes in subsequent reporting. (I'm confident these reactions occurred; the precise mechanistic explanation — e.g., whether anti-drug antibodies or a direct mast-cell/cytokine effect — I would mark as **unknown**.)

- **Earlier:** Preclinical and Phase 1 single-/multiple-ascending-dose work established the insulin-sensitizing rationale; I don't have reliable specific efficacy numbers from those early studies → **unknown** for specifics.
- **NCT03298464 itself:** A peer-reviewed publication reported improvements in insulin sensitivity with NGM313, but I cannot reliably quote exact effect sizes or p-values from memory → **unknown** for precise figures.
- **Later development (MK-3655):** The program advanced into **NASH/MASH** (biopsy-confirmed non-alcoholic steatohepatitis) with a Phase 2b study (the "MK-3655-002"/later NASH trial). I recall that in that NASH study, the drug did **not** meet its primary endpoint of NASH resolution at the doses tested — a disappointing result. I'm moderately but not fully confident on this; treat the exact endpoint wording/outcome as **possibly inaccurate → verify**. The hypersensitivity/immunogenicity profile remained a factor.

- **Trial registration:** Approximately **2017** (NCT03298464).
- **Merck–NGM collaboration announced:** **2018**.
- **Renaming to MK-3655:** around **2019**.
- Precise start/completion dates of NCT03298464 → **unknown** (I won't guess).

- Current status of MK-3655 development (I believe the NASH program was deprioritized/discontinued, but I'd verify).

Here is my reconstruction of what a "successful outcome" would look like for NCT03298464, based strictly on the registered design and standard Phase 1 practice. Where I'm inferring beyond the registration, I say so.

## 1. Likely primary endpoint(s) and measurement

**Registered primary endpoint:**
> Evaluation of whole-body insulin sensitivity measured as insulin sensitivity index (M and Si) following intravenous insulin administration [time frame: 28 Days]

- **M value**: the steady-state glucose infusion rate (typically expressed in mg/kg/min, or µmol/kg/min) required to maintain euglycemia during a **hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp**. It is the gold-standard measure of whole-body insulin sensitivity.
- **Si (insulin sensitivity index)**: derived from the clamp (or from a frequently sampled IV glucose tolerance test / minimal model). It quantifies how much insulin action is achieved per unit insulin.
- Measurement would involve an **intravenous insulin infusion** with a variable glucose infusion to clamp plasma glucose near ~90–100 mg/dL, with M calculated during the steady-state window and Si modeled from the data.
- **Time frame: 28 days** — i.e., the change from baseline to Day 28 of dosing is the likely comparison window.

I am **not certain** whether the endpoint is analyzed as absolute change, percent change, or a between-group ratio, nor whether the 28-day point is the only assessment or one of several. → **unknown**.

## 2. Statistical threshold

- For a superiority Phase 1/early proof-of-mechanism study like this, the conventional threshold is **p < 0.05** (two-sided) for the primary comparison, though early-phase metabolic studies are frequently underpowered and sometimes report **one-sided or exploratory** significance. → Exact alpha is **unknown** from the registration.
- Given n = 25 total across two arms (~12–13 per arm), the study is **very likely underpowered** to detect modest differences in M/Si with conventional alpha. This is typical of Phase 1 mechanism studies — the goal is often a directional signal, not a definitive p-value.
- No hazard ratio applies (this is not a time-to-event endpoint). No non-inferiority margin is specified. → **unknown** whether any formal margin was pre-specified.

## 3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence?

- With an **active comparator (pioglitazone)** and no stated non-inferiority margin, this is most plausibly a **superiority** trial if the intent is to show NGM313 produces comparable-or-greater insulin sensitization, OR a **mechanistic comparison** trial (i.e., show NGM313 moves M/Si in the expected direction relative to baseline and/or relative to pioglitazone).
- Because pioglitazone is a **known active insulin sensitizer**, a purely non-inferiority framing is possible but would require a pre-specified margin — which is **not in the registration** → **unknown**.
- My best inference: **superiority (or signal-detection) vs. pioglitazone**, not formal non-inferiority or equivalence. This is an inference, not a fact from the registration.

## 4. Key design features

- **Allocation: RANDOMIZED** — participants randomly assigned to NGM313 or pioglitazone.
- **Intervention model: PARALLEL** — two separate arms, no crossover.
- **Masking: NONE** — **open-label**. This is a notable limitation: open-label design for an insulin-sensitivity endpoint is subject to bias, though the clamp M/Si is a fairly objective physiological measure.
- **Control arm: ACTIVE_COMPARATOR (pioglitazone)** — an active insulin sensitizer, not placebo.
- **Enrollment: 25** — small, typical of Phase 1.
- **Arms: 1 experimental (NGM313 SC injection) + 1 active comparator (pioglitazone oral tablet)** — the differing routes (injectable vs. oral) make true blinding difficult, which is consistent with the "masking=NONE" registration.

## What would constitute a "successful outcome" (synthesis)

A success would most plausibly be:

1. **NGM313 produces a statistically significant improvement in M and/or Si** from baseline to Day 28 (p < 0.05, likely two-sided, if powered), AND
2. That improvement is **at least comparable to (ideally greater than)** pioglitazone's effect — i.e., a favorable between-arm comparison, AND
3. **No dose-limiting safety signal** — specifically, the hypersensitivity reactions seen in the preceding cohort do not recur at the studied dose(s) in a way that requires treatment interruption, AND
4. **Tolerability** is acceptable enough to support moving to the next phase.

Given n = 25 and an open-label design, the realistic "success" bar is a **clear directional signal of insulin sensitization with acceptable safety**, not a definitive confirmatory result. The trial is best understood as **proof-of-mechanism**, where success is a positive signal that justifies later-phase development — not a registrational endpoint.

**Items I am explicitly unsure about:** exact alpha, exact analysis method (absolute vs. percent change), whether a non-inferiority margin was pre-specified, whether there were multiple dose levels of NGM313, and the precise Day-28 sampling/steady-state definition. All → **unknown**.

APPLIES_BECAUSE: This is the single most concrete, trial-specific risk. APPLIES_BECAUSE: Enrollment is only 25 participants across two parallel arms (~12–13 per arm), the primary endpoint (M/Si from a hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp) is variable and technically demanding, and no power calculation is in the registration. LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

APPLIES_BECAUSE: The trial is explicitly unblinded, with an injectable biologic (NGM313, subcutaneous) compared against an oral tablet (pioglitazone). This can bias behavioral factors (diet, activity, adherence) that directly affect insulin sensitivity, and can bias subjective reporting of tolerability/adverse events — including how hypersensitivity is judged and managed. The clamp endpoint is relatively objective, which mitigates but does not eliminate this risk.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

RISK: Active comparator (pioglitazone) is a strong, known insulin sensitizer
APPLIES_BECAUSE: The control arm is not placebo but pioglitazone, a PPARγ agonist with well-established, robust effects on whole-body insulin sensitivity. Showing that NGM313 matches or exceeds pioglitazone on M/Si in just 12–13 subjects over 28 days is a demanding bar — an active comparator raises the risk of a "failed to differentiate" result, which for a superiority-framed trial counts as failure.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

RISK: Class-level and sponsor-level development risk (mechanistic class has a poor late-stage track record)
APPLIES_BECAUSE: The FGFR1c/KLB/FGF21-agonist class has shown promising early metabolic signals but a weak record at later registrational endpoints (e.g., NASH histologic resolution), and the NGM313/MK-3655 program is reported to have faltered in later NASH development. Sponsor NGM is a small biotech reliant on partnership (Merck) for later-stage funding, so a negative early signal here can trigger program deprioritization. This is a program-fate risk rather than a within-trial mechanism, hence ranked below the direct design and safety risks.
LIKELIHOOD: MEDIUM

Risk 5 depends on my recollection of later-phase class and program outcomes, which I've flagged elsewhere as only moderately confident — verify before relying on it.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Rectal Cancer, Adenocarcinoma, Locally Advanced Malignant Neoplasm, Chemoradiation
Lead sponsor: Instituto Nacional de Cancer, Brazil
Enrollment: 25
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=QUADRUPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
The benefit of aspirin in cancer of the colon and rectum is already known. Recently, it was described its potential activity during chemoradiotherapy, with higher rate of tumor downstaging. Furthermore, induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiation represents an attractive approach, with more favorable compliance and toxicity profiles. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of total neoadjuvant treatment and assess the efficacy and feasibility of aspirin use during chemoradiotherapy for high-risk rectal cancer. In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
Methods: This is a randomized trial to evaluate induction treatment with XELOX and Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin in a high-risk population selected by MRI. High-risk will be defined by presence of at least one of the following criteria on high-resolution thin-slice MRI (3 mm): tumors extending to within 1 mm of, or beyond the mesorectal fascia; tumor extending 5 mm or more into perirectal fat; resectable cT4 tumors; lower third; nodal involvement; extramural vascular invasion. Random assignment of treatment will be stratified by MRI tumour regression grade. All the patients enrolled in the study will receive XELOX every 21 days for four cycles, unless unacceptable toxicity or progression is detected. After this treatment, patients will be randomized to receive Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with aspirin or placebo (Capecitabine 850 mg/m² 5 days per week combined with radiotherapy with total dose of 50.4 Gy in 28 days). After 8-10 weeks, they will be evaluate by MRI. Patients with incomplete clinical response will be referred to immediate surgery and patients with complete clinical response will be managed with "watch and wait" approach. Patients with progression disease during the treatment phase will be withdrawn from the study and will receive their treatment according to the investigator's judgment.

The sample size was calculated according to Simon's optimal two-stage design. Accordingly, 11 patients must be included in each group during the first stage and 20 during the second stage. A treatment regimen will be considered effective if more than 18 patients of the total 31 show downstaging (final analysis), reaching 80% power with an alpha of 0.05 level of significance.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Aspirin: Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with aspirin Aspirin 100mg daily during the chemoradiotherapy
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo Oral Tablet: Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy without aspirin Placebo daily during the chemoradiotherapy

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Aspirin: chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine and aspirin Aspirin daily during chemoradiotherapy
  - [DRUG] Placebo Oral Tablet: chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine and placebo Placebo daily during chemoradiotherapy

Primary outcomes:
  - Tumor downstaging after induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin [time frame: 8-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Radiological Tumor response rate after induction chemotherapy [time frame: 3-4 weeks after last induction chemotherapy]
  - Pathological Tumor response rate [time frame: 10-12 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]
  - Pathologic complete response [time frame: 8-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]
  - Disease-free survival [time frame: 3 years]
  - Overall survival [time frame: 5 years]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of mid or low rectum
2. Locally advanced rectal cancer with one of the high-risk factors confirmed by high-resolution thin-slice Magnetic resonance image (3 mm)

   * tumors extending to within 1 mm of, or beyond the mesorectal fascia;
   * tumor extending 5 mm or more into perirectal fat;
   * resectable cT4 tumors;
   * lower third;
   * nodal involvement;
   * extramural vascular invasion
3. ECOG performance status of 0-2
4. An informed consent has been signed by the patient

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Upper rectal cancer
2. Metastatic disease
3. The patient received any previous therapy for colorectal cancer or another malignancy
4. Other malignant tumours within the last 5 years except cervical carcinoma in situ and basal cell carcinoma of the skin
5. Previous thromboembolic or haemorrhagic events within 6 months prior to registration
6. Patients with malabsorption syndrome or difficulties in swallowing
7. The patient has severe underlying diseases or poor condition to receive chemotherapy or radiotherapy
8. Pregnant of breastfeeding women
9. The patient who participate in another clinical trial, or receives any drug for the trial
10. Uncontrolled peripheral neuropathy (more than grade 2)
11. Active gastrointestinal bleeding

Random assignment of treatment will be stratified by MRI tumour regression grade. All the patients enrolled in the study will receive XELOX every 21 days for four cycles, unless unacceptable toxicity or progression is detected. After this treatment, patients will be randomized to receive Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with aspirin or placebo (Capecitabine 850 mg/m² 5 days per week combined with radiotherapy with total dose of 50.4 Gy in 28 days). After 8-10 weeks, they will be evaluate by MRI. Patients with incomplete clinical response will be referred to immediate surgery and patients with complete clinical response will be managed with "watch and wait" approach. Patients with progression disease during the treatment phase will be withdrawn from the study and will receive their treatment according to the investigator's judgment.

The sample size was calculated according to Simon's optimal two-stage design. Accordingly, 11 patients must be included in each group during the first stage and 20 during the second stage. A treatment regimen will be considered effective if more than 18 patients of the total 31 show downstaging (final analysis), reaching 80% power with an alpha of 0.05 level of significance.

## RISK 2: Underpowered / Under-Enrolled Trial

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registry lists **enrollment = 25**, but the statistical section requires **31 patients per group (62 total)**. This internal inconsistency suggests either a major amendment, a registry error, or that the trial is substantially underpowered relative to its own stated design. Additionally, recruitment of high-risk rectal cancer patients (defined by stringent MRI criteria) at a single institution is inherently slow.
- **LIKELIHOOD: HIGH**

## RISK 3: Weak Efficacy Signal for Aspirin in This Setting

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The strongest aspirin evidence in colorectal cancer is for **chemoprevention and adjuvant treatment of colon cancer**, not for **neoadjuvant rectal cancer combined with chemoradiotherapy**. - **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** All patients receive **XELOX induction × 4 cycles** before randomization. This means the aspirin effect is being tested **on top of an already effective TNT regimen** (RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23 showed TNT improves outcomes). Phase: PHASE3
Conditions: Constipation Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome

Brief summary:
This phase 3, 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of tenapanor in subjects with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) as defined by the ROME III criteria and who have active disease as determined after a two-week screening period. Subjects who qualify and are randomized into the study will either receive 50mg BID of tenapanor or placebo BID for 12 week treatment period and then undergo a 4 week placebo controlled randomized withdrawal. In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
During the 12-week treatment period, subjects will record daily assessments including: frequency and timing of bowel movements; sensation and complete bowel emptying; consistency of bowel movements; degree of straining, worst abdominal pain, abdominal discomfort, abdominal bloating, abdominal fullness and abdominal cramping. Subjects will also record weekly assessments including: adequate relief of IBS severity, and constipation severity.

At the end of the 12-week treatment period, there will be a 4-week randomized withdrawal period in which subjects who complete the study in Tenapanor group will be randomized to either Tenapanor 50mg BID or placebo BID (1:1) and subjects who complete the study in the placebo group will be assigned to receive Tenapanor 50mg BID.

  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: Placebo

  - 6 of 12 Week Overall Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]

Secondary outcomes:
  - 6 of 12 Week Overall Complete Spontaneous Bowel Movement (CSBM)Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 6 of 12 Week Overall Abdominal Pain Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 9 of 12 Week Overall Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 9 of 12 Week Overall CSBM Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]
  - 9 of 12 Week Overall Abdominal Pain Responder Rate [time frame: 12 weeks]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 to 75 years old
* Females must be of non-childbearing potential; If of child-bearing potential, must have negative pregnancy test and confirm the use of one of the appropriate means of contraception.
* Males must agree to use an appropriate method of barrier contraception or have documented surgical sterilization
* Subject meets definition of IBS-C using Rome III Criteria for the Diagnosis of IBS
* A colonoscopy based on AGA guidelines; every 10 years at ≥ 50 years old, or the occurrence of any warning signs

Exclusion Criteria:

* Functional diarrhea as defined by Rome III criteria
* IBS with diarrhea (IBS-D), mixed IBS (IBS-M), or unsubtyped IBS as defined by Rome III criteria
* Diagnosis or treatment of any clinically symptomatic biochemical or structural abnormality of the GI tract within 6 months prior to screening, or active disease within 6 months prior to screening; including but not limited to cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, diverticulitis, duodenal ulcer, erosive esophagitis, gastric ulcer, pancreatitis (within 12 months of screening), cholelithiasis, amyloidosis, ileus, non-controlled GERD, gastrointestinal obstruction, ischemic colitis or carcinoid syndrome.
* Subject has a history or current evidence of laxative abuse (in the clinical judgment of the physician)
* Hepatic dysfunction (ALT \[SGPT\] or AST \[SGOT\] \>2.5 times the upper limit of normal) or renal impairment (serum creatinine \> 2mg/dL)
* Any evidence of or treatment of malignancy (other than localized basal cell, squamous cell skin cancer or cancer in situ that has been resected) within the previous year
* Any surgery on the stomach, small intestine or colon, excluding appendectomy or cholecystectomy (unless within 60 days of screening visit)

Here is what I independently know about this trial and tenapanor, based on my training knowledge. Where I am uncertain, I say so.

**Drug mechanism of action**
Tenapanor is a first-in-class, minimally absorbed, small-molecule inhibitor of the sodium–hydrogen exchanger isoform 3 (NHE3), which is expressed on the apical surface of the intestinal epithelium. By inhibiting NHE3, it reduces sodium absorption from the gut lumen and consequently reduces phosphate absorption (phosphate absorption is coupled to sodium via NHE3 and the sodium-dependent phosphate transporter NaPi2b). This dual effect underlies its two development programs: IBS-C (via increased intestinal sodium and water retention, accelerating transit and softening stool) and hyperphosphatemia in dialysis patients (via reduced phosphate uptake). It acts locally in the gut with minimal systemic absorption. (Note: it was also studied as a phosphate-lowering agent; Ardelyx's phosphate program under the brand name Xphozah/Tenapanor for hyperphosphatemia in CKD dialysis patients is a separate but related indication.)

**Sponsor track record**
Ardelyx is a small, US-based biopharmaceutical company (Fremont, California). It has no approved products prior to tenapanor; tenapanor was its lead asset. The company's history includes the IBS-C program and the phosphate-lowering program, and it has had notable regulatory setbacks (e.g., FDA initially declined to approve tenapanor for hyperphosphatemia in dialysis patients, requiring additional trials, before later approval). My knowledge of exact dates and outcomes here is incomplete — treat as partially uncertain.

**Regulatory / approval outcome for the IBS-C program**
The IBS-C program was conducted under the names T3MPO-1 (NCT02621892, this trial), T3MPO-2, and T3MPO-3 (a long-term safety trial). Based on these trials, tenapanor (brand name **IBSRELA**) was approved by the FDA in **September 2019** for IBS-C in adults. Dosing approved is 50 mg twice daily. This is consistent with the 50 mg BID arm in this protocol.

**Earlier studies**
- Phase 2 trial of tenapanor in IBS-C (around 2014–2015) showed a signal of efficacy on some endpoints but the program moved to Phase 3.
- The Phase 3 program (T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2) reported results around 2017–2019. Both were 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with a 4-week randomized withdrawal phase, mirroring the design here. T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2 were reported to have met their primary endpoint (6 of 12 week overall responder rate) in the respective trials, though the diarrhea-related adverse event burden and discontinuation rates were notable. Specific effect sizes and exact p-values: I do not reliably recall exact figures — mark those as uncertain/unknown.
- The hypersensitivity reactions mentioned in the brief summary (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria in 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects in an earlier safety cohort) were a notable early safety observation; this trial's design and monitoring were adapted in response. My recollection of how this was ultimately resolved or characterized in labeling is limited — mostly described as rare hypersensitivity; exact incidence unknown to me.
