Phase: PHASE1
Conditions: Advanced Solid Tumors Cancer
Lead sponsor: AbbVie
Enrollment: 19
Design: allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=not specified

Brief summary:
This is an open-label, Phase I, dose-escalation study to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and the recommended phase two dose (RPTD), and to assess the safety, preliminary efficacy, and pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of ABBV-176 for participants with advanced solid tumors likely to express Prolactin Receptor (PRLR). The study will consist of 2 cohorts: Dose Escalation and Expanded Recommended Phase 2 Dose. In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Dose Escalation Cohort: ABBV-176 will be administered via intravenous infusion at escalating dose levels until the maximum tolerated dose is reached.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Expanded RPTD Cohort: ABBV-176 via intravenous administration in participants with breast cancer at the Recommended Phase Two Dose (RPTD) determined during the Dose Escalation Cohort

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] ABBV-176: Intravenous infusion

Primary outcomes:
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: Tmax of ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 57 days]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: AUC∞ for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 57 days]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: Terminal phase elimination rate constant (β) for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 57 days]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: Recommended Phase 2 dose (RPTD) for ABBV-176 [time frame: Minimum first cycle of dosing (up to 21 days)]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: Cmax of ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 57 days]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: Maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of ABBV-176 [time frame: Minimum first cycle of dosing (up to 21 days)]
  - Expanded Recommended Phase Two Dose (RPTD) Cohort: Objective Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: Up to approximately 2 years]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: AUCt for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 57 days]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: t1/2 for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 57 days]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: AUCt for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 15 days]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: Tmax of ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 15 days]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: Overall Survival (OS) [time frame: Up to 2 years after the last dose of study drug]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: Cmax of ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 15 days]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: Duration of Response (DOR) [time frame: Up to approximately 2 years]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: Terminal phase elimination rate constant (β) for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 15 days]
  - Expanded Recommended Phase Two Dose (RPTD) Cohort: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) [time frame: Up to approximately 2 years]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: Change in ECOG Performance Status [time frame: Up to approximately 2 years]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: AUC∞ for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 15 days]
  - Expanded RPTD Cohort: t1/2 for ABBV-176 [time frame: Up to approximately 15 days]
  - Dose Escalation Cohort: Change from Baseline in QTcF [time frame: Up to approximately 47 days]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participant has histological confirmation of a locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor of a type associated with Prolactin Receptor (PRLR) expression that has progressed on prior treatment, is not amenable to treatment with curative intent, and has no other therapy options known to provide clinical benefit or the subject is ineligible for such therapies.
* Dose Escalation Cohort: must have breast cancer, colorectal cancer, adrenocortical carcinoma, chromophobe renal cell carcinoma.
* Expanded Cohort: must have breast cancer.
* Participant must consent to provide the following for biomarker analyses:
* Dose Escalation Cohort: archived tumor tissue or fresh tumor biopsy.
* Expanded Cohort: archived tumor tissue and fresh tumor biopsy.
* Participant has Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0-1.
* Participant has adequate bone marrow, renal, and hepatic function.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participant received anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, biologic, or any investigational therapy within 21 days before Study Day 1; participant received palliative radiotherapy or small molecule targeted anti-cancer agents within 14 days of Study Day 1.
* Participant has prior exposure to any pyrrolobenzodiazopine-containing agent
* Participant has unresolved, clinically significant toxicities from prior anticancer therapy, defined as greater than Grade 1 on Common Terminology for adverse events.
* Participant has clinically significant uncontrolled conditions.
* Participant has a history of major immunologic reaction to any Immunoglobulin G (IgG).
* Participant has received more than 4 prior lines of systemic cytotoxic therapy (not including neo-adjuvant or adjuvant therapy).

  * For prior cytotoxic therapy, treatment for 1 full cycle or less will not be considered as prior therapy unless the patient experienced progression of disease while on that therapy.
* Participant has a history of \>= grade 3 AST, ALT, or bilirubin increase or has extensive liver resection (i.e., left lobe resection).
* Participant has a history of cholecystitis (subject with history of cholecystectomy will not be excluded), or has active gallbladder disease.

# Success Criteria for NCT03145909

## 1. Likely Primary Endpoints and How They Would Be Measured

**Dose Escalation Cohort (the design-determining portion):**
- **MTD (Maximum Tolerated Dose):** Determined via a 3+3 or similar dose-escalation algorithm. The MTD is the highest dose at which ≤1/6 (or a pre-specified fraction) of evaluable participants experience a Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT) during the first cycle (21 days). This is not a statistical hypothesis test — it's a decision rule.
- **RPTD (Recommended Phase 2 Dose):** Selected by integrating MTD with PK, pharmacodynamic, and preliminary activity data. Also a decision, not a hypothesis test.
- **PK parameters (Tmax, Cmax, AUC∞, AUCt, t½, β):** Descriptive summaries (means, CV%, geometric means) with no inferential threshold. Success is simply that these are characterizable.
- **Objective Response Rate (ORR) in the Expanded RPTD Cohort:** Measured by RECIST 1.1 (or possibly irRECIST), confirmed responses required. ORR = (CR + PR) / evaluable participants.

**If a formal efficacy claim were intended**, ORR by RECIST 1.1 would be the operative endpoint. However, for a Phase 1 expansion, ORR is typically reported descriptively with a confidence interval, not tested against a null.

## 2. Statistical Threshold

- **Dose escalation:** No p-value. Success = MTD identified, RPTD declared, DLT rate below threshold (commonly ≤33% at MTD across evaluable patients).
- **Expanded cohort ORR:** A typical Phase 1 expansion "success" threshold would be a lower bound of the 90% or 95% CI exceeding a pre-specified futility rate (e.g., ORR ≥ 20–30% in breast cancer, depending on subtype and line of therapy). This is often a Simon two-stage or Bayesian futility-monitoring design rather than a formal hypothesis test.
- **Formal statistical significance (p<0.05):** **unknown** — there is no evidence in the registered design that this trial was powered for a hypothesis test. It is a Phase 1, non-randomized study.
- **Hazard ratio / non-inferiority margin:** Not applicable to the primary design as registered. PFS and OS appear as secondary outcomes and would be summarized with Kaplan-Meier estimates and medians, not formally tested.

## 3. Superiority, Non-Inferiority, or Equivalence

**None of these.** This is a single-arm, non-randomized, open-label, dose-finding Phase 1 study. There is no control arm and no formal comparative hypothesis. Success is defined by:
- Establishing a tolerable dose,
- Demonstrating sufficient PK exposure,
- Observing preliminary antitumor activity above a futility bar.

Any "success" language is descriptive/exploratory, not inferential.

## 4. Key Design Features

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Randomization | **NON_RANDOMIZED** (per registered spec) |
| Blinding / masking | **NONE** (open-label) |
| Control arm | **None** (single-arm, both cohorts experimental) |
| Allocation | Non-randomized, parallel cohorts |
| Intervention model | Parallel (Dose Escalation vs. Expanded RPTD) |
| Primary purpose | Dose-finding / safety (MTD, RPTD) |
| Typical escalation design | 3+3 or mTPI/BOIN — **exact algorithm unknown** |
| Sample size rationale | n=19; presumably not powered for efficacy — **design assumptions unknown** |

**Design-specific "success" definition:**
1. No DLT-driven halt; MTD and RPTD declared.
2. PK profile adequate (measurable exposure, predictable Tmax/t½, no unexpected accumulation).
3. Safety profile acceptable — no MTD-exceeding toxicity signal; **hypersensitivity was already observed (4/20 Grade 2–3), so a key success criterion would be that this is manageable with premedication/rate control.**
4. Preliminary ORR in the expansion cohort exceeds the pre-specified futility threshold, providing rationale for Phase 2.

## Unknowns
- Exact escalation algorithm (3+3 vs. model-based): **unknown**
- Pre-specified futility rate / Simon stage boundaries: **unknown**
- Whether DLT window was 21 or 28 days: **unknown** (registered interval is "up to 21 days")
- Whether ORR required confirmation: **unknown**
- Any formal alpha spending or power calculation: **unknown**

In short: this trial's "success" would be a **dose-finding and safety success with a supportive efficacy signal above a futility bar**, not a statistical superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence result.

What are the key risk factors that could cause this trial to fail?

List 3-5 specific risks, ordered from most to least concerning. For each risk, provide:

Consider: safety signals from earlier phases, efficacy concerns, enrollment challenges, regulatory issues, competitive landscape, and trial design limitations.

# Key Risk Factors for NCT03145909

**1. RISK: PBD-payload class toxicity (hypersensitivity and beyond)**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The exclusion criterion barring prior exposure to any pyrrolobenzodiazepine-containing agent confirms ABBV-176 carries a PBD-dimer payload. PBD ADCs — most notably AbbVie's own Rova-T — have been associated with severe class toxicities including infusion/hypersensitivity reactions, pleural and pericardial effusions, photosensitivity, and vascular effects. More directly, the trial's own safety cohort already produced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) in 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects, requiring treatment interruption. This is not a theoretical risk — it is an observed, on-trial signal that directly threatens dose escalation and the ability to reach an MTD/RPTD.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

**2. RISK: Failure to establish a tolerable and effective dose (MTD/RPTD not reachable or not meaningful)**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The entire primary objective of the dose-escalation cohort is to determine MTD and RPTD. If hypersensitivity and other toxicities force repeated dose de-escalation, treatment interruption, or early discontinuation, the trial may fail to identify a dose that is both tolerable and likely to be efficacious. With only n=19 enrolled, the study has very little room to absorb dose-limiting toxicities or patient dropouts before becoming uninterpretable.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

**3. RISK: Efficacy failure — unvalidated target (PRLR) and weak preliminary activity**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** Prolactin receptor is not an established oncogenic driver or clinically validated ADC target, and the indication is heavily pretreated advanced solid tumors (up to 4 prior cytotoxic lines allowed, progressed on prior therapy). This is a last-line population unlikely to respond robustly. The expanded cohort's primary endpoint is ORR, and if the observed response rate falls below the futility bar (especially in breast cancer, where competing ADCs like T-DXd have set a high efficacy bar), the program is not viable.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

**4. RISK: Small sample size and non-randomized, open-label design limiting interpretability**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** With allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED, masking=NONE, no control arm, and n=19, the trial cannot support comparative efficacy claims and is highly vulnerable to selection bias, confounding by prior therapy, and chance findings. A single-arm open-label design also makes it difficult to distinguish drug-related toxicity from disease- or infusion-related events, and small numbers mean PK and safety estimates are unstable. Even a genuinely active drug could fail to show a clear signal with this design.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

**5. RISK: Competitive landscape making the program commercially unattractive**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** By the time this trial was running (~2017–2019), the HER2 and breast cancer ADC space was being transformed by highly effective agents (e.g., T-DXd/Enhertu and others). AbbVie's own PBD-ADC experience (Rova-T) had already collapsed. If ABBV-176 could not clearly differentiate on efficacy or safety — and the hypersensitivity signal harms differentiation — the sponsor would rationally discontinue regardless of a modest signal. I recall this is in fact what happened (program discontinued), which supports this as a real, realized risk.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM–HIGH (I'm treating this as MEDIUM on a mechanistic basis but noting it likely materialized)

---

**Ordering rationale:** Safety (PBD class + the already-observed hypersensitivity signal) is the most concerning because it is an *observed on-trial event* that directly threatens the dose-finding objective, making risk #1 and #2 tightly coupled and dominant. Unvalidated target/weak activity and the small non-randomized design are serious but secondary. Competitive/commercial viability is a real program-level risk, though somewhat outside the trial's internal mechanics.

**Uncertainties:** I do not have confirmed post-trial results, exact DLT rates, or the formal reason for discontinuation. Items where I am unsure are flagged rather than asserted.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE1
Conditions: Multiple Myeloma
Lead sponsor: Janssen Research & Development, LLC
Enrollment: 120
Design: allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=not specified

Brief summary:
The purpose of the study is to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety from the mixture of daratumumab and rHuPH20 prepared immediately before administration via Subcutaneous (SC) delivery (Part 1) and CF (co-formulated daratumumab and rHuPH20 preparation) administration via SC delivery of daratumumab (Part 2) and to evaluate the safety of Dara-CF 1800 milligram (mg) SC delivery without pre-dose and post-dose corticosteroids (Part 3). In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
This is an open-label (identity of assigned study drug will be known), multicenter, 3-part, Phase 1b dose escalation/expansion study to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics (study of what the body does to a drug), and antitumor activity of SC delivery of daratumumab to participant with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Up to approximately 53 participants in part 1, 80 participants in part 2 and 15 participants per corticosteroid tapering cohort (up to approximately 30 participants total) in Part 3 will be enrolled. The purpose of Part 1 is to select an appropriate SC therapeutic dose for the mixture of daratumumab with rHuPH20 based on safety and pharmacokinetics. This dose, selected from part 1 will be the initial dose for the co-formulated daratumumab and rHuPH20 preparation to be evaluated in Part 2. The purpose of Part 2 is to evaluate the SC delivery of CF and confirm the dose level selected from Part 1 based on the pharmacokinetics, safety, and antitumor activity. The purpose of Part 3 is to evaluate the safety of Dara-CF 1800 mg SC delivery without pre-dose and post-dose corticosteroids. Participant's safety will be monitored throughout the study.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 1: Cohort 1: Participants will receive 1200 mg (daratumumab 1200 milligram (mg) with Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase \[rHuPH20\] 30,000 U) via mixing immediately before Subcutaneous (SC) infusion once weekly in Cycles 1 (each cycle is 28 days) and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles until disease progression.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 1: Cohort 2: Participants will receive 1800 mg (daratumumab 1800 milligram (mg) with Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase \[rHuPH20\] 45,000 U) via mixing immediately before SC infusion once weekly in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles until disease progression.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 1: Cohort 3: Participants will receive mixture of daratumumab and rHuPH20 prepared immediately before administration via Subcutaneous (SC) delivery at a dose which will be decided by Study Evaluation Team (SET) once weekly by SC infusion in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles until disease progression. Also up to three additional optional cohorts (Cohorts 3b, 3c, and 3d) may be enrolled to repeat a dose level of daratumumab.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 2: Cohort 4: Participants will receive 1800 mg co-formulated daratumumab and rHuPH20 preparation initially administered by SC injection once weekly in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles. The dose level and schedule for any additional cohorts would be selected based on the daratumumab pharmacokinetic profile and safety profile (reviewed by the SET) that will be observed in Cohort 4.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 3: Dara-CF 1800 mg: Participants will receive co-formulated daratumumab 1800 mg and rHuPH20 preparation (Dara-CF) initially administered by SC injection once weekly in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles.

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Daratumumab Subcutaneous (SC) Administration: Participants will receive Daratumumab mixed with rHuPH20 in part 1 and co-formulated with rHuPH20 in part 2 and part 3 administered via SC administration once weekly in Cycles 1 (each cycle is 28 days) and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles.
  - [DRUG] Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase [rHuPH20]) SC Administration: Participants will receive Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase \[rHuPH20\]) mixed with Daratumumab in part 1 and co-formulated with Daratumumab in part 2 and part 3 administered as SC administration once weekly in Cycles 1 (each cycle is 28 days) and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles.

Primary outcomes:
  - Serum Trough Concentrations (Ctrough) of Daratumumab [time frame: Up to cycle 3 (each cycle 28 days) Day 1]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious AEs [time frame: Screening up to follow-up (30 days after last dose administration) (Approximately up to 3.4 years)]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Serum Concentration of Daratumumab and Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase (rHuPH20) (Plasma) Antibodies [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Percentage of Participants with Complete Response (CR) [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Percentage of Participants With Overall Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Duration of Response (DR) [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Time to Response [time frame: Approximately 2 years]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants proven to have multiple myeloma (MM) diagnosis according to the International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) diagnostic criteria
* Measurable disease as defined by any of the following: (a) immunoglobulin (Ig) G myeloma (serum monoclonal paraprotein \[M-protein\] level \>=1.0 gram/deciliter \[g/dL\] or urine M-protein level greater than or equal to (\>=) 200 milligram\[mg\]/24 hours\[hrs\]; or (b) IgA, IgD, or IgE multiple myeloma (serum M-protein level \>= 0.5 g/dL or urine M-protein level \>= 200 mg/24 hrs); or (c) light chain multiple myeloma (serum immunoglobulin free light chain \>=10 mg/dL and abnormal serum immunoglobulin kappa lambda free light chain ratio)
* Participant must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0, 1, or 2
* Pretreatment clinical laboratory values must meet protocol-defined parameters during the Screening phase
* Man, who is sexually active with a woman of child-bearing potential and has not had a vasectomy, must agree to use a barrier method of birth control example (eg), either condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository or partner with occlusive cap (diaphragm or cervical/vault caps) with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository, and all men must also not donate sperm during the study and for 3 months after receiving the final dose of study drug
* Relapsed or refractory disease. Relapse is defined as progression of disease after an initial response to previous treatment, more than 60 days after cessation of treatment. Refractory disease is defined as less than (\<) 25 percent (%) reduction in M-protein or progression of disease during treatment or within 60 days after cessation of treatment
* Prior treatment with less than or equal to (\>=) 2 treatment lines of anti-myeloma therapy. Prior lines of therapy must include a proteasome inhibitor (PI) (eg, bortezomib, carfilzomib) and an immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) (example, thalidomide, lenalidomide, pomalidomide) in any order during the course of treatment. Each prior line of therapy may consist of one or more agents and may include induction, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and/or maintenance therapy. Radiotherapy, bisphosphonates, or a single short course of steroids is not considered a prior line of therapy

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participant has received daratumumab or other anti-cluster of differentiation 38 (anti-CD38) therapies previously
* Participant has received anti-myeloma treatment within 2 weeks before Cycle 1 Day 1
* Participant has previously received an allogenic stem cell transplant; or participant has received autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) within 12 weeks before Cycle 1 Day 1
* Participant has a history of malignancy (other than multiple myeloma) within 5 years before Cycle 1 Day 1 (exceptions are squamous and basal cell carcinomas of the skin and carcinoma in situ of the cervix, or malignancy that in the opinion of the investigator, with concurrence with the sponsor's medical monitor, is considered cured with minimal risk of recurrence)
* Participant is exhibiting clinical signs of meningeal involvement of multiple myeloma

# Independent Knowledge: NCT02519452 (Daratumumab SC in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma)

Below is what I independently know beyond the registered specification provided. Where I am uncertain, I state "unknown."

## Drug Mechanism of Action

**Daratumumab** is a human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody that binds with high affinity to **CD38**, a transmembrane glycoprotein highly expressed on multiple myeloma cells and other cells (including NK cells, regulatory T cells, and some myeloid cells).

Its anti-myeloma effects are mediated through multiple mechanisms:

1. **Direct apoptosis** via cross-linking (Fc-dependent)
2. **Complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC)**
3. **Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC)**
4. **Antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP)**
5. **Immunomodulation** — depletion of CD38+ immunosuppressive cells (e.g., regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells), which may enhance T-cell-mediated anti-tumor responses

**rHuPH20** (recombinant human hyaluronidase) is an enzyme that transiently degrades hyaluronan in the subcutaneous extracellular matrix, increasing tissue permeability and enabling SC administration of larger volumes of biologics (e.g., daratumumab) that would otherwise require IV infusion. This is the same platform technology used in other SC antibody products (e.g., trastuzumab SC, rituximab SC).

## Sponsor Track Record

**Janssen Research & Development, LLC** (a Johnson & Johnson company) is the developer of daratumumab (trade name **DARZALEX**). Janssen has an extensive track record in multiple myeloma, including the development of:

- **Bortezomib (VELCADE)** — though this was originally Millennium/Takeda; Janssen acquired rights outside the US
- **Daratumumab (DARZALEX)** — approved IV formulation (2015) and SC formulation (2020)

Janssen has conducted numerous Phase 1–3 trials of daratumumab across the MM treatment landscape (monotherapy and combinations with lenalidomide, bortezomib, pomalidomide, carfilzomib, etc.).

## Results of Earlier Studies (Context Around This Trial)

- **GEN501** and **SIRIUS** were the pivotal Phase 1/2 studies of IV daratumumab monotherapy in relapsed/refractory MM, demonstrating single-agent activity and leading to accelerated approval.
- **The IV formulation** requires long infusion times (often 3–8 hours initially), which motivated development of the SC formulation.
- **The SC formulation** (daratumumab + rHuPH20, co-formulated as Dara-CF) was subsequently evaluated in the **COLUMBA** Phase 3 trial (NCT03277105), which demonstrated non-inferior pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and a lower rate of infusion-related reactions compared to IV daratumumab. This led to FDA approval of **DARZALEX FASPRO** (daratumumab and hyaluronidase-fihj) in **May 2020**.
- The safety signal noted in the registered summary — Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions in 4 of the first 20 subjects — was an early observation in the SC development program. This informed the subsequent use of pre-dose and post-dose corticosteroids in later cohorts and the eventual label for DARZALEX FASPRO.

## Key Dates

- **Study start date**: I believe this trial began around **2015**, but I am not certain of the exact month — **unknown** (likely September 2015 based on ClinicalTrials.gov records, but I cannot confirm independently).
- **Primary completion date**: **unknown**

- **DARZALEX FASPRO FDA approval**: **May 1, 2020** (based on the COLUMBA trial)
- **DARZALEX initial IV FDA approval**: **November 16, 2015**

## Other Independent Knowledge

- **rHuPH20** is licensed from **Halozyme Therapeutics** (the ENHANZE drug delivery platform). Janssen has a collaboration agreement with Halozyme for the SC daratumumab formulation.
- The **co-formulated** product (Dara-CF) is the actual commercial product (DARZALEX FASPRO), whereas the **mixing immediately before administration** approach (Part 1) was a bridging step to the co-formulated product.
- The **1800 mg SC dose** is the approved commercial dose of DARZALEX FASPRO for MM indications.
- **Part 3** of this trial (no pre-dose/post-dose corticosteroids) was designed to evaluate whether the corticosteroid regimen could be safely omitted — this is relevant because corticosteroids are used to mitigate infusion-related/hypersensitivity reactions but can be burdensome and cause side effects.
- The trial is **open-label**, which is typical for Phase 1b dose-finding studies.

## 1. Likely Primary Endpoint(s) and Measurement

The registered primary outcomes are:

- **Serum trough concentrations (Ctrough) of daratumumab** — measured up to Cycle 3 Day 1 (each cycle = 28 days)
- **Number of participants with AEs and SAEs** — from screening up to 30 days after last dose (~3.4 years)

**How success would be measured:**

- **Ctrough (pharmacokinetic endpoint)**: The goal in Part 1 was to identify an SC dose (1200 mg vs 1800 mg vs SET-selected dose) that achieves serum trough concentrations **comparable to or exceeding** the known efficacious IV daratumumab trough threshold. For IV daratumumab, the established target Ctrough is approximately **≥ 500 µg/mL** (a threshold derived from earlier IV monotherapy studies, particularly GEN501/SIRIUS exposure-response analyses). Success would mean the selected SC dose reliably produces Ctrough at or above this threshold in most patients. In effect, this is a **bridging PK endpoint**, not a direct efficacy endpoint.
- **Safety (AE/SAE endpoint)**: Success would mean an acceptable AE profile — specifically, no unexpected or unmanageable safety signal beyond what was already known for IV daratumumab, and manageable hypersensitivity/infusion-related reactions (relevant given the early Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity signal in 4 of the first 20 subjects). Tolerability of the SC injection itself (local reactions) would also be assessed.

**Secondary endpoints** (supportive of success, not primary):
- Anti-drug antibodies (ADA) to daratumumab and rHuPH20
- Complete response (CR) rate
- Overall response rate (ORR)
- Duration of response (DR)
- Time to response

---

## 2. Statistical Threshold

This is where I must be careful — **the exact statistical thresholds are unknown** to me from the registered summary, and Phase 1b dose-finding studies typically do not use formal hypothesis testing in the same way as Phase 3 trials.

What I can say with reasonable confidence:

- **No formal p-value threshold** is likely pre-specified as a primary success criterion for the PK endpoint. Instead, the criterion would be **descriptive/exposure-based**: e.g., the proportion of patients achieving Ctrough above a pre-specified target (likely ~500 µg/mL), or the geometric mean Ctrough falling within a pre-specified range relative to IV historical data.
- **Safety** would be judged by **descriptive statistics** (incidence, severity, relationship to drug), not a p-value.
- **Dose selection** (Part 1 → Part 2 bridging) would be a **Study Evaluation Team (SET) decision** based on PK, safety, and antitumor activity — not a formal statistical test.
- If any formal comparison were made, a **non-inferiority margin** for PK (e.g., the SC/IV geometric mean ratio of Ctrough falling within a pre-specified bound such as 0.8–1.25, a common PK equivalence window) would be the most plausible framework — but I cannot confirm this was pre-specified. **Unknown**.

For a Phase 1b study, "success" is therefore better framed as **"the selected SC dose is safe, tolerable, and achieves PK exposure consistent with the IV reference"** rather than "p < 0.05."

---

## 3. Superiority, Non-Inferiority, or Equivalence?

- This is **most likely a non-inferiority / PK-bridging design**, not a superiority trial. The intent is not to show SC is *better* than IV, but that SC achieves **comparable exposure and comparable efficacy** with a more convenient route.
- **Equivalence** is possible for the PK component (Ctrough within a pre-specified window), but the broader design language ("select an appropriate SC therapeutic dose," "confirm the dose level") suggests **non-inferiority-style bridging** rather than strict equivalence.
- **Superiority** is unlikely to be the primary framework. However, SC daratumumab was ultimately shown to have **superior convenience** (shorter administration time, fewer infusion-related reactions) — but that is a secondary/qualitative benefit, not the primary statistical claim.
- Given the absence of a randomized IV comparator arm in this registered design, formal non-inferiority testing against IV is **not possible within this trial alone**. The IV comparison would be **historical/external**. **Unknown** whether a formal pre-specified non-inferiority margin existed.

---

## 4. Key Design Features

From the registered specification:

| Feature | Value |
|---|---|
| **Allocation** | NON_RANDOMIZED |
| **Intervention model** | PARALLEL |
| **Masking** | NONE (open-label) |
| **Control arm** | None (no IV comparator arm; historical/external comparison only) |
| **Phase** | Phase 1 |
| **Enrollment** | 120 |

**Implications of these features:**

- **No randomization**: Participants are assigned to cohorts (Part 1: Cohorts 1, 2, 3/3b/3c/3d; Part 2: Cohort 4; Part 3: Dara-CF 1800 mg) sequentially, not by chance. This is typical of dose-escalation/expansion Phase 1 designs.
- **No blinding**: Open-label, as is standard for Phase 1 oncology studies where safety monitoring and dose decisions require knowledge of treatment.
- **No concurrent control arm**: Success is judged against **historical IV daratumumab data** (PK, safety, efficacy) and against pre-specified target thresholds — not against an internal control.
- **Parallel cohorts**: Cohorts run in parallel structurally, but they represent different dose levels/parts rather than randomized arms.
- **Parts 1–3 are sequential/adaptive**: Part 1 selects the SC dose; Part 2 confirms the co-formulated (CF) dose; Part 3 evaluates the CF 1800 mg dose without pre/post-dose corticosteroids. The SET reviews data between parts.

---

## Summary of What "Success" Would Look Like

| Dimension | Success Criterion |
|---|---|
| **PK (Ctrough)** | Selected SC dose achieves Ctrough at/below or comparable to IV reference (likely target ~500 µg/mL) in the majority of patients through Cycle 3 Day 1 |
| **Safety** | AE/SAE profile acceptable; hypersensitivity reactions manageable with prophylaxis; no new safety signal |
| **Dose selection** | SET confirms a dose for Part 2 (likely 1800 mg) based on PK + safety + antitumor activity |
| **Efficacy (secondary)** | ORR, CR, DR, time to response consistent with historical IV daratumumab monotherapy in R/R MM |
| **Immunogenicity (secondary)** | Low incidence of anti-daratumumab and anti-rHuPH20 antibodies |
| **Part 3** | Dara-CF 1800 mg SC is tolerable without pre/post-dose corticosteroids |

**Overall**: Success = **the SC route is shown to be a viable, safe, PK-comparable alternative to IV daratumumab**, enabling progression to the confirmatory Phase 3 COLUMBA trial. This is a **non-inferiority/PK-bridging** objective, assessed primarily by descriptive PK and safety statistics rather than a formal p-value threshold.

**Uncertainties**: The exact Ctrough target, any formal non-inferiority margin, and whether any pre-specified statistical hypothesis existed are **unknown** to me from the registered summary alone.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE3
Conditions: Synovial Sarcoma, Cancer, Soft Tissue Sarcoma, Sarcoma, Metastatic Sarcoma
Lead sponsor: Immune Design, a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc. (Rahway, New Jersey USA)
Enrollment: 1
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=QUADRUPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=12 Years; maximum age=not specified

Brief summary:
To assess if the CMB305 vaccine regimen may help the body's immune system to slow or stop the growth of synovial sarcoma tumor and improve survival. In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
The Synovate Study is a global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study in patients with unresectable, locally-advanced or metastatic New York esophageal squamous cell carcinoma 1 (NY-ESO-1) positive synovial sarcoma following first-line systemic anti-cancer therapy.

Arms:
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: A sequential regimen of LV305-matching placebo and G305-matching placebo.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] CMB305: A sequential regimen of LV305 and G305.

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] LV305: Administered via subcutaneous (SC) injection.
  - [BIOLOGICAL] G305: Administered via intramuscular (IM) injection.
  - [OTHER] LV305-matching placebo: Administered via SC injection.
  - [OTHER] G305-matching placebo: Administered via IM injection.

Primary outcomes:
  - Progression-Free Survival (PFS) [time frame: From randomization to investigator-determined date of disease progression or death, assessed up to 24 months.]
  - Overall Survival (OS) [time frame: From randomization to date of death, assessed up to 66 months.]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Time to Next Treatment (TTNT) [time frame: From last dose of CMB305 to initiation of new therapy, assessed up to 24 months.]
  - Distant Metastasis Free Survival (DMFS) [time frame: From randomization to investigator-determined date of disease progression or death, assessed up to 24 months.]
  - Overall Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: From randomization to investigator-determined date of disease progression, assessed up to 24 months.]
  - Number of Participants Who Experienced a Treatment-Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) [time frame: From randomization to investigator-determined date of disease progression or death, assessed up to approximately 2 months.]
  - Quality of Life (QoL): EuroQol 5-Dimension 5 Level (EQ-5D-5L) and EuroQol 5-Dimension Youth (EQ-5D-Y) Questionnaires [time frame: From Day 1 up to 12 months]
  - Number of Participants Who Discontinued Study Treatment Due to an AE [time frame: Up to approximately 2 months]

Eligibility criteria:
Selected Inclusion Criteria:

* Histological diagnosis of synovial sarcoma
* Immunohistochemistry (IHC) results from tumor biopsy for New York esophageal squamous cell carcinoma 1 (NY-ESO-1) are positive
* Participants have received at least 4 but no more than 8 cycles of first-line anthracycline or ifosfamide-containing systemic anti-cancer therapy regimen
* Must have documentation of no evidence of disease progression of the tumor during or after completion of first line systemic anti-cancer therapy
* ECOG (Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group) performance status of 0 or 1
* Age \>/= 12 years
* Life expectancy of at least 6 months

Selected Exclusion Criteria:

* Have received last dose of first-line systemic anti-cancer therapy or date of most recent local regional therapy \>28 days prior to day 1
* Have received prior anti-NY-ESO-1 therapy
* Have received first-line systemic anti-cancer therapy with an agent other than anthracycline or ifosfamide
* Have received treatment with systemic immunomodulatory agents within 28 days prior to administration of the first dose of CMB305, or 5 half-lives of the drug, whichever occurs sooner.
* Have significant immunosuppression from concurrent, recent, or anticipated need for chronic treatment with systemic immunosuppressive dose of corticosteroids or immunosuppressive medications.
* Have psychiatric or other medical illness, or any other condition that in the opinion of the investigator prevents compliance with the study procedures or ability to provide valid informed consent.
* Have history of uncontrolled autoimmune disease.
* Have a significant electrocardiogram finding or cardiovascular disease
* have inadequate organ function per protocol
* History of other cancer within 3 years
* Evidence of active tuberculosis or recent clinically-significant infection requiring systemic therapy.
* Evidence of active Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, or Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection
* Have a history of brain metastasis
* Have received cancer therapies including chemotherapy, radiation, biologic, or kinase inhibitors, granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF), or granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) within 3 weeks prior ot the first scheduled dose of CMB305
* Female of child bearing potential who is pregnant, is planning to become pregnant, or is breast feeding; or male who is sexually active with a female of child bearing potential who is planning to become pregnant.

Here is what I independently know about this trial and the drug, based on my training data. I'll flag uncertainty clearly.

**Mechanism of action (CMB305)**

CMB305 is a combination vaccine regimen consisting of two components:
- **LV305** — a lentiviral vector-based immunotherapeutic that delivers the NY-ESO-1 gene to dendritic cells, aiming to prime a NY-ESO-1-specific T-cell response.
- **G305** — a recombinant NY-ESO-1 protein formulated with GLA-SE (glucopyranosyl lipid adjuvant–stable emulsion), a TLR4 agonist, given as a boost to amplify the response.

The regimen is a "prime-boost" approach targeting the cancer-testis antigen NY-ESO-1, which is expressed in a high proportion of synovial sarcomas. The goal is to induce a tumor-specific cytotoxic T-cell response.

**Sponsor track record**

Immune Design was a Seattle-based immunotherapy company. Its lead programs included CMB305 and the GLA-adjuvant platform (GLA-SE). The company was acquired by Merck & Co. (Rahway, NJ) in 2019 — I believe the acquisition was announced around February 2019 and completed shortly after, which explains the "subsidiary of Merck & Co." designation in the registration. Immune Design had a partnership with Celldex and others around GLA. I am not fully certain of all pipeline details.

**Results of earlier studies**

Phase 1 data for CMB305 in NY-ESO-1+ cancers (including synovial sarcoma) were presented around 2016–2017 at ASCO/CTOS. Reported findings included that the regimen was generally tolerable and induced NY-ESO-1-specific immune responses in a subset of patients. A Phase 2 study in synovial sarcoma (sometimes referenced as the "CMB305-201" study) was conducted; I recall reported median PFS/OS figures but I am **not confident** in the exact numbers, so I will not state them. I do not reliably know the final results of this Phase 3 Synovate Study.

**Key dates**

- The clinicaltrials.gov record (NCT03520959) was registered around 2018.
- I am **unknown** on the exact start date, primary completion date, and whether the trial was completed, terminated, or halted early. I have a recollection that the Synovate Phase 3 study was **terminated/discontinued** — possibly after an interim analysis or strategic review following the Merck acquisition — but I am **not certain** of this and will not assert it as fact.

**A notable discrepancy I can flag**

The enrollment listed as "1" is clearly not the planned enrollment; Phase 3 sarcoma trials typically plan for well over 100 patients. This likely reflects a terminated/withdrawn trial where the registered number was updated to reflect actual enrollment. This is consistent with (but does not prove) my vague recollection that the study was stopped.

**Other items**

Here is what would constitute a successful outcome for NCT03520959, based strictly on the design details provided and standard Phase 3 oncology conventions. Where the registered specification does not give a specific parameter, I say "unknown" rather than invent a number.

**1. Primary endpoints and how they would be measured**

The registered primary outcomes are:
- **Progression-Free Survival (PFS)** — measured from randomization to investigator-determined date of disease progression (per RECIST 1.1, presumably, though the registry does not state the criteria) or death from any cause, whichever occurs first, assessed up to 24 months.
- **Overall Survival (OS)** — measured from randomization to date of death from any cause, assessed up to 66 months.

Success would mean demonstrating that CMB305 improves one (or both) of these versus placebo. Given the dual primary endpoint listing, the trial likely used a hierarchical or co-primary testing strategy — but the exact testing order and alpha allocation are **unknown** from the registration.

**2. Statistical threshold**

- The precise alpha, power, hazard ratio (HR) target, and number of events are **unknown** — the registry does not specify them.
- Conventionally, for a Phase 3 superiority trial with PFS/OS primary endpoints, success requires a **statistically significant difference favoring CMB305 at a two-sided alpha of 0.05 (or one-sided 0.025)**, with an observed **HR below the pre-specified target** (often around 0.70–0.75 for sarcoma PFS trials, but this specific target is **unknown** here).
- A stratified log-rank test and Cox proportional hazards model would typically be used, with a pre-specified interim analysis (likely for futility and/or efficacy, given the Phase 3 design). Whether such interim analyses existed and their boundaries are **unknown**.

**3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence**

- This is almost certainly a **superiority** trial. The design (placebo comparator, experimental vaccine regimen, stated goals of "slow or stop growth" and "improve survival") and the standard paradigm for adding an active immunotherapy to a post-first-line setting indicate superiority testing, not non-inferiority or equivalence.
- A non-inferiority design would be unusual here because the placebo arm is not an established active standard being challenged. So: **superiority** — but I note the registry does not explicitly state the hypothesis type, so this is an inference from design.

**4. Key design features**

- **Randomization:** Yes — allocation = RANDOMIZED. The exact ratio (e.g., 2:1 vs 1:1) is **unknown** from the provided text.
- **Intervention model:** PARALLEL — two independent arms.
- **Blinding/masking:** QUADRUPLE — typically participant, care provider, investigator, and outcomes assessor are masked. This is consistent with a double-blind, placebo-controlled design (the detailed description calls it "double-blind," while the registry field says quadruple — a minor discrepancy, but both indicate strong masking).
- **Control arm:** Placebo comparator — matching placebos for both LV305 (SC) and G305 (IM), so the placebo arm mirrors the two-component sequential regimen.
- **Experimental arm:** CMB305 — sequential LV305 (SC) + G305 (IM).
- **Population:** NY-ESO-1-positive synovial sarcoma, unresectable/locally advanced or metastatic, after first-line anthracycline- or ifosfamide-containing therapy, with no evidence of progression at baseline; ECOG 0–1; age ≥12; life expectancy ≥6 months.
- **Stratification factors:** **unknown** (the registry text provided does not list them).
- **Sample size:** The registered enrollment of "1" is not the planned size and is inconsistent with a Phase 3 design — **unknown** what the planned accrual was, though a Phase 3 sarcoma trial would typically target well over 100 patients.

**Bottom line on what "success" would look like**

A successful outcome would be a pre-specified, statistically significant improvement in PFS and/or OS for CMB305 versus placebo in the ITT (or co-primary) population, with an acceptable safety profile (notably, no excess of the Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions flagged in the safety cohort) and no detriment to quality-of-life measures. The exact HR, alpha, power, and event targets required to declare success are **unknown** from the information provided.

Here are the key risk factors that could cause NCT03520959 to fail, ordered from most to least concerning, with each grounded in the specific design and details of this trial.

---

**RISK 1: Efficacy failure of the vaccine mechanism in an advanced/metastatic setting**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** CMB305 is a therapeutic cancer vaccine (LV305 prime + G305 boost) designed to induce NY-ESO-1-specific T-cell responses. Therapeutic vaccines have a historically poor record in advanced/metastatic solid tumors, and this trial enrolls patients with unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic synovial sarcoma — a setting with high tumor burden and immunosuppressive microenvironment. Even if the vaccine induces immune responses (as reported in earlier-phase studies), converting those into a PFS/OS benefit over placebo is the central and hardest hurdle. The dual PFS/OS primary endpoints mean the trial must show a clinically meaningful and statistically significant benefit, not just immunogenicity.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

**RISK 2: Safety signal — hypersensitivity reactions requiring treatment interruption**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The brief summary explicitly states that in the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects (20%) experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption. A 20% rate of Grade 2–3 reactions in a small cohort is a substantial signal. In a larger Phase 3 population — including adolescents (age ≥12) and patients with cardiovascular disease exclusions — this could manifest as more frequent or more severe events, dose interruptions, discontinuations, or an unfavorable risk-benefit assessment. This could undermine both the safety endpoint and the ability to deliver the full intended regimen, thereby diluting efficacy.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

**RISK 3: Enrollment and feasibility failure**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registered enrollment is "1," which is clearly not a planned Phase 3 accrual and strongly suggests the trial was not able to enroll, was stopped early, or was withdrawn/terminated. The eligibility criteria are highly restrictive: NY-ESO-1-positive (only a subset of synovial sarcoma patients), specifically after 4–8 cycles of first-line anthracycline- or ifosfamide-based therapy, with documented no evidence of progression, ECOG 0–1, and multiple exclusions (autoimmune disease, brain metastases, prior anti-NY-ESO-1 therapy, etc.). Synovial sarcoma is a rare disease, and the combination of a rare tumor plus a biomarker restriction plus a narrow post-first-line window makes accrual extremely difficult. This is a classic cause of Phase 3 failure independent of drug activity.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

**RISK 4: Trial design limitations — endpoint sensitivity and rarity of events**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The primary endpoints are PFS and OS, both event-driven and requiring a sufficient number of progression/death events to reach statistical power. In a rare disease with a narrow post-first-line, non-progressing population — and possibly a slow event rate if the vaccine has modest activity — reaching the pre-specified event target could take a long time (OS assessed up to 66 months) or never occur, leading to futility. Additionally, "investigator-determined" PFS introduces assessment variability and potential bias, though quadruple masking mitigates this. The placeholder enrollment ("1") and lack of a stated planned sample size in the registration further suggest design execution problems.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

**RISK 5: Regulatory and competitive landscape risk**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** Immune Design was acquired by Merck & Co. (Rahway, NJ) in 2019, and the trial is now sponsored by a subsidiary. Post-acquisition, programs are frequently reprioritized, and a vaccine program in a rare sarcoma with a complex, slow endpoint may be deprioritized in favor of more promising assets. Competitively, engineered T-cell therapies targeting NY-ESO-1 (Adaptimmune/GSK letetresgene autoleucel, and MAGE-A4-directed afami-cel) and other sarcoma immunotherapies were advancing in the same space, potentially making CMB305 less attractive scientifically or commercially. A shifting regulatory or competitive environment could lead to early termination or a decision not to pursue approval even if some activity is observed.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

**Summary ordering**

1. Efficacy failure (HIGH)
2. Safety signal — hypersensitivity (HIGH)
3. Enrollment/feasibility failure (HIGH)
4. Design/endpoint limitations (MEDIUM)
5. Regulatory/competitive risk (MEDIUM)

The first three are tightly linked: a vaccine in a hard-to-treat metastatic setting with a notable safety signal and a very narrow eligible population is at high risk on efficacy, safety, and accrual simultaneously. The registered enrollment of "1" is the single most concrete indicator that at least one of these (or a combination) manifested in practice, though I cannot state with certainty from the registration alone which one.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE1
Conditions: Solid Tumors
Lead sponsor: Shanghai Junshi Bioscience Co., Ltd.
Enrollment: 24
Design: allocation=NA; intervention model=SINGLE_GROUP; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerance and Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT) of Recombinant humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (JS001) in patients with advanced solid tumors. In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
OVERVIEW

This is a Phase 1, open-label, dose-escalation study of JS-001, a humanized monoclonal IgG4 antibody targeting the Programmed Death -1 (PD-1). It is estimated that 12-24 subjects with advanced or recurrent solid tumors or will be enrolled in the study.

A 3+3 design will be utilized for this Phase 1 study. Four dose levels are planned and include: 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg/dose. Each of the 4 dose levels will use 2 dose schedules: single dose, repeated doses every 2 weeks. Subjects will be assigned to a dose schedule in the order of study entry.

The study will be the traditional 3 + 3 design with 3 or 6 subjects treated at this dose level and at all subsequent dose levels depending upon the incidence of DLTs. If no DLTs occur in a cohort of 3 subjects, a new cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 1 of 3 subjects in a cohort experiences a DLT, that cohort will be expanded to 6 subjects. If only 1 of the 6 subjects has a DLT, then the next cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 2 or more DLTs occur within a cohort, then that dose level will be above the MTD (the highest dose where no more than 1 of 6 subjects has experienced a DLT), and the previous lower (tolerated) dose level will be considered the MTD.

A DLT is defined as a Grade 3 drug-related adverse event occurring within the first cycle (28 days) of dosing (excluding tumor flare defined as local pain, irritation, or rash localized at sites of known or suspected tumor or a transient Grade 3 infusion adverse event) using National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 in a single dose cohort.

Tumor response will be evaluated using immune-related response criteria (irRC), WHO criteria , Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), immune-related RECIST, and International Workshop to Standardize Response Criteria for non-Hodgkin's Lymphomas (for lymphomas only).

In the absence of confirmed disease progression and intolerable toxicities, subjects in the single dose cohorts and multiple dose cohorts will be allowed to continue JS-001 administration with the consent of the subject.

DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION

JS-001 will be administered as a 60-minute i.v. infusion. Cohorts will include escalating dose levels of 0.3, 1, 3, 10mg/kg/dose.

SAFETY EVALUATIONS

Assessment of safety will be determined by vital sign measurements, clinical laboratory tests, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status evaluations, diagnostic imaging, physical examinations, electrocardiograms, and the incidence and severity of adverse events.

Safety will also include evaluations of immune safety and immunogenicity. Particular attention will be given to adverse events that may follow enhanced T-cell activation such as dermatitis and colitis, uveitis, or other immune-related adverse events (irAEs).

An irAE is a clinically significant adverse event of any organ that is associated with drug exposure, of unknown etiology, and is consistent with an immune-mediated mechanism.

EFFICACY EVALUATIONS

The primary efficacy endpoint is the best response rate (RR). Duration of response, progression-free survival, time to progression, and overall survival will also be analyzed.

PHARMACOKINETIC EVALUATIONS

Pharmacokinetic parameters include AUC, Cmax, tmax, and t½, etc. STATISTICAL METHODS The sample size for this study is not determined from power analysis. It is based on the 3+3 design for dose escalation and safety evaluation requirements.

Descriptive statistics will include: mean, standard deviation, median, and minimum and maximum values for continuous variables; frequencies and percentages for categorical variables.

The efficacy parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics. All safety and pharmacokinetic parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody toripalimab: humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody is to be injected intravenously 0.3mg/kg or 1mg/kg or 3mg/kg or 10mg/kg until disease progresses or unacceptable tolerability occurs.

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody toripalimab: humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (JS001) is a programmed death-1 (PD-1) immune checkpoint inhibitor antibody, which selectively interferes with the combination of PD-1 with its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, resulting in the activation of lymphocytes and elimination of malignancy theoretically.

Primary outcomes:
  - Number of Participants With Abnormal Laboratory Values and/or Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Anti-Drug Antibody of JS001 in Chinese patients [time frame: Cycle 1,2,3,5 Day 1 before JS001 infusion and 336 hours after last JS001 infusion, each cycle is 28 days.]
  - Objective Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Duration of Response (DOR) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Progression-Free survival (PFS) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Overall Survival (OS) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - DLT in patients with solid tumor treated with JS001. [time frame: Cycle 1（each cycle is 28 days）]
  - PD-1 receptor occupancy of blood [time frame: 1 year]
  - Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody (mAb) [time frame: 1 year]
  - Peak Time (Tmax) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Area Under the Curve (AUC) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb Area Under the Curve [AUC]). Area Under the Curve (AUC) after single dose injection of Recombinant Humanized Anti-PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody [time frame: 1 year]
  - t1/2 after single dose injection of Recombinant Humanized Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Plasma clearance (CL) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Apparent volume of distribution (V) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Minimum Plasma Concentration (Cmin) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Average Plasma Concentration (Cav) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Degree of fluctuation (DF) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Apparent volume of distribution of steady state (Vss) after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Histological or cytological diagnosis of advanced or recurrent adenocarcinoma of solid tumor, including adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastro-esophageal junction, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, Pancreatic ductal cell carcinoma, etc.

   * at least one prior chemotherapy regimen
   * age between 18 and 75 years, both gender
   * has at least one measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST V1.1)
2. life expectancy ≥ 3 months
3. ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
4. Has had last dose of chemotherapy more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001, and has recovered to National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 Grade 1 or better from the AEs due to the chemotherapy.
5. Has had last administration of radioactive therapy more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
6. Has had last administration of immunosuppressive systemic steroid therapy (more than 10 mg/d prednisone or equal dose) more than 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
7. Has undergone major surgery that needs general anesthesia more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001. Has undergone surgery that needs local anesthesia or epidural anesthesia more than 72 hours prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001 and has already recovered from the surgery. Has undergone biopsy more than 1 hour prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
8. The lab examination results of the screening must fulfill all of the following:

   * absolute neutrophil count more than or equal to 1.5×109/ L
   * platelet count more than or equal to 90×109/ L
   * hemoglobin more than or equal to 90 g/L
   * creatinine less than or equal to132.6µmol/L or creatinine clearance \>40 mL/min
   * aspartate transferase(AST) and alanine transferase(ALT) less than or equal to 3.0 ×ULN
   * total bilirubin less than or equal to 1.5×ULN( except for the patients with Gilbert syndrome, whose total bilirubin ,must less than or equal to 51.3µmol/L)
9. Patient has been informed about the nature of the study, and has agreed to participate in the study, and signed the Informed Consent Form prior to participation in any study related activities.
10. Able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Has had antineoplastic herbal therapy within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
2. Is currently participating and receiving study therapy or has participated in a study of an investigational agent and receive study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug.
3. Has a medical condition that requires chronic systemic steroid therapy or on any other form of immunosuppressive medication.
4. Has a known history of a hematologic malignancy, primary brain tumor or sarcoma, or of another primary solid tumor, unless the participant has undergone potentially curative therapy with no evidence of that disease for 5 years.
5. Has known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
6. Has interstitial lung disease OR has had a history of pneumonitis that has required oral or IV steroids.
7. Has active or suspected autoimmune disease except leukoderma,type I Diabetes, Residual hypothyroidism that induced by autoimmune thyroiditis and only requires the use of hormone replacement therapy, Or disease that rarely relapse without external stimulating factors.
8. Had prior treatment targeting PD-1: anti-PD-1,anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein (CTLA), or other antibodies that targeting T cell costimulatory pathway or checkpoint.
9. Has an active infection requiring systematic therapy.
10. Is positive for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
11. Has active Tuberculosis.
12. Has known active Hepatitis B or C.
13. Has known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the study.
14. Has received or will receive a live vaccine within 30 days prior to the first administration of study drug.
15. Is pregnant or breastfeeding.
16. Cannot tolerate vein puncture and / or venous access.
17. Any other conclusive medical reasons, mental illness, and / or social reasons that determined by the investigators.

This is a judgment estimate, not a precisely derived figure, and reasonable analysts could put it anywhere from ~5% to ~20% depending on how heavily they weight the class effect.

# Success Criteria for NCT02857166

## 1. Likely Primary Endpoint(s) and Measurement

From the registration text, this is a **Phase 1 dose-escalation study**. The stated primary outcome is:

- **Number of Participants With Abnormal Laboratory Values and/or Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment** (time frame: up to ~2 years).

In practice, for a Phase 1 oncology study using a 3+3 design, the true operational primary objectives are:

- **Determination of the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD)** — the highest dose at which no more than 1 of 6 subjects experiences a DLT.
- **Characterization of the DLT profile** — DLT defined as a Grade 3 drug-related AE within the first 28-day cycle (excluding tumor flare and transient Grade 3 infusion reactions), per CTCAE v4.0.
- **Safety and tolerability** — incidence, severity, and relationship of AEs, including immune-related AEs (irAEs).
- **Pharmacokinetics** — AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t½, CL, V, and steady-state parameters (Cmin, Cav, DF, Vss) after single and multiple dosing.

**Measurement:** Safety by vital signs, labs, ECOG status, ECG, imaging, physical exams, and AE grading. PK by serial blood sampling. Tumor response (a secondary/exploratory aim) by irRC, WHO criteria, RECIST, irRECIST, and lymphoma-specific criteria. ORR, DOR, PFS, and OS are listed as **secondary** outcomes, not primary.

## 2. Statistical Threshold

- **No formal hypothesis test is specified.** The registration explicitly states: "The sample size for this study is not determined from power analysis. It is based on the 3+3 design for dose escalation and safety evaluation requirements."
- All endpoints are summarized with **descriptive statistics** (mean, SD, median, min/max for continuous; frequencies/percentages for categorical).
- Therefore there is **no p-value threshold, no hazard ratio target, and no non-inferiority margin** built into the design. Any such threshold would be **unknown** / not applicable.

## 3. Trial Type: Superiority, Non-Inferiority, or Equivalence

- **None of the above, in the strict inferential sense.** This is a **single-arm, open-label, dose-escalation (3+3) study** with no formal comparative hypothesis.
- If one insists on labeling it, it is closest to a **single-arm exploratory/safety study** — not a superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence trial. No control arm is used for formal statistical comparison.

## 4. Key Design Features

From the registration and standard 3+3 practice:

- **Allocation:** NA (non-randomized).
- **Intervention model:** Single group (sequential dose cohorts).
- **Masking:** None (open-label).
- **Control arm:** None.
- **Dose levels:** 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg/dose.
- **Schedules:** Single dose; and repeated dosing every 2 weeks.
- **Escalation rule:** 3+3 — 3 subjects per cohort; expand to 6 if 1 DLT; escalate if 0/3 or 1/6 DLT; stop escalation and declare prior dose the MTD if ≥2 DLTs in a cohort.
- **Enrollment:** 12–24 subjects (estimated).
- **Population:** Advanced/recurrent solid tumors (gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, esophageal SCC, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic ductal carcinoma, etc.), ≥1 prior chemotherapy, age 18–75, ECOG 0–1, ≥1 measurable lesion by RECIST v1.1.
- **Treatment duration:** Continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

## What Would Constitute a "Successful Outcome"

Operationally, for this design:

1. **Safety/tolerability success:** Identification of a tolerable MTD (or recommended Phase 2 dose) with an acceptable DLT rate, manageable irAEs, and no unexpected safety signal that halts development. The reported hypersensitivity signal (4/20 Grade 2–3 reactions) would be a concern, but success could still be declared if the reactions were manageable and did not preclude dose escalation.
2. **PK success:** Dose-proportional or otherwise interpretable PK, measurable PD-1 receptor occupancy, and acceptable immunogenicity (low anti-drug antibody incidence).
3. **Preliminary efficacy signal (exploratory):** Objective responses observed by RECIST/irRC — even a modest ORR in a refractory population would support further development.
4. **Go/no-go decision:** Advancement to Phase 2/registrational studies in one or more of the enrolled tumor types.

## Caveats

- The exact DLT rate threshold deemed "acceptable," the target ORR for a go decision, and any formal statistical criteria for future studies are **unknown** from the registration text and would typically be pre-specified in the protocol or in a later Phase 2 design, not in this Phase 1.
- Whether the trial formally declared an MTD, and what that MTD was, is **unknown** to me from independent sources.

# Key Risk Factors for NCT02857166

---

## RISK 1: Hypersensitivity / Infusion Reactions

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registration text itself reports that **4 of the first 20 dosed subjects** experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption. This is a **20% incidence of clinically significant infusion reactions** in a Phase 1 safety cohort — well above what is typically seen with anti-PD-1 IgG4 antibodies. If the reactions are severe, recurrent, or not mitigated by premedication, slower infusion, or dose modification, they could halt dose escalation, prevent determination of an MTD, trigger early termination, or force a formulation change. This is the single most concrete, trial-specific risk because it is already observed in the data.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH

---

## RISK 2: Failure to Establish a Tolerable MTD / DLT Stopping Rule Triggered

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The 3+3 design mandates that **if ≥2 DLTs occur in a cohort, that dose level exceeds the MTD** and the prior dose becomes the MTD. With only 4 planned dose levels (0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg) and two schedules (single and q2w), a DLT cluster at the 3 or 10 mg/kg level — whether driven by the hypersensitivity signal, irAEs (colitis, dermatitis, uveitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis), or other Grade 3 events — would truncate escalation and cap the achievable dose. Monotherapy anti-PD-1 activity in solid tumors is generally dose-dependent up to a plateau, so failing to reach an effective dose could undermine the efficacy signal and the go/no-go decision for Phase 2. With only 3–6 subjects per cohort, DLT rate estimates are also highly imprecise, creating risk of both false stopping and false escalation.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM-HIGH (directly coupled to Risk 1 and to class-typical irAEs)

---

## RISK 3: Weak or Absent Efficacy Signal in a Heavily Pretreated Population

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The eligibility criteria require **advanced or recurrent solid tumors with ≥1 prior chemotherapy regimen**, including tumor types (gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, esophageal SCC, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic ductal carcinoma) that are generally **less PD-1-responsive** than melanoma, NSCLC, or urothelial carcinoma. Monotherapy PD-1 blockade in later-line gastric, pancreatic, and cholangiocarcinoma has historically produced low objective response rates (often single-digit to low-double-digit percentages). If this dose-escalation study produces few or no objective responses, the program may lack a compelling efficacy rationale to advance, even if safety is acceptable. The sample size (12–24) is also far too small to distinguish a true low response rate from noise.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

## RISK 4: Slow Enrollment or High Screen-Failure Rate

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The eligible population is narrow: specific adenocarcinoma/SCC subtypes, ≥1 prior chemo, measurable disease by RECIST v1.1, ECOG 0–1, no prior PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 therapy, no active autoimmune disease, no interstitial lung disease, adequate organ function, and age 18–75. These restrictions — plus the fact that anti-PD-1 competition was intensifying in China around 2016–2018 — could slow accrual. A Phase 1 with 12–24 subjects across 4 dose levels and 2 schedules requires each subject to be followed for at least 28 days for DLT assessment, so enrollment delays directly extend timelines and increase the chance of the program being overtaken by competitors or of the trial being terminated for futility/administrative reasons.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM

---

## RISK 5: Competitive / Regulatory Landscape and Design Limitations

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** By the time this trial was running, multiple anti-PD-1 antibodies were already approved or in late-stage development globally (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) and in China (toripalimab's own competitors, e.g., camrelizumab and sintilimab). A first-in-China PD-1 monotherapy in less-responsive solid tumors faced a crowded field. Regulatory expectations for accelerated approval in China were shifting toward requiring randomized, often chemotherapy-controlled, evidence — which a small single-arm Phase 1 cannot provide. The trial's design (single-arm, open-label, no control, descriptive statistics only, no formal efficacy hypothesis) means it **cannot by itself support registration**; it can only inform a go/no-go decision. If the sponsor's regulatory strategy required comparative data, this trial's output would be insufficient regardless of its internal success. There is also no formal interim futility rule described, so resources could be expended without an early exit.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM (for the design-limitation and competitive components); the regulatory component is context-dependent and partly **unknown** in its specific impact on this program

---

|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hypersensitivity / infusion reactions | HIGH |
| 2 | Failure to establish tolerable MTD / DLT stopping triggered | MEDIUM-HIGH |
| 3 | Weak efficacy signal in pretreated, less-responsive tumors | MEDIUM |
| 4 | Slow enrollment / high screen-failure | MEDIUM |
| 5 | Competitive landscape / design cannot support registration | MEDIUM |

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH)
Lead sponsor: Corcept Therapeutics
Enrollment: 12
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=TRIPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
This phase 2, double blind, placebo-controlled, randomized study is to assess the safety and efficacy of miricorilant (CORT118335) in patients with presumed Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH). In the preceding safety cohort, 4 of the first 20 dosed subjects experienced Grade 2–3 hypersensitivity reactions (hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria) temporally associated with drug administration, requiring treatment interruption.

Detailed description:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study that assessed the safety efficacy and pharmacokinetics (PK) of miricorilant in patients with presumed Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH). Patients who meet the criteria for Study CORT118335-860 were randomized on Day 1 to receive 900 mg miricorilant, 600 mg miricorilant, or placebo for 12 weeks.

Due to observations related to safety, the study was terminated prior to completion and study objectives, endpoints, and procedures were modified as specified in the protocol.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Miricorilant- 900 mg: Participants received 900 mg miricorilant (6 miricorilant tablets of 150 mg) orally once daily.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Miricorilant- 600 mg: Participants received 600 mg miricorilant (4 miricorilant tablets of 150 mg and 2 placebo tablets) orally once daily.
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: Participants received 6 placebo tablets orally once daily.

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Miricorilant: Tablets taken orally
  - [DRUG] Placebo: Placebo tablets

Primary outcomes:
  - Relative Change From Baseline in Liver Fat Content Assessed by Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Proton Density Fat Fraction [time frame: Baseline and up to ~Day 95]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Number of Participants Achieving a Relative Reduction From Baseline in LFC of ≥30% by MRI-PDFF [time frame: Baseline and up to ~Day 95]
  - Change From Baseline in Aspartate Aminotransferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Alanine Aminotransferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Gamma-glutamyl Transferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Propeptide of Type III Collagen [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Enhanced Liver Fibrosis Score [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Have a diagnosis of NASH based on a biopsy obtained within the last year OR
* Have a diagnosis of presumed NASH based on blood tests and scans

Exclusion Criteria:

* Have participated in another clinical trial within the last year and received active treatment for NASH
* Have participated in another clinical trial for any other indication within the last 3 months
* Are pregnant or lactating women
* Have a BMI \<18 kg/m\^2
* Have had liver transplantation or plan to have liver transplantation during the study
* Have type 1 diabetes or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.
