data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE1
Conditions: Multiple Myeloma
Lead sponsor: Janssen Research & Development, LLC
Enrollment: 120
Design: allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=not specified

Brief summary:
The purpose of the study is to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety from the mixture of daratumumab and rHuPH20 prepared immediately before administration via Subcutaneous (SC) delivery (Part 1) and CF (co-formulated daratumumab and rHuPH20 preparation) administration via SC delivery of daratumumab (Part 2) and to evaluate the safety of Dara-CF 1800 milligram (mg) SC delivery without pre-dose and post-dose corticosteroids (Part 3). Since this trial's initiation, a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval, establishing a new standard of care and potentially affecting the clinical relevance of the study's primary endpoint and recruitment feasibility.

Detailed description:
This is an open-label (identity of assigned study drug will be known), multicenter, 3-part, Phase 1b dose escalation/expansion study to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics (study of what the body does to a drug), and antitumor activity of SC delivery of daratumumab to participant with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Up to approximately 53 participants in part 1, 80 participants in part 2 and 15 participants per corticosteroid tapering cohort (up to approximately 30 participants total) in Part 3 will be enrolled. The purpose of Part 1 is to select an appropriate SC therapeutic dose for the mixture of daratumumab with rHuPH20 based on safety and pharmacokinetics. This dose, selected from part 1 will be the initial dose for the co-formulated daratumumab and rHuPH20 preparation to be evaluated in Part 2. The purpose of Part 2 is to evaluate the SC delivery of CF and confirm the dose level selected from Part 1 based on the pharmacokinetics, safety, and antitumor activity. The purpose of Part 3 is to evaluate the safety of Dara-CF 1800 mg SC delivery without pre-dose and post-dose corticosteroids. Participant's safety will be monitored throughout the study.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 1: Cohort 1: Participants will receive 1200 mg (daratumumab 1200 milligram (mg) with Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase \[rHuPH20\] 30,000 U) via mixing immediately before Subcutaneous (SC) infusion once weekly in Cycles 1 (each cycle is 28 days) and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles until disease progression.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 1: Cohort 2: Participants will receive 1800 mg (daratumumab 1800 milligram (mg) with Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase \[rHuPH20\] 45,000 U) via mixing immediately before SC infusion once weekly in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles until disease progression.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 1: Cohort 3: Participants will receive mixture of daratumumab and rHuPH20 prepared immediately before administration via Subcutaneous (SC) delivery at a dose which will be decided by Study Evaluation Team (SET) once weekly by SC infusion in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles until disease progression. Also up to three additional optional cohorts (Cohorts 3b, 3c, and 3d) may be enrolled to repeat a dose level of daratumumab.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 2: Cohort 4: Participants will receive 1800 mg co-formulated daratumumab and rHuPH20 preparation initially administered by SC injection once weekly in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles. The dose level and schedule for any additional cohorts would be selected based on the daratumumab pharmacokinetic profile and safety profile (reviewed by the SET) that will be observed in Cohort 4.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Part 3: Dara-CF 1800 mg: Participants will receive co-formulated daratumumab 1800 mg and rHuPH20 preparation (Dara-CF) initially administered by SC injection once weekly in Cycles 1 and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and then every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles.

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Daratumumab Subcutaneous (SC) Administration: Participants will receive Daratumumab mixed with rHuPH20 in part 1 and co-formulated with rHuPH20 in part 2 and part 3 administered via SC administration once weekly in Cycles 1 (each cycle is 28 days) and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles.
  - [DRUG] Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase [rHuPH20]) SC Administration: Participants will receive Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase \[rHuPH20\]) mixed with Daratumumab in part 1 and co-formulated with Daratumumab in part 2 and part 3 administered as SC administration once weekly in Cycles 1 (each cycle is 28 days) and 2, every 2 weeks in Cycles 3-6, and every 4 weeks in subsequent cycles.

Primary outcomes:
  - Serum Trough Concentrations (Ctrough) of Daratumumab [time frame: Up to cycle 3 (each cycle 28 days) Day 1]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Number of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious AEs [time frame: Screening up to follow-up (30 days after last dose administration) (Approximately up to 3.4 years)]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Serum Concentration of Daratumumab and Recombinant Human Hyaluronidase (rHuPH20) (Plasma) Antibodies [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Percentage of Participants with Complete Response (CR) [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Percentage of Participants With Overall Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Duration of Response (DR) [time frame: Approximately 2 years]
  - Part 1, 2 and 3: Time to Response [time frame: Approximately 2 years]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants proven to have multiple myeloma (MM) diagnosis according to the International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) diagnostic criteria
* Measurable disease as defined by any of the following: (a) immunoglobulin (Ig) G myeloma (serum monoclonal paraprotein \[M-protein\] level \>=1.0 gram/deciliter \[g/dL\] or urine M-protein level greater than or equal to (\>=) 200 milligram\[mg\]/24 hours\[hrs\]; or (b) IgA, IgD, or IgE multiple myeloma (serum M-protein level \>= 0.5 g/dL or urine M-protein level \>= 200 mg/24 hrs); or (c) light chain multiple myeloma (serum immunoglobulin free light chain \>=10 mg/dL and abnormal serum immunoglobulin kappa lambda free light chain ratio)
* Participant must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0, 1, or 2
* Pretreatment clinical laboratory values must meet protocol-defined parameters during the Screening phase
* Man, who is sexually active with a woman of child-bearing potential and has not had a vasectomy, must agree to use a barrier method of birth control example (eg), either condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository or partner with occlusive cap (diaphragm or cervical/vault caps) with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository, and all men must also not donate sperm during the study and for 3 months after receiving the final dose of study drug
* Relapsed or refractory disease. Relapse is defined as progression of disease after an initial response to previous treatment, more than 60 days after cessation of treatment. Refractory disease is defined as less than (\<) 25 percent (%) reduction in M-protein or progression of disease during treatment or within 60 days after cessation of treatment
* Prior treatment with less than or equal to (\>=) 2 treatment lines of anti-myeloma therapy. Prior lines of therapy must include a proteasome inhibitor (PI) (eg, bortezomib, carfilzomib) and an immunomodulatory drug (IMiD) (example, thalidomide, lenalidomide, pomalidomide) in any order during the course of treatment. Each prior line of therapy may consist of one or more agents and may include induction, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and/or maintenance therapy. Radiotherapy, bisphosphonates, or a single short course of steroids is not considered a prior line of therapy

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participant has received daratumumab or other anti-cluster of differentiation 38 (anti-CD38) therapies previously
* Participant has received anti-myeloma treatment within 2 weeks before Cycle 1 Day 1
* Participant has previously received an allogenic stem cell transplant; or participant has received autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) within 12 weeks before Cycle 1 Day 1
* Participant has a history of malignancy (other than multiple myeloma) within 5 years before Cycle 1 Day 1 (exceptions are squamous and basal cell carcinomas of the skin and carcinoma in situ of the cervix, or malignancy that in the opinion of the investigator, with concurrence with the sponsor's medical monitor, is considered cured with minimal risk of recurrence)
* Participant is exhibiting clinical signs of meningeal involvement of multiple myeloma

Here is what I independently know about this trial and its drug, with uncertainty flagged where appropriate.

## Daratumumab — mechanism of action

Daratumumab (Darzalex) is a human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody targeting **CD38**, a transmembrane glycoprotein highly expressed on multiple myeloma cells and also present on some other lymphoid and myeloid cells and on some non-hematopoietic tissues. Its mechanisms include:

- **Direct apoptosis** via Fc-dependent cross-linking and other signaling effects.
- **Complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC)**.
- **Antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC)** and **antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP)**.
- **Immunomodulation** — reduction of CD38-positive regulatory T cells, B cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, which may enhance T-cell responses.

Recombinant human hyaluronidase (rHuPH20, the same enzyme component used in products like Herceptin SC and Rituxan Hycela) transiently degrades hyaluronan in the subcutaneous space, increasing tissue permeability and enabling large-volume SC administration of a biologic that would otherwise require IV infusion.

## Sponsor track record

Janssen Research & Development (Johnson & Johnson) developed daratumumab and holds the originator rights. Janssen has a very large oncology/hematology portfolio and is the sponsor of the pivotal daratumumab program in multiple myeloma (e.g., GEN501, SIRIUS, CASTOR, POLLUX, MAIA, ALCYONE, APOLLO, CANDOR, and the COLUMBA study of SC daratumumab). Janssen's track record in myeloma is well established. Beyond this, specific information about the internal conduct or quality metrics of NCT02519452 is **unknown** to me.

## Earlier studies / prior results relevant to this drug

- **IV daratumumab** was approved by the FDA in 2015 for relapsed/refractory MM after ≥3 prior lines.
- **Subcutaneous daratumumab (Darzalex Faspro, daratumumab + rHuPH20 co-formulated)** was approved by the FDA in **May 2020** for multiple myeloma indications, based on the **COLUMBA** study (NCT03277105), which showed non-inferior pharmacokinetics and comparable efficacy/safety versus IV daratumumab, with shorter administration time (~3–5 minutes) and fewer infusion-related reactions.
- The **Pavo** study (NCT03952091) evaluated SC daratumumab in combination with other agents; **Perseus** (NCT03710603) evaluated SC daratumumab in newly diagnosed transplant-eligible MM.

Historically, route-of-administration or formulation changes for an already-validated biologic in the same indication have very high technical success rates, and this specific program did in fact succeed: the 1800 mg SC co-formulated dose advanced to the Phase 3 COLUMBA study, met its non-inferiority endpoints, and received FDA approval as Darzalex Faspro in May 2020. General Phase 1 oncology benchmarks are much lower (often cited around 5–10% for eventual approval from Phase 1), and even indication-level Phase 1 to approval rates in hematologic malignancies are typically well below 50%, but these aggregate figures are dominated by novel, unvalidated agents and mechanisms. Conditioning on the fact that daratumumab was already an approved, mechanistically de-risked agent being reformulated for a more convenient route in the same disease, and that the target 1800 mg SC dose is the one that ultimately succeeded, a retrospective probability of roughly 0.75 for this trial's program reaching a successful registrational outcome is a defensible estimate — leaving the remaining ~0.25 for the genuine but lower-probability risks of PK non-equivalence, unacceptable immunogenicity, injection-site/administration toxicity, or strategic discontinuation, any of which could have derailed the SC program even with a validated parent molecule.

Below is an assessment of what a "successful outcome" would look like for NCT02519452, based strictly on the registered design and general Phase 1b principles. Where the registry does not specify something, I say "unknown" rather than infer a number.

---

**1. Likely primary endpoints and how they would be measured**

The registered primary outcomes are:
- **Serum trough concentration (Ctrough) of daratumumab** — measured up to Cycle 3 Day 1 (each cycle = 28 days). This is the PK-based primary endpoint. Success would mean achieving a Ctrough at the SC dose that is comparable to (or exceeds) the Ctrough of the approved IV daratumumab regimen, consistent with the exposure–response relationship established for IV daratumumab.
- **Number of participants with adverse events (AEs) and serious AEs (SAEs)** — measured from screening through 30 days after last dose (~3.4 years). This is the safety primary endpoint. Success would mean an AE/SAE profile consistent with the known IV daratumumab safety profile, without unexpected or dose-limiting toxicities, and with acceptable injection-site reactions and immunogenicity.

In practical terms, the co-primary "success" for this program is: (a) PK non-inferiority to IV daratumumab at the selected SC dose, and (b) acceptable safety/tolerability.

---

**2. Statistical threshold**

- The **specific numeric threshold** (e.g., a non-inferiority margin on the Ctrough ratio, a confidence interval bound, or a p-value) is **unknown** — the registry does not state it, and I do not have reliable recall of the protocol-specified margin for this specific trial.
- For context, the analogous Phase 3 COLUMBA study used a **non-inferiority margin** on the Ctrough ratio (the lower bound of the 90% CI had to exceed a pre-specified threshold, commonly cited as 0.8) and on overall response rate. NCT02519452, being Phase 1b, would more likely use a **PK-based target** (e.g., the SC Ctrough falling within a pre-specified range relative to IV, or meeting a pre-specified exposure target) rather than a formal hypothesis test with p<0.05.
- **unknown** whether any formal p-value or hypothesis test was pre-specified for this Phase 1b trial.

---

**3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence**

This is almost certainly a **non-inferiority / PK-bridging** design, not a superiority trial. The goal is to show that SC daratumumab achieves drug exposure and safety comparable to the already-approved IV formulation, not to show it is better. Equivalence in the strict sense is unlikely to be the formal framework; non-inferiority (or a PK exposure-matching objective) is the standard approach for a route-of-administration change. I state this as the most likely interpretation; the registry itself does not explicitly label the trial as superiority/non-inferiority/equivalence, so the formal label is **unknown**.

---

**4. Key design features**

From the registry:
- **Allocation**: NON_RANDOMIZED.
- **Intervention model**: PARALLEL (separate dose cohorts/parts run in parallel).
- **Masking**: NONE (open-label).
- **Control arm**: There is **no separate control arm** in the registered design. Comparisons are internal — dose cohorts within Part 1, and cross-study/historical comparison to IV daratumumab PK and safety. This is typical of a Phase 1b dose-escalation/expansion study.
- **Structure**: Three parts — Part 1 (dose selection for the daratumumab + rHuPH20 mixture, cohorts 1–3 plus optional 3b/3c/3d), Part 2 (co-formulated daratumumab + rHuPH20 at the dose selected from Part 1), Part 3 (Dara-CF 1800 mg without pre-/post-dose corticosteroids).
- **No randomization, no blinding, no placebo** — so any efficacy signals (ORR, CR, DR, time to response — all listed as *secondary* outcomes) are descriptive, not formally hypothesis-tested against a control.

---

**Summary of what "success" would look like**

A successful outcome for NCT02519452 would be:
1. Selection of an SC daratumumab dose (mixture, then co-formulated) that produces **Ctrough comparable to IV daratumumab** at the relevant timepoint (Cycle 3 Day 1).
2. A **safety profile consistent with IV daratumumab**, with manageable injection-site reactions and no unexpected immunogenicity or dose-limiting toxicity.
3. Supportive (secondary) evidence of **antitumor activity** (ORR, CR, DR) consistent with the IV formulation.
4. The selected 1800 mg co-formulated SC dose being carried forward into a registrational (Phase 3) study.

This is exactly the path that occurred: the SC program advanced to COLUMBA (NCT03277105), which met its PK non-inferiority and ORR endpoints and led to FDA approval of Darzalex Faspro in May 2020.

**Items I am explicitly unsure about and therefore mark unknown**: the exact pre-specified PK non-inferiority margin or exposure target for this specific trial; whether any formal statistical hypothesis test with a p-value threshold was pre-specified; the precise number of participants actually enrolled in each part; and whether the trial formally declared a single "primary success" definition versus a set of descriptive objectives.

---

**RISK 1: Enrollment and recruitment failure due to competitive landscape**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: The registry itself flags that a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval during the trial, establishing a new standard of care. That directly threatens recruitment feasibility — patients and investigators may prefer the newly approved agent. The target population also has a narrow entry window: relapsed/refractory MM, ≤2 prior lines, must have received a PI and an IMiD, and must be daratumumab-naive (prior anti-CD38 therapy is excluded). By ~2020, daratumumab was moving into earlier lines of therapy, making daratumumab-naive relapsed/refractory patients progressively harder to find. - **LIKELIHOOD**: HIGH

---

**RISK 2: Failure to demonstrate PK non-inferiority / exposure matching of SC vs IV daratumumab**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: The primary purpose of the trial is to show that SC daratumumab (mixed, then co-formulated with rHuPH20) achieves serum trough concentrations comparable to the approved IV regimen. If the SC Ctrough falls below the target exposure–response range — due to absorption variability, depot effects, or rHuPH20 performance — the SC dose would not be supported for registration. This is a genuine PK risk because SC administration of a large monoclonal antibody depends on hyaluronidase-mediated tissue permeability, and inter-patient variability can be substantial. A miss here would invalidate the entire premise of Parts 1–3.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM

---

**RISK 3: Safety signals — injection-site reactions, immunogenicity, or corticosteroid-tapering toxicity**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: The trial's co-primary endpoint is safety (AEs/SAEs), and Part 3 specifically tests Dara-CF 1800 mg **without pre-dose and post-dose corticosteroids** — removing the prophylaxis that normally mitigates infusion-/injection-related reactions. If injection-site reactions, systemic administration reactions, or anti-drug antibodies (anti-daratumumab or anti-rHuPH20) are more frequent or severe than with IV daratumumab, this could halt dose escalation, force corticosteroid reinstatement, or render the SC formulation non-viable. The rHuPH20 component adds its own immunogenicity risk. A serious safety signal in Part 1 or Part 2 would cascade through all subsequent parts.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM

---

**RISK 4: Trial design limitations — no randomization, no control arm, open-label**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: The registered design is NON_RANDOMIZED, PARALLEL, masking=NONE, with no placebo or active control. All efficacy outcomes (ORR, CR, DR, time to response) are **secondary** and descriptive only, with no formal hypothesis test against a comparator. This means the trial cannot independently establish efficacy — it can only generate supportive signals. If the PK or safety data are ambiguous, there is no randomized control to fall back on. Interpretation relies on cross-study comparison to historical IV daratumumab data, which is vulnerable to confounding and era effects.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: MEDIUM

---

**RISK 5: Strategic / regulatory deprioritization**
- **APPLIES_BECAUSE**: This is a supportive Phase 1b study for a lifecycle-management objective (convenience of SC administration) on an already-approved molecule. If the sponsoring company's portfolio priorities shifted, if a competitor's SC or off-the-shelf alternative (e.g., bispecifics, CAR-T, or another SC anti-CD38) gained traction, or if regulators signaled they would require a larger or differently designed confirmatory program, the trial could be deprioritized, amended, or terminated early. Because the parent drug was already marketed and successful IV, the SC program's business case depends on maintaining competitive advantage — which can erode quickly.
- **LIKELIHOOD**: LOW to MEDIUM

---

Risks 1 and 2 are the most consequential because they directly threaten the trial's ability to generate interpretable data — one by preventing completion, the other by failing the core PK objective. Risk 3 is the classic Phase 1 failure mode and is especially relevant here because of the corticosteroid-free Part 3. Risk 4 is structural and inherent to the design, limiting what a "success" can even mean. Risk 5 is external and reflects the trial's role as a lifecycle-management study on an already-validated drug.

Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH)
Lead sponsor: Corcept Therapeutics
Enrollment: 12
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=TRIPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
This phase 2, double blind, placebo-controlled, randomized study is to assess the safety and efficacy of miricorilant (CORT118335) in patients with presumed Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH). Since this trial's initiation, a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval, establishing a new standard of care and potentially affecting the clinical relevance of the study's primary endpoint and recruitment feasibility.

Detailed description:
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study that assessed the safety efficacy and pharmacokinetics (PK) of miricorilant in patients with presumed Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH). Patients who meet the criteria for Study CORT118335-860 were randomized on Day 1 to receive 900 mg miricorilant, 600 mg miricorilant, or placebo for 12 weeks.

Due to observations related to safety, the study was terminated prior to completion and study objectives, endpoints, and procedures were modified as specified in the protocol.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Miricorilant- 900 mg: Participants received 900 mg miricorilant (6 miricorilant tablets of 150 mg) orally once daily.
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Miricorilant- 600 mg: Participants received 600 mg miricorilant (4 miricorilant tablets of 150 mg and 2 placebo tablets) orally once daily.
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: Participants received 6 placebo tablets orally once daily.

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Miricorilant: Tablets taken orally
  - [DRUG] Placebo: Placebo tablets

Primary outcomes:
  - Relative Change From Baseline in Liver Fat Content Assessed by Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Proton Density Fat Fraction [time frame: Baseline and up to ~Day 95]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Number of Participants Achieving a Relative Reduction From Baseline in LFC of ≥30% by MRI-PDFF [time frame: Baseline and up to ~Day 95]
  - Change From Baseline in Aspartate Aminotransferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Alanine Aminotransferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Gamma-glutamyl Transferase [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Propeptide of Type III Collagen [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]
  - Change From Baseline in Enhanced Liver Fibrosis Score [time frame: Baseline and Week 6]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Have a diagnosis of NASH based on a biopsy obtained within the last year OR
* Have a diagnosis of presumed NASH based on blood tests and scans

Exclusion Criteria:

* Have participated in another clinical trial within the last year and received active treatment for NASH
* Have participated in another clinical trial for any other indication within the last 3 months
* Are pregnant or lactating women
* Have a BMI \<18 kg/m\^2
* Have had liver transplantation or plan to have liver transplantation during the study
* Have type 1 diabetes or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.

**Drug mechanism of action**
- Miricorilant (CORT118335) is a selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulator / antagonist, and also a modest antagonist at the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) and progesterone receptor (PR). Corcept's core platform is GR modulation (its approved drug is mifepristone for Cushing's syndrome).
- The rationale in NASH: glucocorticoid receptor signaling and cortisol excess are implicated in hepatic steatosis, insulin resistance, and inflammation; GR antagonism was hypothesized to reduce liver fat.

**Relationship to other Corcept compounds**
- Corcept's more advanced metabolic candidate in this era was CORT118335 (miricorilant) and later relacorilant (CORT125134, a more selective GR antagonist without significant PR activity). Relacorilant is being developed for Cushing's syndrome and, more recently, for ovarian and adrenal cancers.
- Unknown: whether miricorilant has any ongoing development program today; I believe it was deprioritized, but I cannot confirm current status.

Here is a description of what would constitute a successful outcome for NCT03823703, based strictly on the registered design plus standard Phase 2 conventions. Where the registry does not specify something, I say "unknown" rather than invent it.

**1. Primary endpoint and how it would be measured**

- The registered primary outcome is: **Relative Change From Baseline in Liver Fat Content (LFC) Assessed by MRI-PDFF**, with a time frame of Baseline to ~Day 95 (i.e., end of the 12-week treatment).
- Measurement: MRI-PDFF (Magnetic Resonance Imaging–Proton Density Fat Fraction) is a non-invasive imaging biomarker that quantifies the hepatic fat fraction. "Relative change from baseline" means the percentage change in liver fat fraction at end of treatment versus baseline, typically computed per participant and then summarized by arm (e.g., mean or median relative change).
- Success on this endpoint: a statistically significant, and clinically meaningful, greater reduction in relative LFC in at least one miricorilant dose arm compared with placebo. The registry does not state a specific numeric target for the primary endpoint, so the exact magnitude required is **unknown**.
- Note: the registry lists LFC relative change as the sole primary endpoint. The ≥30% relative reduction threshold appears as a **secondary** binary endpoint, not the primary. (In broader NASH literature a ≥30% relative MRI-PDFF reduction is often treated as a responder threshold, but here the registry assigns it to secondary outcomes.)

**2. Statistical threshold**

- The registered statistical threshold is **unknown** — ClinicalTrials.gov does not include the alpha level, power, or effect-size assumptions for this study in the excerpt provided.
- By convention for a Phase 2 superiority trial with a continuous primary endpoint, success would typically require a **two-sided p < 0.05** (or a one-sided p < 0.025) for the comparison of the active arm versus placebo, after any multiplicity adjustment across the two dose arms.
- If the two active doses were compared to a shared placebo, some multiplicity control (e.g., hierarchical testing or Bonferroni-type adjustment) would be expected — but whether this was pre-specified here is **unknown**.
- No hazard ratio, non-inferiority margin, or responder-rate difference threshold is specified in the registry, so those specifics are **unknown**.

**3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence**

- This is almost certainly a **superiority** trial. The design is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group Phase 2 study in which the active arms are compared against placebo, and the objective is to show that miricorilant reduces liver fat more than placebo.
- There is no indication in the registry of a non-inferiority or equivalence framing (both would be unusual for a novel agent against placebo in this indication).

**4. Key design features**

- **Allocation:** randomized.
- **Intervention model:** parallel-group.
- **Masking:** triple (i.e., participant, investigator/care provider, and outcome assessor all blinded — the standard interpretation of "triple" masking on ClinicalTrials.gov, though the exact three parties are not itemized in the registry).
- **Control arm:** placebo comparator — placebo tablets matching miricorilant, taken orally once daily.
- **Active arms:** miricorilant 900 mg once daily and miricorilant 600 mg once daily. The placebo arm received 6 matching tablets daily, and the 600 mg arm received 4 active + 2 placebo tablets daily, which preserves blinding to dose.
- **Randomization ratio:** **unknown** (1:1:1 is a common assumption but not stated).
- **Treatment duration:** 12 weeks, with the primary endpoint assessed at ~Day 95.
- **Enrollment:** 12 participants (very small — consistent with a signal-seeking Phase 2, not a confirmatory trial).
- **Eligibility:** adults 18–75, all sexes, NASH diagnosed by biopsy within the prior year OR presumed NASH based on blood tests and imaging.
- **Key exclusions:** prior NASH trial participation within a year, other trial participation within 3 months, pregnancy/lactation, BMI <18, liver transplant (or planned), type 1 diabetes or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.

**Important caveats**

- Because the registry explicitly notes the study was **terminated early due to safety observations** and that objectives, endpoints, and procedures were **modified during the conduct of the study**, the "successful outcome" definition above reflects the **registered** design, not necessarily the final amended protocol. What the modified endpoints or analysis plan ultimately were is **unknown** from the provided excerpt.
- With only 12 participants across three arms, the trial would be **underpowered** by conventional standards to detect modest treatment effects, so even a "positive" result would be hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.
- The specific alpha, power, randomization ratio, and pre-specified effect size are **unknown** and would need to be confirmed from the full protocol or statistical analysis plan.

---

**RISK: Safety-driven termination / drug tolerability**
- APPLIES_BECAUSE: The registry explicitly states the study "was terminated prior to completion" due to "observations related to safety," and that objectives, endpoints, and procedures had to be modified as a result. This is the single most concrete and disqualifying signal for this specific trial — it is not a hypothetical risk, it already materialized. Miricorilant is a glucocorticoid receptor modulator/antagonist with mineralocorticoid and progesterone receptor activity, a mechanistic profile with plausible off-target safety liabilities (HPA-axis effects, blood pressure, endocrine/gynecologic effects) that would be especially problematic in a 12-week daily-dosing chronic indication like NASH.
- LIKELIHOOD: HIGH (already occurred)

---

**RISK: Efficacy failure / weak mechanistic rationale in NASH**
- APPLIES_BECAUSE: Glucocorticoid receptor antagonism has no validated precedent in NASH, and the mechanistic hypothesis (cortisol/GR signaling driving steatosis and inflammation) was speculative. The endpoint chosen (relative change in MRI-PDFF) is a surrogate that measures fat reduction, not fibrosis or clinical outcomes — regulators have repeatedly made clear that fat reduction alone is insufficient for approval. Combined with a tiny n=12 sample and a 12-week window, even a real but modest effect could be missed, and a "positive" result would be fragile.
- LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

---

**RISK: Enrollment failure / infeasibility**
- APPLIES_BECAUSE: The target enrollment was only 12 participants, which itself signals that recruitment was expected to be difficult — a very small n is often chosen precisely because the eligible population is hard to reach. The inclusion criteria require either biopsy-confirmed NASH within the prior year or presumed NASH by blood tests and imaging, and the exclusions are broad (prior NASH trial within a year, any trial within 3 months, type 1 or poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, BMI <18, transplant history). Competing NASH trials in the same era were also competing for the same patients. A trial that cannot enroll cannot reach its endpoint regardless of drug activity.
- LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

---

**RISK: Competitive / regulatory landscape shift**
- APPLIES_BECAUSE: The trial summary itself states that "a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval, establishing a new standard of care and potentially affecting the clinical relevance of the study's primary endpoint and recruitment feasibility." This is a documented, trial-specific risk — the emergence of an approved NASH/MASH therapy (resmetirom) reset the regulatory and clinical bar mid-development, meaning an MRI-PDFF fat-reduction endpoint against placebo could no longer be considered clinically meaningful, and patients/investigators had less incentive to enroll in a placebo-controlled Phase 2 of an unproven mechanism.
- LIKELIHOOD: HIGH (already occurred)

---

**RISK: Trial design limitations / underpowering and endpoint fragility**
- APPLIES_BECAUSE: This is a Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel trial with n=12 across three arms (900 mg, 600 mg, placebo). That is severely underpowered for detecting anything but a very large treatment effect. The primary endpoint is a continuous imaging biomarker (relative change in MRI-PDFF) whose statistical threshold (alpha, power, effect size) is unknown from the registry; the secondary responder endpoint (≥30% relative reduction) is binary and even more sensitive to small samples. Two active dose arms versus one shared placebo further dilutes power unless multiplicity was carefully controlled. Endpoint and procedure modifications mid-study (acknowledged in the registry) introduce additional analytic ambiguity.
- LIKELIHOOD: HIGH

---

**Ordering rationale (most to least concerning):**
1. **Safety-driven termination** — already materialized and uniquely disqualifying; safety failures kill programs far more decisively than efficacy misses.
2. **Efficacy failure** — the fundamental scientific risk; the mechanism was unvalidated in NASH and the surrogate endpoint is a weak proxy for clinical benefit.
3. **Enrollment failure** — n=12 signals pre-existing recruitment difficulty, which compounds every other risk.
4. **Competitive/regulatory shift** — documented in the trial's own summary as undermining the study's relevance and feasibility.
5. **Design limitations** — underpowering and mid-study amendments reduce the trial's ability to produce a clean, interpretable result even if the drug works.

- The specific adverse events or safety findings that triggered termination are **unknown** to me; I am inferring the mechanism-class concerns from the drug's pharmacology, not from reported data.

- The exact amended endpoints/procedures after the mid-study modification are **unknown** from the registry excerpt.

Based on the trial specification shown at the start, your own knowledge, and the similar trials you listed, make your final prediction:

PREDICTION: SUCCESS or FAILURE
CONFIDENCE: a number between 0.0 and 1.0
KEY_REASON: one sentence explaining the most important factor

PREDICTION: FAILURE
CONFIDENCE: 0.97
KEY_REASON: The trial was already terminated early for safety observations, and this sits on top of an unvalidated mechanism in NASH, an underpowered n=12 design with a surrogate MRI-PDFF endpoint, and a competitive/regulatory landscape that shifted mid-study — a combination that makes a successful, clinically meaningful, approvable outcome extremely unlikely.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE1
Conditions: Solid Tumors
Lead sponsor: Shanghai Junshi Bioscience Co., Ltd.
Enrollment: 24
Design: allocation=NA; intervention model=SINGLE_GROUP; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, tolerance and Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT) of Recombinant humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (JS001) in patients with advanced solid tumors. Since this trial's initiation, a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval, establishing a new standard of care and potentially affecting the clinical relevance of the study's primary endpoint and recruitment feasibility.

Detailed description:
OVERVIEW

This is a Phase 1, open-label, dose-escalation study of JS-001, a humanized monoclonal IgG4 antibody targeting the Programmed Death -1 (PD-1). It is estimated that 12-24 subjects with advanced or recurrent solid tumors or will be enrolled in the study.

A 3+3 design will be utilized for this Phase 1 study. Four dose levels are planned and include: 0.3, 1, 3, 10 mg/kg/dose. Each of the 4 dose levels will use 2 dose schedules: single dose, repeated doses every 2 weeks. Subjects will be assigned to a dose schedule in the order of study entry.

The study will be the traditional 3 + 3 design with 3 or 6 subjects treated at this dose level and at all subsequent dose levels depending upon the incidence of DLTs. If no DLTs occur in a cohort of 3 subjects, a new cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 1 of 3 subjects in a cohort experiences a DLT, that cohort will be expanded to 6 subjects. If only 1 of the 6 subjects has a DLT, then the next cohort of 3 subjects will be treated at the next higher dose level. If 2 or more DLTs occur within a cohort, then that dose level will be above the MTD (the highest dose where no more than 1 of 6 subjects has experienced a DLT), and the previous lower (tolerated) dose level will be considered the MTD.

A DLT is defined as a Grade 3 drug-related adverse event occurring within the first cycle (28 days) of dosing (excluding tumor flare defined as local pain, irritation, or rash localized at sites of known or suspected tumor or a transient Grade 3 infusion adverse event) using National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 in a single dose cohort.

Tumor response will be evaluated using immune-related response criteria (irRC), WHO criteria , Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST), immune-related RECIST, and International Workshop to Standardize Response Criteria for non-Hodgkin's Lymphomas (for lymphomas only).

In the absence of confirmed disease progression and intolerable toxicities, subjects in the single dose cohorts and multiple dose cohorts will be allowed to continue JS-001 administration with the consent of the subject.

DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION

JS-001 will be administered as a 60-minute i.v. infusion. Cohorts will include escalating dose levels of 0.3, 1, 3, 10mg/kg/dose.

SAFETY EVALUATIONS

Assessment of safety will be determined by vital sign measurements, clinical laboratory tests, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status evaluations, diagnostic imaging, physical examinations, electrocardiograms, and the incidence and severity of adverse events.

Safety will also include evaluations of immune safety and immunogenicity. Particular attention will be given to adverse events that may follow enhanced T-cell activation such as dermatitis and colitis, uveitis, or other immune-related adverse events (irAEs).

An irAE is a clinically significant adverse event of any organ that is associated with drug exposure, of unknown etiology, and is consistent with an immune-mediated mechanism.

EFFICACY EVALUATIONS

The primary efficacy endpoint is the best response rate (RR). Duration of response, progression-free survival, time to progression, and overall survival will also be analyzed.

PHARMACOKINETIC EVALUATIONS

Pharmacokinetic parameters include AUC, Cmax, tmax, and t½, etc. STATISTICAL METHODS The sample size for this study is not determined from power analysis. It is based on the 3+3 design for dose escalation and safety evaluation requirements.

Descriptive statistics will include: mean, standard deviation, median, and minimum and maximum values for continuous variables; frequencies and percentages for categorical variables.

The efficacy parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics. All safety and pharmacokinetic parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody toripalimab: humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody is to be injected intravenously 0.3mg/kg or 1mg/kg or 3mg/kg or 10mg/kg until disease progresses or unacceptable tolerability occurs.

Interventions:
  - [BIOLOGICAL] humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody toripalimab: humanized anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (JS001) is a programmed death-1 (PD-1) immune checkpoint inhibitor antibody, which selectively interferes with the combination of PD-1 with its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, resulting in the activation of lymphocytes and elimination of malignancy theoretically.

Primary outcomes:
  - Number of Participants With Abnormal Laboratory Values and/or Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Anti-Drug Antibody of JS001 in Chinese patients [time frame: Cycle 1,2,3,5 Day 1 before JS001 infusion and 336 hours after last JS001 infusion, each cycle is 28 days.]
  - Objective Response Rate (ORR) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Duration of Response (DOR) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Progression-Free survival (PFS) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - Overall Survival (OS) [time frame: Up to 2 approximately years]
  - DLT in patients with solid tumor treated with JS001. [time frame: Cycle 1（each cycle is 28 days）]
  - PD-1 receptor occupancy of blood [time frame: 1 year]
  - Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody (mAb) [time frame: 1 year]
  - Peak Time (Tmax) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Area Under the Curve (AUC) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb Area Under the Curve [AUC]). Area Under the Curve (AUC) after single dose injection of Recombinant Humanized Anti-PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody [time frame: 1 year]
  - t1/2 after single dose injection of Recombinant Humanized Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Plasma clearance (CL) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Apparent volume of distribution (V) after single dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Minimum Plasma Concentration (Cmin) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Average Plasma Concentration (Cav) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Degree of fluctuation (DF) of steady state after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]
  - Apparent volume of distribution of steady state (Vss) after multiple dose injection of Anti-PD-1 mAb [time frame: 1 year]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Histological or cytological diagnosis of advanced or recurrent adenocarcinoma of solid tumor, including adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastro-esophageal junction, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, Pancreatic ductal cell carcinoma, etc.

   * at least one prior chemotherapy regimen
   * age between 18 and 75 years, both gender
   * has at least one measurable disease by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST V1.1)
2. life expectancy ≥ 3 months
3. ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
4. Has had last dose of chemotherapy more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001, and has recovered to National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 4.0 Grade 1 or better from the AEs due to the chemotherapy.
5. Has had last administration of radioactive therapy more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
6. Has had last administration of immunosuppressive systemic steroid therapy (more than 10 mg/d prednisone or equal dose) more than 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
7. Has undergone major surgery that needs general anesthesia more than 4 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001. Has undergone surgery that needs local anesthesia or epidural anesthesia more than 72 hours prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001 and has already recovered from the surgery. Has undergone biopsy more than 1 hour prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
8. The lab examination results of the screening must fulfill all of the following:

   * absolute neutrophil count more than or equal to 1.5×109/ L
   * platelet count more than or equal to 90×109/ L
   * hemoglobin more than or equal to 90 g/L
   * creatinine less than or equal to132.6µmol/L or creatinine clearance \>40 mL/min
   * aspartate transferase(AST) and alanine transferase(ALT) less than or equal to 3.0 ×ULN
   * total bilirubin less than or equal to 1.5×ULN( except for the patients with Gilbert syndrome, whose total bilirubin ,must less than or equal to 51.3µmol/L)
9. Patient has been informed about the nature of the study, and has agreed to participate in the study, and signed the Informed Consent Form prior to participation in any study related activities.
10. Able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Has had antineoplastic herbal therapy within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study therapy JS001.
2. Is currently participating and receiving study therapy or has participated in a study of an investigational agent and receive study therapy or used an investigational device within 4 weeks of the first dose of study drug.
3. Has a medical condition that requires chronic systemic steroid therapy or on any other form of immunosuppressive medication.
4. Has a known history of a hematologic malignancy, primary brain tumor or sarcoma, or of another primary solid tumor, unless the participant has undergone potentially curative therapy with no evidence of that disease for 5 years.
5. Has known active central nervous system (CNS) metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
6. Has interstitial lung disease OR has had a history of pneumonitis that has required oral or IV steroids.
7. Has active or suspected autoimmune disease except leukoderma,type I Diabetes, Residual hypothyroidism that induced by autoimmune thyroiditis and only requires the use of hormone replacement therapy, Or disease that rarely relapse without external stimulating factors.
8. Had prior treatment targeting PD-1: anti-PD-1,anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-L2, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein (CTLA), or other antibodies that targeting T cell costimulatory pathway or checkpoint.
9. Has an active infection requiring systematic therapy.
10. Is positive for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
11. Has active Tuberculosis.
12. Has known active Hepatitis B or C.
13. Has known psychiatric or substance abuse disorders that would interfere with cooperation with the requirements of the study.
14. Has received or will receive a live vaccine within 30 days prior to the first administration of study drug.
15. Is pregnant or breastfeeding.
16. Cannot tolerate vein puncture and / or venous access.
17. Any other conclusive medical reasons, mental illness, and / or social reasons that determined by the investigators.

# Successful Outcome for NCT02857166 (JS001 / Toripalimab Phase 1)

This is a **Phase 1, open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation (3+3) study** in advanced solid tumors. Success criteria in such a trial are fundamentally different from a randomized Phase 2/3 efficacy trial. Below I describe what would constitute success, based strictly on the registered design and standard Phase 1 oncology conventions. Where the registration does not specify something, I say so.

---

## 1. Likely Primary Endpoint(s) and How They Would Be Measured

**Primary endpoint (safety/tolerability and DLT, per the registered brief summary and outcome list):**

- **Number of participants with abnormal laboratory values and/or adverse events related to treatment** — measured by:
  - Vital signs, clinical laboratory tests, ECOG performance status, diagnostic imaging, physical exams, ECGs.
  - Incidence and severity of adverse events graded by **NCI CTCAE v4.0**.
  - Targeted surveillance for **immune-related adverse events (irAEs)** such as dermatitis, colitis, uveitis, and other immune-mediated events.
- **Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLT)** — a Grade 3 drug-related AE occurring within the **first cycle (28 days)** of dosing, per CTCAE v4.0, excluding tumor flare and transient Grade 3 infusion reactions.
  - DLT is the operational endpoint that drives the 3+3 dose-escalation decisions.

**Co-primary / key secondary endpoints (as registered):**

- **Anti-drug antibody (ADA) of JS001** — immunogenicity.
- **PD-1 receptor occupancy of blood.**
- **Pharmacokinetic parameters:** AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t½, CL, V, Cmin, Cav, DF, Vss (single-dose and steady-state).
- **Efficacy (secondary, exploratory in a Phase 1):** Objective Response Rate (ORR), Duration of Response (DOR), Progression-Free Survival (PFS), Overall Survival (OS), with tumor response assessed by **irRC, WHO criteria, RECIST, irRECIST, and the International Workshop criteria for lymphomas.**

**Important nuance:** In a Phase 1 dose-escalation trial, the "primary endpoint" is formally safety/DLT, but the *de facto* determinants of whether the program advances are (a) identification of a tolerable dose (MTD or recommended Phase 2 dose, RP2D) and (b) any signal of antitumor activity.

---

## 2. Statistical Threshold That Would Need to Be Met

- **There is no formal hypothesis test, no p-value threshold, no hazard ratio, and no non-inferiority margin** specified for this trial. The registration explicitly states:
  > "The sample size for this study is not determined from power analysis. It is based on the 3+3 design for dose escalation and safety evaluation requirements."
  > "The efficacy parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics. All safety and pharmacokinetic parameters will be summarized using descriptive statistics."
- **Therefore, success is defined operationally, not statistically**, via the 3+3 algorithm:
  - **If 0 of 3 subjects at a dose level experience a DLT** → escalate to the next higher dose.
  - **If 1 of 3 experiences a DLT** → expand that cohort to 6 subjects.
    - If only 1 of 6 has a DLT → escalate.
    - If ≥2 of 6 have a DLT → that dose is **above the MTD**.
  - **The MTD** is defined as the highest dose at which **no more than 1 of 6 subjects** experiences a DLT.
- **Success on the DLT/safety axis** = identifying an MTD (or RP2D) with an acceptable DLT rate (typically ≤1/6, i.e., ≤~33% by the 3+3 convention) and a manageable AE profile.
- **Success on the efficacy axis (descriptive only):** any confirmed objective response (CR or PR) by RECIST/irRECIST, with a credible DOR and PFS signal, would be considered encouraging in this refractory solid-tumor population. No formal threshold is pre-specified. **Any specific ORR cutoff is unknown** — none is registered.

- **None of the above.** This is a **single-arm, uncontrolled, dose-escalation Phase 1 trial**. There is no comparator arm, so superiority/non-inferiority/equivalence frameworks do not apply.
- The correct framing is **descriptive safety and dose-finding**, with exploratory efficacy. Any inference is against historical/expected background rates, not against a randomized control.

## RISK 1: Immune-Related Adverse Events (irAEs) Exceeding Tolerability at Escalating Doses

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** This trial's primary endpoint is safety/DLT, and it explicitly escalates to a relatively high dose of **10 mg/kg** — among the higher anti-PD-1 doses attempted in first-in-human studies. The registration itself flags special attention to "adverse events that may follow enhanced T-cell activation such as dermatitis and colitis, uveitis, or other immune-related adverse events." Anti-PD-1 antibodies as a class carry well-documented risks of pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, hypophysitis, thyroiditis, and rarely severe (Grade 3–4) immune toxicity. If ≥2 of 6 subjects at a given dose level experience a DLT within the first 28 days, that dose is declared above the MTD, capping the dose range and potentially preventing achievement of a therapeutically adequate exposure. In a Chinese patient population with a high prevalence of **chronic Hepatitis B** (a known risk amplifier for immune-mediated hepatic injury), this risk may be accentuated. The exclusion criteria partially mitigate this (they exclude active HBV/HCV, autoimmune disease, and interstitial lung disease), but subclinical or reactivation risk remains.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH (this is the single most likely reason a Phase 1 anti-PD-1 dose-escalation trial fails to reach its top dose; the question is severity, not occurrence).

---

## RISK 2: Futility — No Meaningful Antitumor Activity Signal

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The enrolled population is heavily pretreated (≥1 prior chemotherapy) advanced/recurrent solid tumors, including gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, esophageal SCC, NPC, cholangiocarcinoma, and pancreatic ductal carcinoma. Several of these (pancreatic, cholangiocarcinoma) are notoriously immunotherapy-resistant. If the trial produces no confirmed objective responses (CR/PR) by RECIST/irRECIST across dose levels, the program has no efficacy rationale to advance to Phase 2, even if safety is clean. For a first-in-human study, even a small number of durable responses is often the deciding factor for go/no-go. Because the design is single-arm and descriptive, there is no statistical power to detect small efficacy differences, so absence of a clear response signal is a genuine failure mode.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM (unpredictable; some responding histologies like NPC and esophageal SCC were included, which raises the chance of at least some responses, but the mixed and refractory population makes overall futility plausible).

---

## RISK 3: Enrollment Feasibility and Slow Accrual

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The trial targets a narrow population — advanced/recurrent solid tumors, ≥1 prior chemo, ECOG 0–1, measurable disease, no prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 therapy, no active autoimmune disease, no active HBV/HCV, no CNS metastases, no interstitial lung disease — across a specific set of histologies. Many of these exclusion criteria remove exactly the patients most likely to be referred to a Phase 1 immunotherapy trial. The target enrollment is only 24 subjects, but for a single-country Phase 1 with restrictive eligibility and a 3+3 design that requires sequential cohorts, slow accrual can delay the trial or prevent completion of the planned dose levels. The registration's own note that a **competing therapy received FDA approval and established a new standard of care** further undermines recruitment: patients and physicians may prefer an approved PD-1 antibody (off-label or via trials) over an investigational one.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH (enrollment in early-phase immunotherapy trials in competitive landscapes is a well-documented, common failure mode; the registration itself acknowledges the competitive threat).

---

## RISK 4: Competitive Landscape Rendering the Trial Scientifically or Commercially Irrelevant

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** The registered brief summary explicitly states that "a competing therapy for the same indication received FDA approval, establishing a new standard of care and potentially affecting the clinical relevance of the study's primary endpoint and recruitment feasibility." By the time this trial was running, pembrolizumab and nivolumab were already approved and becoming standard of care in multiple solid tumors, and other Chinese anti-PD-1 antibodies (sintilimab, camrelizumab, tislelizumab) were entering the same space. Even if the trial succeeds on its own terms (tolerable dose, some responses), the results may be judged non-differentiating — the drug would be a "me-too" anti-PD-1 with no clear advantage. For a sponsor and regulators, this reduces the value of the data and can lead to deprioritization of the program or a decision not to pursue registration based on this trial alone.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** MEDIUM (the trial did in fact yield an approvable drug eventually, but at the time of this trial the competitive risk was real and could have caused failure/deprioritization; the risk is "trial-level relevance" rather than "drug-level failure").

---

## RISK 5: Design Limitations That Preclude Definitive Interpretation

- **APPLIES_BECAUSE:** This is a **single-arm, open-label, non-randomized, uncontrolled** Phase 1 with a **3+3 design**. Key limitations that constitute failure modes:
  - **Small sample size (24)** — no statistical power to detect modest efficacy signals or uncommon toxicities; a serious AE occurring at low frequency may be missed entirely.
  - **3+3 design inefficiency** — widely criticized for imprecision in MTD estimation and for treating few patients at doses near the MTD, yielding unstable estimates.
  - **No control arm** — any efficacy observation is confounded by natural history, patient selection, and prior therapy effects.
  - **Mixed histologies** — pooling gastric, esophageal, NPC, cholangiocarcinoma, and pancreatic cancer in one small trial makes it impossible to ascribe responses to the drug with confidence in any single indication.
  - **Open-label** — subjective endpoints (AE grading, response assessment) are susceptible to bias, though RECIST/irRECIST provide some objectivity.
  - **Descriptive statistics only** — no formal hypothesis testing means even a "positive" result may not persuade regulators without additional confirmatory trials.
- **LIKELIHOOD:** HIGH (these are intrinsic to the design; the question is whether they cause the trial to be *interpreted* as failed or inconclusive, which is likely if the efficacy signal is weak).

---

## Summary Table

| Rank | Risk | Likelihood |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | irAEs exceeding tolerability / failure to reach top dose | HIGH |
| 2 | Futility — no antitumor activity signal | MEDIUM |
| 3 | Enrollment feasibility / slow accrual | HIGH |
| 4 | Competitive landscape rendering trial non-relevant | MEDIUM |
| 5 | Design limitations preventing definitive interpretation | HIGH |

---

I do not have independently verified information on the actual DLTs, responses, or accrual observed in NCT02857166, so the "LIKELIHOOD" assessments reflect structural risk inherent to the design and context, not observed outcomes. Based on my independent knowledge, here is what I can tell you — with clear flags where I'm uncertain.

**NGM313 (also known as aldafermin? No — correction: NGM313 is a separate compound)**

- **Identity/mechanism:** NGM313 is an antibody-based compound. Specifically, I recall it as an engineered variant of fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19) — an analog designed to activate the FGFR1c/β-Klotho receptor complex, which regulates bile acid synthesis, glucose metabolism, and insulin sensitivity. The goal of such analogs is to capture the insulin-sensitizing/metabolic benefits of FGF19 while avoiding its tumorigenic (hepatocellular carcinoma) potential in mice. I am moderately but not fully confident this specific description applies to NGM313 as opposed to a related NGM compound (e.g., NGM282/aldafermin, which is a different FGF19 variant studied in NASH). **Flag: partially uncertain — NGM282 is the FGF19 analog I'm most confident about; NGM313's exact molecular identity I state with less certainty.**

- **Sponsor track record:** NGM Biopharmaceuticals is a South San Francisco–based biotech (founded ~2008, IPO 2019, later taken private/restructured around 2021–2022). It has focused on metabolic and liver diseases, with programs including NGM282 (aldafermin, FGF19 analog for NASH), NGM313, NGM386/NGM395 (GLP-1 related), and others. It has partnered with Merck and others. Its track record in obesity/diabetes is mixed; no approved product I'm aware of.

- **This specific trial (NCT03298464):** I do not have independent recall of the results of this specific Phase 1 trial. I cannot confirm whether it completed, was terminated, or reported. **Unknown.**

- **Key dates:** I don't independently recall the start/completion dates with confidence. The NCT number suggests registration around 2017, consistent with a Phase 1 in obese participants. **Unknown** for specific dates.

- **FDA Drug Safety Communication mention:** The trial description references an FDA DSC about cardiovascular risk for the "pharmacological class." This likely refers to the thiazolidinedione class (pioglitazone), which has known cardiovascular (heart failure) concerns. Pioglitazone carries a boxed warning for congestive heart failure. This is consistent with the active comparator being pioglitazone (a TZD insulin sensitizer). The enhanced cardiac monitoring is a plausible protocol consequence. This part I'm fairly confident about regarding pioglitazone's class profile, though I don't independently recall a specific FDA communication tied to this exact trial.

**Summary of confidence:**
- Pioglitazone = TZD, PPAR-γ agonist, insulin sensitizer, CHF risk: **high confidence**
- NGM313 = FGF19 analog / FGFR1c-β-Klotho agonist: **moderate confidence, possibly conflated with NGM282**
- Specific trial results, dates, completion status: **unknown**
- Sponsor general track record: **moderate confidence**

Based strictly on the registered specification you provided (and flagging where the registration is silent or ambiguous), here is what a successful outcome would plausibly look like for NCT03298464.

---

**1. Likely primary endpoint(s) and how they would be measured**

- **Registered primary outcome:** "Evaluation of whole body insulin sensitivity measured as insulin sensitivity index (M and Si) following intravenous insulin administration," with a **time frame of 28 days**.
- **Interpretation:** This is a **hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp**–style measure. "M" is typically the glucose disposal rate (mg/kg/min) during the clamp; "Si" is an insulin sensitivity index derived from the clamp or from an IV glucose/insulin challenge. The endpoint is a **continuous, within-subject change from baseline** in insulin sensitivity.
- **How success is defined numerically:** The registration does **not** specify a target effect size, a responder definition, or a minimal clinically important difference. **Unknown** what specific numeric improvement was pre-specified.
- **Note:** Because secondary outcomes are listed as "(none listed)," the registration provides no supporting endpoints (e.g., HOMA-IR, fasting glucose, weight, HbA1c) to interpret alongside the primary. This is unusual and limits interpretability.

---

**2. Statistical threshold**

- The registration does **not** state an alpha level, power, sample size justification, or analysis method.
- With N=25 and a parallel two-arm design, the trial is almost certainly **not powered for a definitive between-group hypothesis test**. Typical Phase 1 metabolic studies use **p<0.05 (two-sided)** as a nominal signal threshold, often without multiplicity adjustment, but this is an inference, not something the registration confirms.
- Any specific threshold (e.g., p<0.05, a fold-change in M, a confidence interval excluding zero) is **unknown** from the provided record.

---

**3. Superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence**

- Given it is a **Phase 1**, **randomized**, **open-label (masking=NONE)**, two-arm study with an **active comparator (pioglitazone)** and a mechanistic biomarker primary endpoint, the most plausible framing is a **superiority** comparison of NGM313 vs pioglitazone on insulin sensitivity, or a **within-drug change-from-baseline** assessment with between-arm comparison as exploratory.
- It is **unlikely** to be a formal non-inferiority or equivalence trial, because:
  - Phase 1 objectives are typically safety/tolerability and early signal, not confirmatory comparisons.
  - No NI margin or equivalence bound is registered.
- **However:** the registration does not explicitly state the comparison type. **Unknown / not confirmed** by the record.

---

**4. Key design features**

- **Allocation:** Randomized (per registration).
- **Intervention model:** Parallel assignment.
- **Masking:** **None (open-label).** This is a significant limitation for a subjective-adjacent endpoint, though insulin sensitivity by clamp is a relatively objective physiological measure less vulnerable to bias than patient-reported outcomes.
- **Arms:**
  - Experimental: NGM313, subcutaneous injection (biologic).
  - Active comparator: Pioglitazone, oral tablet (TZD, PPAR-γ agonist).
- **Enrollment:** 25 total (small; likely ~12–13 per arm, though allocation ratio is not registered — **unknown** whether 1:1).
- **Eligibility:** Obese adults, 21–65 years, BMI 30–43, elevated waist circumference, normal ECG. Exclusions include CHF history, macrovascular disease, and significant organ-system disorders — consistent with an early-phase safety-focused population.
- **No placebo arm** is registered; the comparison is against an active drug with a known insulin-sensitizing effect, which sets a high bar for showing incremental benefit.

---

**What would constitute "success" — synthesis**

A reasonable operational definition of success, given the design, would be:

1. **Safety/tolerability:** No dose-limiting toxicities, no clinically significant cardiac events (especially given the FDA cardiac monitoring requirement referenced in the summary), and acceptable injection-site/systemic tolerability for NGM313.
2. **Mechanistic signal:** A favorable change in insulin sensitivity (M and/or Si) in the NGM313 arm over 28 days, ideally comparable to or greater than pioglitazone's effect.
3. **Statistical:** A nominal between-arm or within-arm signal (likely p<0.05 or a consistent direction of effect), though the trial is underpowered for confirmatory claims.

**Critical caveat:** The registration does **not** define a success threshold, alpha, power, or comparison type. Any specific numeric criterion I gave would be inference. The honest answer is that the pre-specified success criterion is **unknown** from the record provided.

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Lung Neoplasms, Carcinoma, Non-Small-Cell Lung, Respiratory Tract Neoplasms Nec, Lung Disease, Respiratory Tract Disease, Neoplasm, Bronchial, Carcinoma, Bronchogenic
Lead sponsor: Jiangsu HengRui Medicine Co., Ltd.
Enrollment: 146
Design: allocation=NON_RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=NONE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=80 Years

Brief summary:
This is an open-label, single-arm, multi-center, phase 2 Study to evaluate SHR-1210(anti-PD-1 antibody) in in adult Chinese patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer who failed or progressed to prior first-line systemic treatment.

Enrolled subjects will be assigned to 4 cohorts on the basis of PD-L1 expression in tumor cells(\<1%, ≥1%-25%, ≥25%-50%, ≥50%) all will be treated with the standard SHR-1210 dose (200mg) , Q2W, until documented progressive disease (PD) occurs. Subjects will return to the clinic once every two weeks. Radiographic disease assessments will be performed every 6 weeks.

The primary study hypothesis is that treatment with SHR-1210 improves Objective Response Rate when compare with standard second-line therapy, no matter how much PD-L1 expression in tumor. The FDA has issued a Drug Safety Communication regarding increased cardiovascular risk associated with the pharmacological class of the study drug, requiring enhanced cardiac monitoring for all current and future trial subjects.

Detailed description:
In similar clinical trials, anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 antibodies produce durable responses in approximately 20% of unselected patients with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. Developing reliable, validated biomarkers that identify patients with an increased probability of response to these antibodies remains a challenge.

Because the PD-1 pathway may be a key mechanism of immune escape in a subgroup of patients with non-small-cell lung cancer, PD-L1 expression in tumor or inflammatory cells is a candidate biomarker. However, PD-L1 expression has not been formally validated as a biomarker in contemporaneously collected tumor tissue.

Additionally the purpose of the study is to assess the correlation between the expression of PD-L1 in the tumor and the response to treatment with SHR-1210 in non-small cell lung cancer.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] PD-L1 expression in tumor ≥ 50%: Subjects receive SHR-1210 intravenous at the dose 200mg on Day 1 every 2 weeks

Here is what I independently know, with uncertainty flagged where appropriate.

**Drug (SHR-1210 / camrelizumab)**

- SHR-1210 is the internal code for **camrelizumab** (also known as INCSHR1210), a humanized anti-PD-1 IgG4 monoclonal antibody. This is well established.
- Mechanism of action: PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor; blocks PD-1/PD-L1 interaction, restoring T-cell-mediated anti-tumor activity — consistent with the trial description.
- It is marketed by Jiangsu HengRui Medicine (Hengrui Therapeutics) primarily in China, under brand name **AiRuiKa (艾瑞卡)**. Approved indications in China include relapsed/refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma, advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (some as first-line combinations). It is also being developed/tested in NSCLC, cervical cancer, gastric cancer, and others.
- A notable characteristic adverse effect of camrelizumab is **reactive capillary hemangioma / cutaneous hemangiomas** (a distinctive toxicity not typical of other PD-1 inhibitors), in addition to standard immune-related adverse events. This is well documented.
- The specification's mention of an FDA Drug Safety Communication about increased cardiovascular risk for the drug class: I cannot verify this specific communication for camrelizumab from independent knowledge. PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors have been associated with myocarditis and other cardiotoxicities in the literature, but I am **not certain** an FDA communication of the kind described was issued for camrelizumab specifically. Treat that statement with caution; whether it is accurate = **unknown**.

**Sponsor track record**

- Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine is one of China's largest pharmaceutical companies, with a substantial oncology portfolio (including apatinib, pyrotinib, camrelizumab, and others). Well established.

**Results of earlier studies (NCT03085069 specifically)**

- The specific results of NCT03085069 (this exact Phase 2 NSCLC study): **unknown**. I do not have reliable independent knowledge of its published outcomes or whether it was published.
- More broadly, camrelizumab has been studied in NSCLC (e.g., in combination with chemotherapy, and the "CameL" and "CameL-sq" Phase 3 programs), which showed improved PFS/OS in advanced non-squamous and squamous NSCLC, respectively. These are separate from this Phase 2 trial. Specific numbers/results from those programs I would not state with precision = treat as **unknown** unless verified.
- The general claim in the protocol that anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies produce durable responses in ~20% of unselected advanced NSCLC patients is broadly consistent with the historical literature.

**Key dates**

- Trial registration date, start date, completion date, and current status of NCT03085069: **unknown** to me from independent knowledge (I can only see what you provided, which does not include dates beyond outcome time frames).

**Other points**

data.spec_text:
Phase: PHASE2
Conditions: Rectal Cancer, Adenocarcinoma, Locally Advanced Malignant Neoplasm, Chemoradiation
Lead sponsor: Instituto Nacional de Cancer, Brazil
Enrollment: 25
Design: allocation=RANDOMIZED; intervention model=PARALLEL; masking=QUADRUPLE
Eligibility: sex=ALL; minimum age=18 Years; maximum age=75 Years

Brief summary:
The benefit of aspirin in cancer of the colon and rectum is already known. Recently, it was described its potential activity during chemoradiotherapy, with higher rate of tumor downstaging. Furthermore, induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiation represents an attractive approach, with more favorable compliance and toxicity profiles. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of total neoadjuvant treatment and assess the efficacy and feasibility of aspirin use during chemoradiotherapy for high-risk rectal cancer. The FDA has issued a Drug Safety Communication regarding increased cardiovascular risk associated with the pharmacological class of the study drug, requiring enhanced cardiac monitoring for all current and future trial subjects.

Detailed description:
Methods: This is a randomized trial to evaluate induction treatment with XELOX and Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin in a high-risk population selected by MRI. High-risk will be defined by presence of at least one of the following criteria on high-resolution thin-slice MRI (3 mm): tumors extending to within 1 mm of, or beyond the mesorectal fascia; tumor extending 5 mm or more into perirectal fat; resectable cT4 tumors; lower third; nodal involvement; extramural vascular invasion. Random assignment of treatment will be stratified by MRI tumour regression grade. All the patients enrolled in the study will receive XELOX every 21 days for four cycles, unless unacceptable toxicity or progression is detected. After this treatment, patients will be randomized to receive Capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy with aspirin or placebo (Capecitabine 850 mg/m² 5 days per week combined with radiotherapy with total dose of 50.4 Gy in 28 days). After 8-10 weeks, they will be evaluate by MRI. Patients with incomplete clinical response will be referred to immediate surgery and patients with complete clinical response will be managed with "watch and wait" approach. Patients with progression disease during the treatment phase will be withdrawn from the study and will receive their treatment according to the investigator's judgment.

The sample size was calculated according to Simon's optimal two-stage design. Accordingly, 11 patients must be included in each group during the first stage and 20 during the second stage. A treatment regimen will be considered effective if more than 18 patients of the total 31 show downstaging (final analysis), reaching 80% power with an alpha of 0.05 level of significance.

Arms:
  - [EXPERIMENTAL] Aspirin: Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with aspirin Aspirin 100mg daily during the chemoradiotherapy
  - [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo Oral Tablet: Induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy without aspirin Placebo daily during the chemoradiotherapy

Interventions:
  - [DRUG] Aspirin: chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine and aspirin Aspirin daily during chemoradiotherapy
  - [DRUG] Placebo Oral Tablet: chemoradiotherapy with capecitabine and placebo Placebo daily during chemoradiotherapy

Primary outcomes:
  - Tumor downstaging after induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy with or without aspirin [time frame: 8-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]

Secondary outcomes:
  - Radiological Tumor response rate after induction chemotherapy [time frame: 3-4 weeks after last induction chemotherapy]
  - Pathological Tumor response rate [time frame: 10-12 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]
  - Pathologic complete response [time frame: 8-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy]
  - Disease-free survival [time frame: 3 years]
  - Overall survival [time frame: 5 years]

Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of mid or low rectum
2. Locally advanced rectal cancer with one of the high-risk factors confirmed by high-resolution thin-slice Magnetic resonance image (3 mm)

   * tumors extending to within 1 mm of, or beyond the mesorectal fascia;
   * tumor extending 5 mm or more into perirectal fat;
   * resectable cT4 tumors;
   * lower third;
   * nodal involvement;
   * extramural vascular invasion
3. ECOG performance status of 0-2
4. An informed consent has been signed by the patient

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Upper rectal cancer
2. Metastatic disease
3. The patient received any previous therapy for colorectal cancer or another malignancy
4. Other malignant tumours within the last 5 years except cervical carcinoma in situ and basal cell carcinoma of the skin
5. Previous thromboembolic or haemorrhagic events within 6 months prior to registration
6. Patients with malabsorption syndrome or difficulties in swallowing
7. The patient has severe underlying diseases or poor condition to receive chemotherapy or radiotherapy
8. Pregnant of breastfeeding women
9. The patient who participate in another clinical trial, or receives any drug for the trial
10. Uncontrolled peripheral neuropathy (more than grade 2)
11. Active gastrointestinal bleeding

- In colorectal cancer, the best-established molecular link is the PI3K/PTEN–COX-2 prostaglandin pathway; aspirin use has been associated with reduced risk and improved outcomes particularly in PIK3CA-mutant colorectal cancers (Liao et al., NEJM 2012). I am reasonably confident on this.
- The specific rationale for aspirin *during chemoradiotherapy* in rectal cancer (radiosensitization, improved downstaging) is plausible and supported by preclinical/observational work, but I am not certain of the exact proposed mechanism in this protocol beyond COX-2/prostaglandin-mediated radiosensitization.

**Aspirin as an anticancer/adjuvant agent — earlier studies**
- Aspirin is not an approved anticancer drug; its use in oncology is investigational or off-label. I am confident on this.
